english: At every family event, my uncle always asks when I'm getting married.

target: Mereka menyewa gedung besar karena tamunya hampir seribu orang.
english: They rented a big hall because they have almost a thousand guests.

target: Saya jadi panitia di nikahan teman baik saya.
english: I'm on the committee at my best friend's wedding.

target: Setiap tamu dapat suvenir kipas kecil dari pengantin.
english: Every guest got a small fan as a souvenir from the couple.

target: Fotonya bagus sekali, siapa fotografer di nikahan kemarin?
english: The photos are really good — who was the photographer at yesterday's wedding?

target: Orang tuanya menangis bahagia waktu akad nikah selesai.
english: Her parents cried tears of joy when the vow ceremony ended.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka tinggal sementara di rumah mertua.
english: After getting married, they are living at the in-laws' house for a while.
grammar: Mertua = your spouse's parents; menantu = your child's spouse. Rumah mertua = the in-laws' house.

target: Hari ini ulang tahun ibu saya yang keenam puluh.
english: Today is my mother's sixtieth birthday.
grammar: yang ke- + number = ordinal: ulang tahun yang keenam puluh = sixtieth birthday.

target: Selamat ulang tahun, semoga panjang umur dan sehat selalu!
english: Happy birthday — may you have a long life and always be healthy!
grammar: Selamat + noun makes a wish: selamat ulang tahun, selamat jalan, selamat makan.

target: Anak-anak menyanyikan lagu ulang tahun sebelum meniup lilin.
english: The children sang the birthday song before blowing out the candles.

target: Ayo tiup lilinnya, jangan lupa ucapkan harapanmu dulu!
english: Come on, blow out the candles — don't forget to make your wish first!
grammar: harapan = a hope/wish, from harap: ucapkan harapanmu = say your wish.

target: Kami memesan kue coklat besar untuk ulang tahun ayah.
english: We ordered a big chocolate cake for dad's birthday.

target: Dia meniup semua lilin dalam satu kali tiupan.
english: He blew out all the candles in one breath.

target: Ulang tahun pertama anak biasanya dirayakan besar-besaran.
english: A child's first birthday is usually celebrated in a big way.

target: Jangan bilang ke ibu, pesta ini kejutan untuk dia.
english: Don't tell mom — this party is a surprise for her.

target: Kami menghias ruang tamu dengan balon warna-warni.
english: We decorated the living room with colorful balloons.

target: Teman-teman kantor memberi saya kue kecil di meja kerja.
english: My office friends gave me a little cake at my desk.

target: Umur kamu berapa sekarang? Jangan malu, hari ini spesial.
english: How old are you now? Don't be shy — today is special.

target: Nenek selalu memberi cucunya uang setiap ulang tahun.
english: Grandma always gives her grandchildren money on every birthday.

target: Tahun ini saya tidak mau pesta, cukup makan bersama keluarga.
english: This year I don't want a party; a meal with the family is enough.

target: Kado apa yang cocok untuk anak umur lima tahun?
english: What present is right for a five-year-old child?
grammar: Kado = a wrapped present (from Dutch cadeau); hadiah is the wider word for gift or prize.

target: Kami merayakan ulang tahun anak kembar mereka di taman kota.
english: We celebrated their twins' birthday at the city park.

target: Dia mentraktir kami makan bakso karena baru ulang tahun.
english: He treated us to meatball soup because he just had a birthday.
grammar: Indonesian birthdays flip the treat: the birthday person mentraktir (treats) the friends.

target: Lilin angka tujuh itu hampir jatuh dari kuenya.
english: That number-seven candle almost fell off the cake.

target: Kirim ucapan ulang tahun ke kakak lewat pesan singkat saja.
english: Just send birthday wishes to your older sibling by text message.

target: Pesta ulang tahunnya dipindah ke dalam rumah karena hujan deras.
english: The birthday party was moved indoors because of heavy rain.

target: Terima kasih sudah datang dan membawa hadiah untuk anak kami.
english: Thank you for coming and bringing a present for our child.

target: Besok kami mampir ke rumah bibi sebelum pulang ke kota.
english: Tomorrow we'll drop by auntie's house before going back to the city.
grammar: Mampir = drop by briefly on the way somewhere: mampir ke rumah bibi = stop by auntie's.

target: Kalau lewat Bandung, mampirlah ke rumah kami.
english: If you pass through Bandung, do stop by our house.

target: Kami menginap tiga malam di rumah kakek waktu Lebaran.
english: We stayed three nights at grandpa's house during Lebaran.
grammar: Lebaran = the Eid homecoming holiday, when the whole country travels to family.

target: Anak-anak paling senang menginap di rumah nenek mereka.
english: The kids like staying over at their grandma's house best.

target: Setiap mudik, jalan ke kampung selalu macet parah.
english: Every homecoming trip, the road to the village is always badly jammed.
grammar: Mudik = the big trip home to your family town before Lebaran — half the country moves at once.

target: Kami membawa tikar dan makan siang di halaman rumah paman.
english: We brought a mat and had lunch in the yard of uncle's house.

target: Sudah lama kami tidak berkunjung ke rumah saudara di desa.
english: We haven't visited our relatives' house in the village for a long time.

target: Nenek pasti memasak banyak kalau cucu-cucunya datang.
english: Grandma is sure to cook a lot when her grandchildren come.

target: Kami mengobrol sampai tengah malam di teras rumah.
english: We chatted until midnight on the terrace of the house.
grammar: Mengobrol = to chat; in speech you will hear it shortened to ngobrol everywhere.

target: Sebelum pulang, kami pamit dulu ke kakek dan nenek.
english: Before going home, we first said goodbye to grandpa and grandma.

target: Rumah sepupu saya jauh, jadi kami berangkat pagi sekali.
english: My cousin's house is far away, so we left very early in the morning.

target: Keponakan saya sekarang sudah bisa jalan dan mulai bicara.
english: My nephew can already walk now and is starting to talk.

target: Tante membuatkan kami teh manis hangat sore itu.
english: Auntie made us warm sweet tea that afternoon.
grammar: -kan can mean 'for someone': membuatkan kami teh = made tea for us.

target: Kamar tamu sudah disiapkan untuk kalian berdua.
english: The guest room has been prepared for the two of you.

target: Kami tidur di rumah saudara karena hotel di kota penuh.
english: We slept at a relative's house because the hotels in town were full.

target: Jangan lupa cium tangan kakek waktu datang dan pamit.
english: Don't forget to kiss grandpa's hand when you arrive and when you say goodbye.
grammar: Cium tangan — a child presses the elder's hand to the face — is the greeting for grandparents.

target: Kakek senang sekali melihat cucunya datang dari jauh.
english: Grandpa was really happy to see his grandchildren come from far away.

target: Kami membawakan nenek kain batik dari Solo.
english: We brought grandma batik cloth from Solo.

target: Setiap kali berkunjung, kami selalu pulang membawa banyak makanan.
english: Every time we visit, we always go home carrying lots of food.

target: Bulan depan giliran kami yang berkunjung ke rumah sepupu.
english: Next month it's our turn to visit our cousin's house.

target: Selamat atas kelahiran anak pertama kalian!
english: Congratulations on the birth of your first child!
grammar: Selamat atas + noun congratulates: selamat atas kelahiran = congrats on the birth.

target: Wah, selamat ya! Bayinya lahir di rumah sakit mana?
english: Wow, congratulations! Which hospital was the baby born at?

target: Semoga kalian berdua bahagia terus sampai kakek-nenek.
english: May you both stay happy all the way to being grandpa and grandma.

target: Turut senang mendengar kabar baik tentang pekerjaan kamu.
english: I'm glad to hear the good news about your job.

target: Semoga cita-cita kamu tercapai tahun ini.
english: May your dreams be achieved this year.

target: Selamat atas kelulusan kamu, kami bangga sekali!
english: Congratulations on your graduation — we're so proud!

target: Akhirnya kakak saya lulus dan langsung dapat kerja.
english: My older sibling finally graduated and got a job right away.

target: Semoga usaha baru kamu berjalan lancar, ya.
english: I hope your new business goes smoothly, okay?
grammar: Semoga + clause = hopefully/may: semoga lancar = hope it goes smoothly.

target: Selamat hari raya, mohon maaf lahir dan batin.
english: Happy Eid — please forgive my wrongs, outward and inward.
grammar: The Eid greeting: mohon maaf lahir dan batin = forgive my wrongs, outward and inward.

target: Selamat menikmati masa pensiun, Pak Hasan!
english: Enjoy your retirement, Mr. Hasan!
grammar: Selamat + verb blesses an activity: selamat menikmati = enjoy, selamat belajar = happy studying.

target: Bibi mendoakan pengantin baru cepat dapat anak.
english: Auntie prayed for the newlyweds to have a child soon.

target: Selamat jalan, hati-hati, kabari kami kalau sudah sampai.
english: Safe travels, take care — let us know when you've arrived.
grammar: Kabari (from kabar, news) = let me know: kabari kalau sudah sampai = tell us when you arrive.

target: Semoga tahun depan kita bisa berkumpul lengkap lagi.
english: Hopefully next year we can gather again with everyone there.

target: Kami ikut bangga, anak kamu diterima di universitas negeri.
english: We're proud too — your child was accepted at a state university.

target: Semoga lekas sembuh, jangan lupa banyak istirahat.
english: Get well soon — don't forget to get plenty of rest.

target: Turut berduka cita, ya. Semoga keluarga diberi ketabahan.
english: My deepest condolences. May the family be given strength.
grammar: Turut berduka cita = the set condolence, 'I share the grief'; the reply is a quiet terima kasih.

target: Jangan lupa bawa oleh-oleh kalau pulang dari Bali.
english: Don't forget to bring souvenirs when you come home from Bali.
grammar: Oleh-oleh = treats you bring people after a trip — coming home empty-handed is not done.

target: Kami membawa dua kotak kue untuk tuan rumah.
english: We brought two boxes of cakes for the host.
grammar: Tuan rumah = the host, literally 'master of the house': kue untuk tuan rumah = cakes for the host.

target: Ibu membungkus makanan untuk tamu yang pulang duluan.
english: Mom wrapped up food for the guests who went home early.

target: Apa yang harus kami bawa ke acara nanti malam?
english: What should we bring to the event tonight?

target: Bawa saja buah atau kue, jangan yang mahal-mahal.
english: Just bring fruit or cakes — nothing expensive.

target: Oleh-oleh khas Yogyakarta itu habis dalam sehari di kantor.
english: Those Yogyakarta specialty treats were gone within a day at the office.

target: Dia datang membawa martabak manis kesukaan anak-anak.
english: He arrived carrying sweet martabak, the kids' favorite.
grammar: Martabak manis = a thick sweet stuffed pancake, the classic treat to bring home at night.

target: Titip oleh-oleh dodol, ya, kalau kamu ke Garut.
english: Get me some dodol, okay, if you go to Garut.
grammar: Titip = ask a traveler to get you something: titip dodol = bring me back some dodol.

target: Kado untuk pengantin sudah saya bungkus rapi tadi malam.
english: I already wrapped the present for the couple neatly last night.
grammar: Object + sudah saya + bare verb = natural passive: sudah saya bungkus = I have wrapped it.

target: Selain kue, kami juga membawakan keponakan mainan.
english: Besides cakes, we also brought our nephews and nieces toys.
grammar: membawakan puts the person right after the verb: membawakan keponakan mainan = brought the nieces and nephews toys.

target: Nenek paling senang diberi kerudung baru warna hijau.
english: Grandma is happiest when given a new green headscarf.

target: Satu kardus mangga ini dari kebun paman di kampung.
english: This box of mangoes is from uncle's orchard in the village.

target: Jangan buka kadonya sekarang, tunggu sampai tamu pulang.
english: Don't open the present now — wait until the guests go home.

target: Oleh-oleh dari kami cepat habis karena banyak yang minta.
english: Our souvenirs ran out fast because lots of people asked for some.

target: Siapa yang membawa nasi dan siapa yang membawa lauk?
english: Who is bringing the rice and who is bringing the side dishes?
grammar: Lauk = the dishes eaten with rice; nasi dan lauk is the shape of every Indonesian meal.

target: Acara kumpul keluarga tahun ini di rumah kami, ya.
english: This year's family gathering is at our house, okay?

target: Kita perlu menyiapkan kursi tambahan untuk para sepupu.
english: We need to prepare extra chairs for all the cousins.
grammar: Para + person noun = plural group: para tamu = the guests, para sepupu = the cousins.

target: Ibu-ibu memasak di dapur, bapak-bapak memasang tenda di halaman.
english: The women cook in the kitchen; the men put up a tent in the yard.

target: Para keponakan bermain kejar-kejaran di halaman belakang.
english: The nephews and nieces play tag in the backyard.

target: Setelah makan, kami berfoto bersama di depan rumah nenek.
english: After eating, we took a photo together in front of grandma's house.

target: Tahun ini keluarga dari Sumatera juga ikut datang.
english: This year the family from Sumatra is coming along too.

target: Kami membuat jadwal kunjungan supaya adil untuk semua rumah.
english: We made a visiting schedule so it's fair for every household.

target: Grup keluarga di ponsel ramai sekali sebelum hari raya.
english: The family group chat on the phone is really busy before the holiday.
grammar: Grup keluarga = the extended-family chat group — every family has one, and it is never quiet.

target: Siapa yang menjemput kakek dari stasiun sore nanti?
english: Who is picking grandpa up from the station later this afternoon?

target: Acara sudah selesai, tapi para tamu masih mengobrol di teras.
english: The event is already over, but the guests are still chatting on the terrace.

target: Sisa makanan dibagi rata untuk dibawa pulang.
english: The leftover food was divided evenly to take home.

target: Sebelum pulang, kami memilih tuan rumah untuk tahun depan.
english: Before going home, we chose the host for next year.

target: Nenek berpesan supaya kami datang lagi liburan sekolah nanti.
english: Grandma told us to come again during the school holidays.

target: Rumah terasa sepi setelah semua saudara pulang ke kota masing-masing.
english: The house feels quiet after all the relatives went home to their own cities.
grammar: Masing-masing = each/their own: kota masing-masing = their own cities.

target: Setelah tiga bulan les, saya akhirnya bisa berenang sampai ujung kolam.
english: After three months of lessons, I can finally swim to the end of the pool.
grammar: Bisa = ability: bisa berenang = can swim. For permission Indonesian uses boleh, not bisa.

target: Adik saya belum bisa naik sepeda tanpa roda kecil di belakang.
english: My little brother can't ride a bike yet without the small wheels at the back.

target: Nenek masih bisa membaca koran pagi tanpa kacamata.
english: Grandma can still read the morning paper without glasses.

target: Kamu bisa mengangkat galon air itu sendirian?
english: Can you lift that water jug by yourself?

target: Dia bisa berbicara tiga bahasa karena keluarganya sering pindah negara.
english: He can speak three languages because his family often moved countries.

target: Saya tidak bisa membuka toples selai ini, tolong bukakan.
english: I can't open this jam jar; please open it for me.

target: Kalau jalan tol kosong, kita bisa sampai bandara dalam empat puluh menit.
english: If the toll road is empty, we can reach the airport in forty minutes.
grammar: Bisa also = possible: kita bisa sampai = we can (it is possible to) get there.

target: Motor tua ini masih bisa dipakai untuk keliling kampung.
english: This old motorbike can still be used for going around the neighborhood.

target: Setelah operasi lutut, kakek belum bisa berjalan jauh.
english: After his knee operation, Grandpa can't walk far yet.

target: Saya sudah bisa menyetir, tapi belum boleh membawa mobil sendirian.
english: I can already drive, but I'm not allowed to take the car out alone.
grammar: Bisa = able (skill), boleh = allowed (permission): bisa menyetir tapi belum boleh.

target: Anak itu sudah bisa berenang, tapi belum boleh masuk kolam yang dalam.
english: That child can swim already, but isn't allowed into the deep pool yet.

target: Kartu ini bisa dipakai di bus, tapi tidak bisa dipakai di kereta bandara.
english: This card can be used on the bus, but can't be used on the airport train.

target: Boleh saya pinjam tangga kamu untuk mengganti lampu teras?
english: May I borrow your ladder to change the porch light?
grammar: Boleh saya...? = May I...? — the everyday way to ask permission: Boleh saya pinjam...?

target: Boleh saya pinjam gunting sebentar? Punya saya hilang entah ke mana.
english: May I borrow your scissors for a moment? Mine disappeared who knows where.

target: Bukunya boleh dipinjam dua minggu dan bisa diperpanjang satu kali.
english: The book may be borrowed for two weeks and can be extended once.
grammar: Rules pair them: boleh dipinjam = allowed to be borrowed, bisa diperpanjang = possible to extend.

target: Pak, boleh saya memakai ruang rapat kecil untuk menelepon klien?
english: Sir, may I use the small meeting room to call a client?

target: Bu, boleh saya minta izin datang siang besok karena ada urusan keluarga?
english: Ma'am, may I have permission to come in late tomorrow because of a family matter?
grammar: Minta izin = ask permission: minta izin datang siang = ask to come in late.

target: Boleh anak-anak berenang di kolam dangkal tanpa pelampung?
english: May the children swim in the shallow pool without floaties?

target: Maaf, pengunjung tidak boleh membawa makanan dari luar ke area kolam.
english: Sorry, visitors may not bring outside food into the pool area.

target: Kamu boleh memakai mobil ayah, asal pulang sebelum jam sepuluh malam.
english: You may use Dad's car, as long as you come home before ten at night.
grammar: Asal = as long as: boleh, asal pulang sebelum malam = allowed, provided you're home early.

target: Boleh saya menyalakan kipas angin? Ruangan ini panas sekali.
english: May I turn on the fan? This room is really hot.

target: Tamu hotel boleh memakai kolam renang sampai jam sembilan malam.
english: Hotel guests may use the swimming pool until nine at night.

target: Maaf Pak, di sini tidak boleh merokok, area merokok ada di lantai satu.
english: Sorry sir, smoking isn't allowed here; the smoking area is on the first floor.
grammar: Tidak boleh = not allowed (spoken): tidak boleh merokok. Signs say dilarang merokok.

target: Karyawan tidak boleh menerima hadiah mahal dari klien perusahaan.
english: Employees may not accept expensive gifts from company clients.

target: Di perpustakaan kampus, pengunjung tidak boleh berbicara keras-keras.
english: In the campus library, visitors may not talk loudly.

target: Boleh saya membawa anjing kecil saya masuk ke kafe ini?
english: May I bring my small dog into this cafe?

target: Anak-anak boleh bermain di halaman sampai lampu jalan menyala.
english: The children may play in the yard until the streetlights come on.

target: Boleh saya menitip tas di sini selama saya berenang?
english: May I leave my bag here while I swim?

target: Boleh saya mengganti jadwal les piano anak saya minggu ini?
english: May I change my child's piano lesson schedule this week?

target: Kata dokter, ayah sudah boleh pulang dari rumah sakit besok pagi.
english: The doctor says Dad is allowed to go home from the hospital tomorrow morning.
grammar: Sudah boleh = allowed now (was not before): sudah boleh pulang = can finally go home.

target: Setelah dua minggu, jahitannya sudah kering dan saya boleh berenang lagi.
english: After two weeks, the stitches were dry and I was allowed to swim again.

target: Boleh saya duduk di sini, atau kursi ini sudah ada yang punya?
english: May I sit here, or is this seat taken?

target: Semua tamu harus menulis nama di buku tamu sebelum masuk gedung.
english: All guests must write their name in the guest book before entering the building.

target: Saya harus menjemput anak saya sebelum kelas renangnya selesai jam lima.
english: I have to pick up my child before her swimming class ends at five.

target: Di rumah kami, sepatu harus dilepas sebelum naik ke lantai kayu.
english: In our house, shoes must be taken off before stepping onto the wooden floor.
grammar: House rules use harus + di-: sepatu harus dilepas = shoes must be taken off.

target: Kamu harus mengembalikan raket ini ke loket sebelum gedung olahraga tutup.
english: You have to return this racket to the counter before the sports hall closes.

target: Sebelum wawancara kerja, kamu harus menyiapkan cerita tentang pengalamanmu.
english: Before a job interview, you have to prepare stories about your experience.

target: Obat batuk ini harus dihabiskan walaupun kamu sudah merasa sehat.
english: This cough medicine must be finished even if you already feel healthy.

target: Kami harus mengganti ban belakang sebelum berangkat ke luar kota.
english: We have to change the rear tire before leaving town.

target: Kamu tidak harus ikut arisan, tapi ibu pasti senang kalau kamu datang.
english: You don't have to join the arisan, but Mom will definitely be happy if you come.
grammar: Tidak harus = don't have to (optional) — NOT forbidden. 'Must not' is tidak boleh.

target: Laporan bulanan harus dikirim ke pusat paling lambat tanggal lima.
english: The monthly report must be sent to head office by the fifth at the latest.
grammar: Paling lambat = at the latest: paling lambat tanggal lima = by the fifth at the latest.

target: Sebelum kelas yoga dimulai, semua peserta harus mengisi formulir kesehatan.
english: Before the yoga class starts, all participants must fill in a health form.

target: Pengemudi harus membawa SIM dan STNK setiap kali berkendara.
english: Drivers must carry their license and vehicle papers whenever they drive.

target: Saya harus menabung enam bulan lagi supaya uang mukanya cukup.
english: I have to save for six more months so the down payment is enough.

target: Kalau mau ikut lomba renang antarkantor, kamu harus mendaftar minggu ini.
english: If you want to join the inter-office swimming competition, you have to register this week.

target: Anak kucing itu harus diberi susu tiga jam sekali.
english: That kitten has to be given milk every three hours.

target: Kenapa formulir ini harus dicetak, tidak bisa dikirim lewat email saja?
english: Why does this form have to be printed — can't it just be sent by email?
grammar: Harus = must, bisa = can: harus dicetak, tidak bisa lewat email = must be printed, can't go by email.

target: Sebelum pindah, kami harus memberi tahu pemilik kos satu bulan sebelumnya.
english: Before moving out, we have to inform the boarding-house owner one month in advance.

target: Sebaiknya kamu berangkat sebelum jam tujuh supaya tidak kena macet.
english: You'd better leave before seven so you don't get stuck in traffic.
grammar: Sebaiknya = you'd better / it's best to — advice, much softer than harus.

target: Kalau demamnya belum turun besok, sebaiknya kamu periksa ke dokter.
english: If the fever hasn't gone down by tomorrow, you'd better see a doctor.

target: Sebaiknya kita membawa jas hujan, langit di barat mulai gelap.
english: We'd better bring raincoats; the sky in the west is getting dark.

target: Waktu bepergian, sebaiknya uang tunai disimpan di dua tempat berbeda.
english: When traveling, it's best to keep cash in two different places.

target: Sebaiknya jangan menaruh dompet di saku belakang waktu naik bus kota.
english: Better not to put your wallet in your back pocket when riding the city bus.
grammar: Sebaiknya jangan = better not to — a gentle warning, friendlier than a flat jangan.

target: Menurut pelatih, sebaiknya kami pemanasan sepuluh menit sebelum angkat beban.
english: According to the coach, we should warm up for ten minutes before lifting weights.

target: Sebaiknya daging ini dimasak hari ini juga supaya tidak bau.
english: This meat had better be cooked today so it doesn't smell.

target: Kamu sebaiknya minta maaf dulu, urusan siapa yang salah bisa nanti.
english: You'd better apologize first; whose fault it is can wait.
grammar: Sebaiknya can follow the subject: kamu sebaiknya minta maaf = you'd better apologize.

target: Sebaiknya kita pesan taksi dari sekarang, malam ini banyak acara di kota.
english: We'd better book a taxi now; there are lots of events in town tonight.

target: Untuk pemula, sebaiknya mulai dari beban yang paling ringan dulu.
english: For beginners, it's best to start with the lightest weights first.

target: Kamu mesti coba sate ayam di warung dekat stasiun itu.
english: You've got to try the chicken satay at the stall near the station.
grammar: Mesti = harus in relaxed speech — you'll hear it everywhere. In writing and formal talk, use harus.

target: Kalau ke Yogyakarta, kamu mesti mampir ke pasar malamnya.
english: If you go to Yogyakarta, you've got to stop by its night market.

target: Saya mesti pulang sekarang, besok ujian saya mulai pagi-pagi.
english: I've got to go home now; my exam starts early tomorrow.

target: Kita mesti berangkat lebih pagi kalau tidak mau antre lama di loket.
english: We've got to leave earlier if we don't want to queue long at the ticket window.

target: Lemari seberat itu mesti diangkat dua orang, jangan coba angkat sendirian.
english: A wardrobe that heavy has to be lifted by two people — don't try lifting it alone.

target: Mesti sabar ya, hasil tes darahnya baru keluar hari Kamis.
english: You've just got to be patient; the blood test results only come out on Thursday.

target: Ban depannya sudah tipis, mesti diganti sebelum musim hujan.
english: The front tire is already worn thin; it's got to be replaced before the rainy season.

target: Kamu mesti tanya harga dulu sebelum naik ojek di tempat wisata.
english: You've got to ask the price first before taking a motorbike taxi at tourist spots.

target: Mesti ada orang dewasa di rumah kalau tukang gas datang.
english: There has to be an adult at home when the gas man comes.

target: Di undangan tertulis jam tujuh, berarti kita mesti keluar rumah jam enam.
english: The invitation says seven, which means we've got to leave the house at six.
grammar: Berarti = that means: berarti kita mesti keluar jam enam = so we've got to leave at six.

target: Sebelum naik pesawat, kami masih sempat membeli oleh-oleh di bandara.
english: Before boarding the plane, we still managed to buy souvenirs at the airport.
grammar: Sempat = managed to / had time to: masih sempat membeli = still managed to buy.

target: Tadi pagi saya tidak sempat sarapan karena bangun kesiangan.
english: This morning I didn't have time for breakfast because I woke up too late.
grammar: Tidak sempat = didn't get the chance: tidak sempat sarapan = no time for breakfast.

target: Untung kami sempat berteduh di halte sebelum hujannya tambah deras.
english: Luckily we managed to take shelter at the bus stop before the rain got heavier.

target: Dia sempat bekerja dua tahun di Makassar sebelum pindah ke Jakarta.
english: He worked for two years in Makassar at one point before moving to Jakarta.
grammar: Sempat + job/place = once did for a while: sempat bekerja di Makassar = worked there at one point.

target: Kamu sempat bertemu Bu Sari kemarin sebelum beliau pindah ke cabang baru?
english: Did you get a chance to meet Mrs. Sari yesterday before she moved to the new branch?

target: Maaf, saya belum sempat membalas pesanmu, minggu ini penuh sekali.
english: Sorry, I haven't had a chance to reply to your message; this week is completely full.

target: Kemarin sore kami sempat mampir sebentar ke rumah nenek.
english: Yesterday afternoon we managed to stop by Grandma's house for a bit.

target: Sebelum listriknya mati, saya sempat menyimpan semua pekerjaan di laptop.
english: Before the power went out, I managed to save all my work on the laptop.

target: Dia tidak sempat makan siang karena rapatnya mundur ke jam satu.
english: He didn't get a chance to eat lunch because the meeting was pushed back to one.

target: Kami hanya sempat melihat candi utama karena sorenya hujan deras.
english: We only had time to see the main temple because it rained hard in the afternoon.

target: Saya sempat bingung di stasiun karena nama jalurnya mirip semua.
english: I was confused for a moment at the station because the platform names all look alike.
grammar: Sempat + feeling = briefly felt: sempat bingung = was confused for a moment.

target: Untung kamu datang, saya sempat berpikir acaranya batal.
english: Good thing you came — for a moment I thought the event was canceled.

target: Saya tidak sanggup menghabiskan porsi nasi padang sebesar ini.
english: I can't manage to finish a Padang rice portion this big.
grammar: Sanggup = can manage/handle it — heavier than bisa: tidak sanggup menghabiskan = can't finish it.

target: Kamu sanggup menyelesaikan revisi laporan ini sebelum Jumat sore?
english: Can you manage to finish the report revisions before Friday afternoon?

target: Setelah latihan setahun, dia sanggup berlari sepuluh kilometer tanpa berhenti.
english: After a year of training, he can run ten kilometers without stopping.

target: Kami tidak sanggup membayar sewa apartemen di tengah kota lagi.
english: We can't afford the rent on an apartment downtown anymore.
grammar: Tidak sanggup + a cost = can't afford: tidak sanggup membayar sewa = can't afford the rent.

target: Kalau tidak sanggup lembur malam ini, bilang ke Pak Anton sekarang.
english: If you can't manage overtime tonight, tell Mr. Anton now.

target: Dia sanggup menunggu dua jam demi tiket konser band favoritnya.
english: He was willing to wait two hours for tickets to his favorite band's concert.
grammar: Demi = for the sake of: demi tiket konser = for the sake of concert tickets.

target: Ibu tidak sanggup menonton film sedih, pasti langsung menangis.
english: Mom can't handle sad movies; she always cries right away.

target: Satu ember penuh begini, kamu sanggup membawanya naik ke lantai tiga?
english: A bucket this full — can you manage to carry it up to the third floor?
grammar: -nya can be 'it' after a verb: membawanya = carry it.

target: Mereka sanggup membuka warung lagi enam bulan setelah kebakaran itu.
english: They managed to open their food stall again six months after the fire.

target: Setelah cedera bahu, berapa kilo yang sanggup kamu angkat sekarang?
english: After your shoulder injury, how many kilos can you manage to lift now?

target: Tidak usah membawa apa-apa besok, cukup datang saja lebih awal.
english: No need to bring anything tomorrow; just come a bit early.
grammar: Tidak usah = no need to (relaxed). Jangan = don't! (warning) — tidak usah bayar is not jangan bayar.

target: Kamu tidak usah menjemput saya, dari stasiun saya naik ojek saja.
english: You don't need to pick me up; I'll just take a motorbike taxi from the station.

target: Tidak usah repot-repot masak, kami benar-benar hanya mampir sebentar.
english: Please don't go to the trouble of cooking; we're really only stopping by for a moment.
grammar: Tidak usah repot-repot = don't go to any trouble — the polite guest's phrase.

target: Piringnya tidak usah dicuci sekarang, biar saya yang beres-beres nanti.
english: No need to wash the dishes now; let me tidy up later.
grammar: Biar saya yang... = let me be the one to: biar saya yang beres-beres = let me tidy up.

target: Kalau lukanya sekecil itu, tidak usah ke rumah sakit.
english: If the wound is that small, there's no need to go to the hospital.

target: Tidak usah malu bertanya, pelatih di sini semuanya ramah.
english: No need to be shy about asking; the trainers here are all friendly.

target: Bilang ke ibu tidak usah masak malam ini, kita makan di luar.
english: Tell Mom she doesn't need to cook tonight; we're eating out.

target: Tiketnya sudah saya beli lewat aplikasi, kamu tidak usah antre.
english: I already bought the tickets through the app; you don't need to queue.

target: Tidak usah menunggu saya untuk makan malam, rapatnya selesai larut malam.
english: No need to wait for me for dinner; the meeting ends late at night.

target: Kata teknisinya, mesin cucinya tidak usah diganti, cukup diperbaiki saja.
english: The technician says the washing machine doesn't need replacing; it just needs repairing.
grammar: Tidak usah works in passives too: tidak usah diganti = doesn't need to be replaced.

target: Tidak usah dibungkus, saya makan di sini saja.
english: No need to wrap it up; I'll just eat here.

target: Untuk kelas percobaan, tidak usah bayar, cukup isi formulir pendaftaran.
english: For the trial class, no need to pay; just fill in the registration form.

target: Silakan menaruh sepatu di rak dekat pintu sebelum masuk.
english: Please put your shoes on the rack by the door before coming in.
grammar: Silakan = please, go ahead. In Java you'll often hear monggo — same warm invitation.

target: Silakan mengambil teh hangat di meja sambil menunggu giliran Anda.
english: Please help yourself to warm tea at the table while waiting for your turn.

target: Kalau mau tambah nasi, silakan ambil sendiri di dapur.
english: If you want more rice, please help yourself in the kitchen.

target: Silakan duduk dulu, dokter giginya masih memeriksa pasien lain.
english: Please have a seat; the dentist is still examining another patient.

target: Silakan memakai loker mana saja yang masih kosong.
english: Please use any locker that's still empty.
grammar: Mana saja = any/whichever: loker mana saja = any locker at all.

target: Silakan hubungi resepsionis kalau AC kamarnya kurang dingin.
english: Please contact reception if the room's air conditioning isn't cold enough.

target: Silakan masuk lewat pintu samping, pintu depannya sedang dicat ulang.
english: Please come in through the side door; the front door is being repainted.

target: Silakan dicicipi dulu sambalnya, jangan takut, tidak terlalu pedas.
english: Please have a taste of the sambal first; don't be afraid, it's not too spicy.
grammar: Silakan di- + verb = extra polite invitation: silakan dicicipi = please do have a taste.

target: Pengunjung kolam wajib mandi di pancuran sebelum masuk ke air.
english: Pool visitors are required to shower before entering the water.
grammar: Wajib = required — the word of rules and signs. In conversation people say harus.

target: Anggota baru wajib mengikuti kelas pengenalan alat sebelum latihan sendiri.
english: New members are required to take an equipment orientation class before training alone.

target: Semua tamu gedung wajib menukar kartu identitas dengan kartu pengunjung.
english: All building guests are required to exchange their ID card for a visitor card.

target: Penumpang wajib memakai sabuk pengaman selama pesawat lepas landas dan mendarat.
english: Passengers are required to wear seatbelts while the plane takes off and lands.
grammar: Announcements use formal wajib: penumpang wajib memakai = passengers are required to wear.

target: Peserta lomba lari wajib mengambil nomor dada sehari sebelum acara.
english: Race participants are required to collect their bib numbers the day before the event.

target: Pengendara motor wajib memakai helm walaupun jaraknya hanya lima menit.
english: Motorbike riders are required to wear a helmet even if the trip is only five minutes.

target: Anggota wajib mengembalikan barbel ke raknya setelah selesai dipakai.
english: Members are required to return the dumbbells to the rack after use.

target: Anak di bawah sepuluh tahun wajib ditemani orang dewasa di kolam ini.
english: Children under ten must be accompanied by an adult in this pool.

target: Di area kolam dilarang berlari, lantainya licin sekali kalau basah.
english: Running is forbidden in the pool area; the floor is very slippery when wet.
grammar: Dilarang = forbidden (sign language): dilarang berlari = no running. Spoken: jangan lari.

target: Dilarang membawa tas besar ke dalam ruang latihan, silakan pakai loker.
english: Large bags are not allowed in the training room; please use a locker.

target: Di ruang ganti ini dilarang memotret, demi kenyamanan semua anggota.
english: Photography is forbidden in this changing room, for the comfort of all members.
grammar: Memotret = to photograph (from potret): dilarang memotret = no photography.

target: Sampah wajib dibuang di tempat yang sudah disediakan.
english: Trash must be thrown in the bins provided.

target: Peminjam wajib melapor kalau alat olahraga rusak waktu dipakai.
english: Borrowers are required to report it if sports equipment breaks during use.

target: Petugas wajib memeriksa kebersihan air kolam setiap pagi sebelum jam buka.
english: Staff are required to check the cleanliness of the pool water every morning before opening time.

target: Di papan itu tertulis wajib, jadi ini aturan, bukan sekadar saran.
english: The sign says 'wajib', so this is a rule, not just a suggestion.
grammar: Wajib = a rule that binds; saran = a suggestion. Signs with wajib are not optional.

target: Saya merasa lelah sekali setelah rapat panjang tadi siang.
english: I feel really tired after the long meeting earlier this afternoon.
grammar: Merasa + a feeling word = to feel: saya merasa lelah = I feel tired.

target: Dia merasa nyaman tinggal di lingkungan yang tenang ini.
english: She feels comfortable living in this quiet neighborhood.

target: Kami merasa aman berjalan kaki di sekitar hotel pada malam hari.
english: We feel safe walking around the hotel at night.

target: Saya merasa bersalah karena lupa membalas pesan kamu kemarin.
english: I feel guilty because I forgot to reply to your message yesterday.
grammar: Bersalah = guilty, from salah (wrong): merasa bersalah = to feel guilty.

target: Setelah berolahraga pagi, badan saya terasa lebih segar.
english: After morning exercise, my body feels fresher.
grammar: People merasa; things terasa: badan saya terasa segar = my body feels fresh.

target: Anak baru itu masih merasa malu untuk bertanya di kelas.
english: That new student still feels shy about asking questions in class.

target: Saya sempat merasa canggung ketika bertemu mantan bos saya di lift.
english: I briefly felt awkward when I met my former boss in the elevator.

target: Nenek merasa kesepian sejak semua cucunya pindah ke luar kota.
english: Grandma has felt lonely since all her grandchildren moved out of town.

target: Setelah bercerita kepada kamu, saya merasa jauh lebih tenang.
english: After telling you about it, I feel much calmer.

target: Dia merasa dihargai karena idenya dipakai oleh tim.
english: He feels appreciated because his idea was used by the team.

target: Saya mulai merasa bosan dengan menu makan siang yang itu-itu saja.
english: I'm starting to feel bored with the same old lunch menu.
grammar: Itu-itu saja = the same old thing: menu yang itu-itu saja = the same old menu.

target: Kalau kamu merasa tidak enak badan, sebaiknya pulang lebih awal.
english: If you feel unwell, you should go home earlier.
grammar: Tidak enak badan = to feel unwell — literally 'body not nice'.

target: Saya merasa bahwa keputusan ini terlalu buru-buru diambil.
english: I feel that this decision was made too hastily.

target: Dia merasa kalau usahanya selama ini belum dihargai.
english: He feels that his efforts all this time have not yet been appreciated.
grammar: In speech, kalau often replaces bahwa after merasa: dia merasa kalau... = he feels that...

target: Kami merasa suasana kantor jauh lebih baik setelah pindah gedung.
english: We feel the office atmosphere is much better after moving buildings.

target: Saya merasa ada yang aneh dengan suara mesin mobil ini.
english: I feel something is odd about the sound of this car's engine.

target: Ibu merasa masakan hari ini kurang asin, bagaimana menurut kamu?
english: Mom feels today's cooking is not salty enough — what do you think?

target: Jujur saja, saya merasa harga sewa di daerah ini semakin tidak masuk akal.
english: Honestly, I feel rent prices in this area are getting more and more unreasonable.
grammar: Masuk akal = to make sense (literally 'enters reason'): tidak masuk akal = unreasonable.

target: Kelihatannya kamu kurang tidur, apakah semuanya baik-baik saja?
english: It looks like you haven't had enough sleep — is everything okay?
grammar: Kelihatannya = it looks like, built from lihat (see): kelihatannya kamu lelah.

target: Langit gelap sekali, kelihatannya sebentar lagi akan hujan deras.
english: The sky is very dark; it looks like it will pour very soon.

target: Kelihatannya dia senang sekali dengan hadiah ulang tahunnya.
english: It looks like she is really happy with her birthday present.

target: Dari wajahnya, kelihatannya kabar yang dia terima bukan kabar baik.
english: From his face, it looks like the news he received was not good news.

target: Restoran baru itu kelihatannya ramai terus setiap akhir pekan.
english: That new restaurant seems to be packed every weekend.

target: Kelihatannya proyek ini butuh waktu lebih lama dari rencana awal.
english: It looks like this project needs more time than the original plan.

target: Sepertinya saya pernah bertemu dengan dia, tetapi saya lupa di mana.
english: It seems I have met him before, but I forget where.
grammar: Sepertinya = it seems, from seperti (like): sepertinya dia sibuk = it seems he's busy.

target: Sepertinya kunci kamar saya tertinggal di dalam mobil.
english: It seems my room key was left behind in the car.

target: Dia tidak mengangkat telepon, sepertinya sedang sibuk.
english: She is not answering the phone; it seems she is busy.

target: Sepertinya sup ini kurang garam, coba cicipi dulu.
english: It seems this soup lacks salt — try tasting it first.

target: Sepertinya kita harus mencari jalan lain, jalan ini ditutup.
english: It seems we have to look for another road; this road is closed.

target: Sepertinya paket kamu baru akan sampai besok sore.
english: It seems your package will only arrive tomorrow afternoon.

target: Sepertinya musim hujan tahun ini datang lebih awal.
english: It seems the rainy season is coming earlier this year.

target: Sepertinya saya salah turun halte, ini bukan daerah yang saya cari.
english: It seems I got off at the wrong stop; this is not the area I am looking for.
grammar: Sepertinya = it seems. In Jakarta speech you'll hear kayaknya for this everywhere — recognize it, model sepertinya.

target: Sepertinya dia lupa dengan janji yang kita buat kemarin.
english: It seems he forgot the promise we made yesterday.

target: Sepertinya akhir film ini sedih, saya sudah membawa tisu.
english: It seems the ending of this movie is sad; I have already brought tissues.

target: Sepertinya enak kalau kita makan bakso hangat saat hujan begini.
english: Seems like it would be nice to have warm meatball soup in rain like this.
grammar: Sepertinya enak = 'that sounds nice' — a common way to float a food idea.

target: Kelihatannya kamu cocok dengan gaya rambut yang baru itu.
english: It looks like that new hairstyle suits you.

target: Saya senang sekali karena akhirnya bisa bertemu kalian semua di sini.
english: I am really happy because I can finally meet all of you here.

target: Dia senang karena hasil ujiannya lebih baik dari yang dia kira.
english: She is happy because her exam result was better than she expected.

target: Kami senang karena tamu-tamu menikmati masakan buatan ibu.
english: We are glad because the guests enjoyed Mom's home cooking.

target: Anak-anak senang karena besok mereka libur sekolah.
english: The kids are happy because tomorrow they have a day off school.

target: Saya senang bekerja di sini karena rekan-rekan saling membantu.
english: I enjoy working here because my colleagues help each other.
grammar: Saling + verb = each other: saling membantu = help each other.

target: Dia sedih karena harus menjual motor kesayangannya.
english: He is sad because he has to sell his beloved motorbike.
grammar: Kesayangan = beloved/favorite, from sayang: motor kesayangannya = his beloved motorbike.

target: Kami sedih karena tetangga baik kami akan pindah ke kota lain.
english: We are sad because our kind neighbors are going to move to another city.

target: Saya ikut sedih mendengar kabar tentang kakek kamu.
english: I am also saddened to hear the news about your grandfather.
grammar: Ikut + feeling = to share it: saya ikut sedih = I'm sad for you too.

target: Dia kelihatan sedih sejak kucingnya hilang minggu lalu.
english: He has looked sad ever since his cat went missing last week.

target: Saya kecewa karena konsernya dibatalkan pada menit terakhir.
english: I am disappointed because the concert was canceled at the last minute.

target: Penonton kecewa karena tim favorit mereka kalah di babak final.
english: The spectators were disappointed because their favorite team lost in the final round.

target: Dia kecewa dengan pelayanan hotel itu, jadi menulis ulasan panjang.
english: She was disappointed with that hotel's service, so she wrote a long review.
grammar: Kecewa dengan = disappointed with: kecewa dengan pelayanan = disappointed with the service.

target: Jangan kecewa dulu, masih ada kesempatan lain tahun depan.
english: Don't be disappointed yet; there is still another chance next year.

target: Kami sedikit kecewa karena pemandangan dari kamar hotel tidak seindah foto di situs pemesanan.
english: We were a little disappointed because the view from the hotel room was not as beautiful as the photos on the booking site.
grammar: Se- + quality = as ... as: seindah foto = as beautiful as the photo.

target: Orang tuanya bangga karena dia lulus dengan nilai terbaik.
english: Her parents are proud because she graduated with the best grades.

target: Saya bangga pada tim ini karena kalian tidak pernah menyerah.
english: I am proud of this team because you all never gave up.
grammar: Bangga pada + person = proud of: bangga pada tim ini = proud of this team.

target: Dia bangga bisa membayar kuliahnya sendiri tanpa bantuan siapa pun.
english: He is proud that he could pay for his own college without anyone's help.

target: Kami bangga sekali karena kopi dari desa kami sekarang mulai dikenal di luar negeri.
english: We are very proud because coffee from our village is now starting to be known abroad.

target: Ibu selalu bilang dia bangga punya anak yang jujur.
english: Mom always says she is proud to have an honest child.

target: Ibu khawatir karena kakak belum pulang, padahal sudah hampir tengah malam.
english: Mom is worried because my older sibling is not home yet, even though it is almost midnight.
grammar: Padahal = even though / when in fact: belum pulang, padahal sudah malam.

target: Saya khawatir kita akan terjebak macet kalau berangkat siang.
english: I am worried we will get stuck in traffic if we leave at midday.

target: Dia khawatir soal biaya rumah sakit ayahnya.
english: She is worried about her father's hospital costs.

target: Tidak usah khawatir, dokumen kamu sudah saya simpan di lemari.
english: No need to worry; I have already put your documents away in the cupboard.
grammar: Tidak usah = no need to: tidak usah khawatir = no need to worry.

target: Warga khawatir karena hujan deras sering membuat sungai meluap.
english: Residents are worried because heavy rain often makes the river overflow.

target: Saya berharap kamu bisa hadir di acara pernikahan kami bulan depan.
english: I hope you can come to our wedding next month.
grammar: Berharap needs a subject: saya berharap... Semoga opens a wish on its own: Semoga lancar!

target: Kami berharap harga bahan pokok tidak naik lagi tahun ini.
english: We hope the prices of basic goods will not rise again this year.

target: Dia berharap bisa mendapat beasiswa ke luar negeri tahun depan.
english: She hopes she can get a scholarship to go abroad next year.

target: Saya berharap hasil pemeriksaan besok tidak ada masalah serius.
english: I hope tomorrow's examination results show no serious problems.

target: Kami berharap kamu betah bekerja di kantor yang baru.
english: We hope you will feel at home working at the new office.
grammar: Betah = to feel at home somewhere: betah bekerja di sini = happy staying here.

target: Penduduk desa berharap jalan rusak itu segera diperbaiki pemerintah.
english: The villagers hope the damaged road will soon be repaired by the government.

target: Semoga acara besok berjalan lancar dari awal sampai akhir.
english: Hopefully tomorrow's event runs smoothly from start to finish.

target: Semoga keluarga kalian selalu diberi kesehatan dan rezeki.
english: May your family always be blessed with health and good fortune.
grammar: Rezeki = livelihood, blessings — a warm everyday wish word: diberi rezeki.

target: Semoga penerbangan kalian nyaman dan sampai dengan selamat.
english: Hope your flight is comfortable and you all arrive safely.
grammar: Sampai dengan selamat = arrive safely — the standard send-off for travelers.

target: Semoga masalah ini cepat selesai supaya kita semua bisa tenang.
english: Hopefully this problem is resolved quickly so we can all be at ease.

target: Semoga hujan berhenti sebelum kita harus berangkat ke stasiun.
english: Hopefully the rain stops before we have to leave for the station.

target: Semoga tahun ini usaha kecil kamu semakin berkembang.
english: Hopefully this year your small business grows more and more.
grammar: Semakin = more and more: semakin berkembang = growing more and more.

target: Saya lebih suka naik kereta daripada pesawat untuk perjalanan pendek.
english: I prefer taking the train to flying for short trips.
grammar: Lebih suka X daripada Y = to prefer X to Y: lebih suka kereta daripada pesawat.

target: Dia lebih suka bekerja pagi-pagi karena kantornya masih sepi.
english: He prefers working very early because his office is still quiet.

target: Kami lebih suka memasak sendiri daripada makan di luar setiap hari.
english: We prefer cooking ourselves to eating out every day.

target: Anak saya lebih suka membaca komik daripada buku pelajaran.
english: My child prefers reading comics to schoolbooks.

target: Untuk liburan, saya lebih suka gunung yang sejuk daripada pantai yang panas.
english: For vacations, I prefer cool mountains to hot beaches.

target: Ayah lebih suka kopi hitam tanpa gula, katanya lebih nikmat.
english: Dad prefers black coffee without sugar; he says it tastes better.
grammar: Katanya = he/she says, they say: katanya lebih nikmat = he says it tastes better.

target: Saya lebih suka rapat singkat di pagi hari daripada rapat panjang sore-sore.
english: I prefer short morning meetings to long late-afternoon meetings.

target: Dia lebih suka berbelanja di pasar karena bisa menawar harga.
english: She prefers shopping at the market because she can bargain over prices.

target: Kalau boleh memilih, saya lebih suka duduk dekat jendela.
english: If I may choose, I prefer sitting near the window.

target: Kakak lebih suka film komedi, sedangkan saya lebih suka film sejarah.
english: My older sibling prefers comedy films, while I prefer historical films.
grammar: Sedangkan contrasts two people or things: kakak suka komedi, sedangkan saya suka sejarah.

target: Tidak apa-apa datang terlambat, yang penting kamu datang dengan selamat.
english: It's fine to arrive late; the main thing is you arrive safely.
grammar: Yang penting = the main thing is: yang penting kamu selamat = what matters is you're safe.

target: Hasilnya belum sempurna, tetapi yang penting kita sudah mencoba.
english: The result is not perfect yet, but the main thing is we have tried.

target: Yang penting sekarang adalah kesehatan kamu, pekerjaan bisa menunggu.
english: The important thing right now is your health; work can wait.

target: Menang atau kalah, yang penting kalian bermain dengan jujur.
english: Win or lose, the main thing is you all play honestly.

target: Yang penting bagi saya, anak-anak tumbuh sehat dan bahagia.
english: What matters to me is that the kids grow up healthy and happy.

target: Rumahnya tidak besar, yang penting nyaman untuk keluarga kami.
english: The house is not big; the main thing is it's comfortable for our family.

target: Yang penting dokumennya lengkap dulu, sisanya bisa kita urus nanti.
english: The main thing is the documents are complete first; we can sort out the rest later.

target: Gajinya biasa saja, tetapi yang penting suasana kerjanya menyenangkan.
english: The salary is just average, but the main thing is the work atmosphere is pleasant.

target: Bagaimana menurut kamu, apakah warna ini cocok untuk ruang tamu?
english: What do you think — does this color suit the living room?
grammar: Bagaimana menurut kamu? = What do you think? — literally 'how according to you?'

target: Bagaimana menurut Anda tentang rencana perubahan jam kerja ini?
english: What is your opinion of this plan to change the working hours?
grammar: In formal settings (meetings, clients) use Anda instead of kamu: Bagaimana menurut Anda?

target: Bagaimana pendapat kalian tentang usul membuat jadwal piket baru?
english: What do you all think about the proposal to make a new duty roster?

target: Menurut saya, presentasi kamu tadi sudah jelas dan meyakinkan.
english: In my opinion, your presentation just now was clear and convincing.

target: Menurut saya pribadi, tempat wisata ini terlalu ramai untuk liburan keluarga yang tenang.
english: Personally, I think this tourist spot is too crowded for a calm family holiday.

target: Kalau menurut saya, kita sebaiknya menunda dulu pembelian mobil itu.
english: In my opinion, we had better postpone buying that car for now.

target: Saya setuju dengan pendapat kamu tentang pentingnya istirahat cukup.
english: I agree with your opinion about the importance of getting enough rest.

target: Saya kurang setuju kalau semua rapat dipindahkan ke hari Jumat.
english: I don't quite agree with moving all the meetings to Friday.
grammar: Kurang setuju softens disagreement — politer than a flat tidak setuju.

target: Maaf, saya berbeda pendapat soal cara membagi tugas ini.
english: Sorry, I have a different opinion about how to divide these tasks.
grammar: Berbeda pendapat = to disagree — literally 'to differ in opinion'.

target: Sebagian teman setuju, sebagian lagi menolak rencana itu.
english: Some friends agree; some others reject the plan.
grammar: Sebagian ... sebagian lagi = some ... others: sebagian setuju, sebagian lagi menolak.

target: Dia jarang berpendapat di rapat, tetapi idenya selalu bagus.
english: He rarely gives his opinion in meetings, but his ideas are always good.

target: Sebelum memutuskan, kita perlu mendengarkan pendapat semua anggota.
english: Before deciding, we need to listen to the opinions of all the members.

target: Menurut pengalaman saya, pelanggan lebih suka jawaban yang jujur.
english: In my experience, customers prefer honest answers.

target: Jangan takut menyampaikan pendapat, di sini semua ide dihargai.
english: Don't be afraid to voice your opinion; here every idea is appreciated.
grammar: Menyampaikan pendapat = to voice an opinion, from sampai (reach).

target: Menurut kamu, lebih baik kita berangkat malam ini atau besok pagi?
english: What do you think — is it better to leave tonight or tomorrow morning?

target: Saya menghargai pendapat kamu, tetapi kali ini saya punya cara sendiri.
english: I appreciate your opinion, but this time I have my own way.

target: Setelah mendengar pendapat kalian, saya jadi lebih yakin dengan pilihan ini.
english: After hearing all of your opinions, I feel more confident about this choice.

target: Pendapat kita memang berbeda, tetapi saya yakin kita tetap bisa bekerja sama dengan baik.
english: Our opinions do differ, but I am sure we can still work together well.

target: Menurut warga sekitar, pasar malam itu paling ramai hari Sabtu.
english: According to the local residents, that night market is busiest on Saturdays.

target: Terima kasih atas masukan kalian, semua akan kami pertimbangkan.
english: Thank you for your input; we will consider all of it.
grammar: Masukan = feedback/input, from masuk (enter): terima kasih atas masukan kalian.

target: Kabar baik itu membuat kami lega setelah menunggu berminggu-minggu.
english: That good news made us relieved after waiting for weeks.
grammar: Membuat + person + feeling = to make someone feel: membuat kami lega = made us relieved.

target: Saya terharu melihat murid-murid menyiapkan kejutan untuk guru mereka.
english: I was touched to see the students preparing a surprise for their teacher.

target: Dia puas dengan hasil renovasi rumahnya walaupun biayanya besar.
english: He is satisfied with the result of his house renovation even though the cost was high.

target: Awalnya saya ragu, tetapi sekarang saya yakin keputusan ini benar.
english: At first I was unsure, but now I am sure this decision is right.
grammar: Awalnya = at first, from awal (beginning): awalnya saya ragu = at first I was unsure.

target: Suasana hati saya langsung membaik setelah mendengar suara anak-anak.
english: My mood improved instantly after hearing the children's voices.
grammar: Suasana hati = mood — literally 'atmosphere of the heart'.

target: Dia berusaha tetap sabar walaupun antreannya panjang sekali.
english: She tries to stay patient even though the queue is very long.

target: Kami kaget mendengar harga tanah di daerah ini naik dua kali lipat.
english: We were shocked to hear that land prices in this area have doubled.
grammar: Dua kali lipat = double: naik dua kali lipat = doubled.

target: Setiap kali gugup, dia menarik napas panjang supaya lebih tenang.
english: Every time he gets nervous, he takes a deep breath to feel calmer.

target: Perasaan saya campur aduk antara senang dan sedih pada hari terakhir saya bekerja di sini.
english: My feelings were all mixed up between happy and sad on my last day working here.
grammar: Campur aduk = all mixed up: perasaan campur aduk = mixed feelings.

target: Jangan pendam perasaan kamu sendirian, ceritakan kepada orang terdekat.
english: Don't bury your feelings alone; tell someone close to you.

target: Saya kagum pada semangat kerja tim kecil ini.
english: I admire the working spirit of this small team.

target: Dia bersemangat sekali menceritakan rencana pernikahannya kepada kami.
english: She was very enthusiastic telling us about her wedding plans.

target: Pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang setelah dia mencoba berenang lagi.
english: Little by little his fear disappeared after he tried swimming again.
grammar: Pelan-pelan = little by little: pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang.

target: Menurut saya, jujur tentang perasaan lebih baik daripada diam saja.
english: In my opinion, being honest about feelings is better than just staying silent.

target: Apa pun pendapat orang, keluarga kami tetap bangga pada pilihan kamu.
english: Whatever people's opinions, our family remains proud of your choice.
grammar: Apa pun = whatever / no matter what: apa pun pendapat orang = whatever people think.

target: Semakin lama saya tinggal di sini, semakin saya suka kota ini.
english: The longer I live here, the more I like this city.
grammar: Semakin ... semakin = the more ... the more: semakin lama, semakin suka = the longer, the more (I) like it.

target: Semakin mahal restorannya, semakin kecil porsinya.
english: The more expensive the restaurant, the smaller the portions.

target: Harga rumah di daerah ini semakin tinggi setiap tahun.
english: House prices in this area get higher and higher every year.
grammar: Semakin + adjective alone = getting more and more X: semakin tinggi = higher and higher.

target: Semakin sering kamu berlatih, semakin cepat kamu maju.
english: The more often you practice, the faster you improve.

target: Cuaca semakin panas menjelang akhir musim kemarau.
english: The weather gets hotter and hotter toward the end of the dry season.
grammar: Menjelang = approaching (a time): menjelang akhir musim = toward the end of the season.

target: Semakin tua, ayah saya semakin rajin berolahraga.
english: The older he gets, the more diligently my father exercises.

target: Jalan ke pusat kota semakin macet sejak pasar baru dibuka.
english: The road to the city center has gotten more and more congested since the new market opened.

target: Semakin banyak saya membaca tentang pulau itu, semakin ingin saya ke sana.
english: The more I read about that island, the more I want to go there.

target: Antrean di kasir semakin panjang menjelang jam makan siang.
english: The line at the checkout gets longer and longer toward lunchtime.

target: Semakin dekat hari keberangkatan, semakin gugup saya.
english: The closer the departure day gets, the more nervous I am.
grammar: Ke-...-an makes a noun: berangkat = to depart, keberangkatan = departure.

target: Kopi di kafe itu semakin enak setelah mereka mengganti mesinnya.
english: The coffee at that cafe has gotten even better since they replaced the machine.

target: Semakin malam, pasar malam itu semakin ramai.
english: The later it gets at night, the busier that night market becomes.

target: Semakin besar layar ponsel, semakin cepat baterainya habis.
english: The bigger a phone's screen, the faster its battery runs out.

target: Udara di gunung semakin dingin begitu hari mulai gelap.
english: The air in the mountains gets colder and colder once it starts to get dark.

target: Semakin sering dia begadang, semakin sering dia sakit kepala.
english: The more often he stays up late, the more often he gets headaches.
grammar: Begadang = to stay up very late: sering begadang = often stays up late.

target: Sungai di belakang kompleks semakin bersih sejak warga rajin membuang sampah pada tempatnya.
english: The river behind the housing complex has gotten cleaner since residents diligently throw trash where it belongs.

target: Makin siang, jalanan di kota ini makin panas.
english: The later in the day it gets, the hotter the streets in this city are.
grammar: Makin is the everyday spoken short form of semakin: makin siang = the later in the day.

target: Belanja online makin populer, jadi toko kecil harus ikut berjualan di internet.
english: Online shopping is getting more and more popular, so small shops have to start selling on the internet too.

target: Tas ini sama mahalnya dengan tas yang kamu beli kemarin.
english: This bag is as expensive as the bag you bought yesterday.
grammar: Sama + adjective + -nya + dengan = as ... as: sama mahalnya dengan = as expensive as.

target: Kopi di warung ini sama enaknya dengan kopi di kafe mahal.
english: The coffee at this food stall is as good as the coffee at an expensive cafe.

target: Kamar hotel ini sama luasnya dengan kamar tidur saya di rumah.
english: This hotel room is as spacious as my bedroom at home.

target: Adik saya sekarang sama tingginya dengan ayah kami.
english: My younger sibling is now as tall as our father.

target: Harga tiket kereta sama dengan harga tiket bus untuk rute ini.
english: The price of a train ticket is the same as the price of a bus ticket for this route.
grammar: Sama dengan = the same as: harga A sama dengan harga B = price A equals price B.

target: Jadwal kerja saya minggu ini sama dengan jadwal minggu lalu.
english: My work schedule this week is the same as last week's schedule.

target: Berat ponsel baru ini hampir sama dengan ponsel lama saya.
english: This new phone's weight is almost the same as my old phone's.

target: Kebiasaan makan kakak sama dengan kebiasaan ayah; dua-duanya suka pedas.
english: My older sibling's eating habits are the same as father's; they both like spicy food.
grammar: Dua-duanya = both of them: dua-duanya suka pedas = they both like spicy food.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini sama basahnya dengan musim hujan tahun lalu.
english: This year's rainy season is as wet as last year's rainy season.

target: Warna jaket saya sama dengan warna jaket teman sekantor saya.
english: The color of my jacket is the same as the color of my officemate's jacket.

target: Suasana desa ini sama tenangnya dengan desa tempat saya lahir.
english: The atmosphere of this village is as peaceful as the village where I was born.
grammar: Tempat + clause = where: desa tempat saya lahir = the village where I was born.

target: Gaji di kantor baru itu hampir sama dengan gaji saya sekarang.
english: The salary at that new office is almost the same as my current salary.

target: Menu sarapan di dua hotel itu hampir sama.
english: The breakfast menus at those two hotels are almost the same.

target: Laptop ini sama cepatnya dengan laptop kantor, tetapi jauh lebih murah.
english: This laptop is as fast as the office laptop, but much cheaper.
grammar: Jauh lebih = much more: jauh lebih murah = much cheaper.

target: Suara anak kembar itu sama persis; saya sering salah memanggil nama.
english: Those twins' voices are exactly the same; I often call the wrong name.
grammar: Persis = exactly: sama persis = exactly the same.

target: Iklim di Bandung berbeda dengan iklim di Jakarta; di sana jauh lebih sejuk.
english: The climate in Bandung is different from the climate in Jakarta; it is much cooler there.
grammar: Berbeda dengan = different from: berbeda dengan iklim Jakarta = different from Jakarta's climate.

target: Kebiasaan sarapan orang sini berbeda dengan kebiasaan di kampung saya.
english: The breakfast habits of people here are different from the habits back in my hometown.

target: Rasa mangga muda berbeda jauh dengan rasa mangga yang sudah matang.
english: The taste of an unripe mango is very different from the taste of a ripe one.
grammar: Muda usually means young, but for fruit it means unripe: mangga muda = unripe mango.

target: Model tahun ini sedikit berbeda dengan model tahun lalu, tetapi harganya jauh lebih mahal.
english: This year's model is slightly different from last year's model, but the price is much higher.

target: Suasana pasar tradisional berbeda sekali dengan suasana mal yang sejuk.
english: The atmosphere of a traditional market is very different from the atmosphere of a cool mall.

target: Cara adik saya belajar berbeda dengan cara saya; dia harus sambil mendengarkan musik.
english: The way my younger sibling studies is different from my way; he has to listen to music while doing it.

target: Jadwal bus hari Minggu berbeda dengan jadwal hari kerja, jadi cek dulu.
english: The Sunday bus schedule is different from the weekday schedule, so check first.

target: Pendapat saya berbeda dengan pendapat atasan, tetapi kami tetap bekerja sama.
english: My opinion is different from my boss's opinion, but we still work together.

target: Gaya hidup di kota besar jelas berbeda dengan gaya hidup di desa.
english: The lifestyle in a big city is clearly different from the lifestyle in a village.

target: Kopi robusta beda jauh dengan arabika; rasanya lebih pahit dan lebih kuat.
english: Robusta coffee is very different from arabica; it tastes more bitter and stronger.
grammar: Beda is the everyday short form of berbeda: beda jauh = very different.

target: Musim di Indonesia berbeda dengan musim di Eropa; di sini hanya ada dua.
english: The seasons in Indonesia are different from the seasons in Europe; here there are only two.

target: Harga di menu berbeda dengan harga yang saya bayar di kasir.
english: The price on the menu is different from the price I paid at the register.

target: Wajah anak itu mirip sekali dengan wajah ibunya.
english: That child's face looks very much like his mother's face.
grammar: Mirip (dengan) = similar to, looks like: mirip ibunya = looks like his mother.

target: Logo merek baru itu mirip dengan logo merek terkenal, jadi banyak orang bingung.
english: That new brand's logo is similar to a famous brand's logo, so many people are confused.

target: Rasa buah ini mirip mangga, tetapi sedikit lebih asam.
english: This fruit tastes similar to mango, but is slightly more sour.

target: Suara penyanyi muda itu mirip dengan suara penyanyi favorit ayah saya.
english: That young singer's voice is similar to the voice of my father's favorite singer.

target: Kota tua di sini mirip dengan kota tua di Semarang.
english: The old town here is similar to the old town in Semarang.

target: Kebiasaan tidur saya mirip dengan kebiasaan kakek: tidur cepat, bangun sebelum subuh.
english: My sleeping habits are similar to grandfather's habits: sleep early, wake up before dawn.
grammar: Subuh = dawn, the hours before sunrise: bangun sebelum subuh = up before dawn.

target: Desain ponsel ini mirip dengan merek sebelah, tetapi kameranya kalah jauh.
english: This phone's design is similar to the neighboring brand's, but its camera is far behind.
grammar: Kalah jauh = far behind (literally loses by far): kameranya kalah jauh = its camera is far worse.

target: Bau sabun ini mirip bau jeruk segar.
english: This soap's smell is similar to the smell of fresh oranges.

target: Cara dia menjelaskan mirip dengan cara dosen kami mengajar di kelas.
english: The way he explains things is similar to the way our lecturer teaches in class.

target: Rumah-rumah di kompleks ini mirip semua; saya pernah salah masuk pagar.
english: The houses in this complex all look alike; I once went through the wrong gate.

target: Setelah hujan, jalan kampung itu licin seperti kaca.
english: After the rain, that village road is slippery like glass.
grammar: Seperti = like, for comparisons: licin seperti kaca = slippery like glass.

target: Kamar anak saya berantakan seperti kapal pecah.
english: My child's room is a mess, like a shipwreck.
grammar: Seperti kapal pecah (like a wrecked ship) is THE image for a hopelessly messy room.

target: Suara mesin cuci tua itu seperti suara pesawat di bandara.
english: The sound of that old washing machine is like the sound of a plane at the airport.

target: Kulit bayi itu halus seperti sutra.
english: That baby's skin is smooth like silk.

target: Antrean tiket konser itu panjang seperti ular.
english: The line for those concert tickets is long like a snake.

target: Siang ini panasnya seperti di dalam oven.
english: This afternoon the heat is like being inside an oven.
grammar: Adding -nya makes hot into the heat: panas = hot, panasnya = the heat.

target: Dia tahu semua gang di kota ini seperti sopir taksi lama.
english: He knows every alley in this city like a longtime taxi driver.

target: Air laut di pantai itu jernih seperti kolam renang.
english: The seawater at that beach is clear like a swimming pool.

target: Kayak mimpi rasanya; tiket promo ke Jepang itu akhirnya saya dapat.
english: It feels like a dream; I finally got that promo ticket to Japan.
grammar: Kayak = colloquial seperti (like); you hear it everywhere: kayak mimpi = like a dream.

target: Kopi buatan ibu pahitnya kayak obat, tetapi saya tetap minum.
english: Mom's coffee is as bitter as medicine, but I drink it anyway.
grammar: Kayak is casual speech; in writing use seperti: pahit kayak obat = bitter like medicine.

target: Setelah lembur seminggu penuh, badan saya lemas seperti tanpa tenaga.
english: After a full week of overtime, my body feels weak, as if it has no energy.

target: Adik tidur nyenyak seperti bayi meskipun tetangga sedang pesta.
english: My younger sibling sleeps soundly like a baby even though the neighbors are having a party.

target: Pagi ini kabut tebal seperti asap; ujung jalan hampir tidak kelihatan.
english: This morning the fog is thick like smoke; the end of the street is barely visible.
grammar: Kelihatan = visible, can be seen: hampir tidak kelihatan = barely visible.

target: Dua sahabat itu ke mana-mana selalu bersama, lengket seperti perangko.
english: Those two best friends go everywhere together, stuck to each other like a stamp.
grammar: Lengket kayak perangko (stuck like a stamp) is the image for two people who are never apart.

target: Seperti orang baru gajian, dia mentraktir semua teman kantornya.
english: Like someone who just got paid, he treated all his officemates.
grammar: Gajian = payday, having just been paid: baru gajian = fresh off payday.

target: Ini bakso paling enak yang pernah saya coba di kota ini.
english: This is the tastiest bakso I have ever tried in this city.
grammar: Paling + yang pernah = the most ... ever: paling enak yang pernah saya coba = tastiest I ever tried.

target: Itu gunung paling indah yang pernah kami daki.
english: That is the most beautiful mountain we have ever climbed.

target: Kereta pagi adalah cara paling cepat untuk sampai ke bandara.
english: The morning train is the fastest way to get to the airport.
grammar: Adalah links two nouns (A is B); never use it before an adjective.

target: Februari biasanya bulan paling basah di kota kami.
english: February is usually the wettest month in our city.

target: Kasur ini paling empuk dari semua kasur yang kami coba di toko.
english: This mattress is the softest of all the mattresses we tried in the store.
grammar: Paling ... dari semua = the most ... of all: paling empuk dari semua kasur = softest of all the mattresses.

target: Dia orang paling sabar yang pernah saya kenal di kantor.
english: He is the most patient person I have ever known at the office.

target: Film itu film paling lucu yang kami tonton tahun ini.
english: That movie is the funniest film we watched this year.

target: Sejak dibuka, jalan tol baru menjadi rute paling cepat menuju pelabuhan.
english: Since it opened, the new toll road has become the fastest route to the harbor.

target: Kamar di lantai atas paling sejuk karena dapat angin dari laut.
english: The room upstairs is the coolest because it gets the breeze from the sea.

target: Ini keputusan paling sulit yang pernah saya ambil selama bekerja.
english: This is the hardest decision I have ever made in my working life.

target: Pantai di sisi timur pulau itu paling sepi pada hari kerja.
english: The beach on the east side of the island is the quietest on weekdays.

target: Nenek selalu bangun paling pagi di rumah kami.
english: Grandma always gets up the earliest in our house.
grammar: Paling also works with time words: bangun paling pagi = up the earliest.

target: Harga di toko itu paling murah, tetapi antreannya juga paling panjang.
english: The prices at that store are the cheapest, but its line is also the longest.
grammar: Ter- + adjective can replace paling: termurah = paling murah = the cheapest.

target: Agustus bulan paling ramai di pulau itu karena musim liburan.
english: August is the busiest month on that island because of the holiday season.

target: Soto di warung ini paling terkenal; turis pun rela antre satu jam.
english: The soto at this stall is the most famous; even tourists are willing to line up for an hour.
grammar: Pun after a noun = even: turis pun = even tourists.

target: Kamus ini paling lengkap untuk pelajar pemula seperti saya.
english: This dictionary is the most complete for beginner learners like me.

target: Dari semua sepatu lari yang saya punya, sepatu ini paling ringan.
english: Of all the running shoes I own, these shoes are the lightest.

target: Menurut hampir semua siswa, ujian hari terakhir paling susah.
english: According to almost all the students, the last day's exam was the hardest.
grammar: Menurut = according to: menurut siswa = according to the students.

target: Lagu itu paling sering diputar di radio sepanjang bulan ini.
english: That song has been played the most often on the radio all this month.

target: Musim kemarau tahun ini paling panjang dalam sepuluh tahun terakhir.
english: This year's dry season is the longest in the last ten years.

target: Saya kira restoran itu mahal, ternyata harganya cukup masuk akal.
english: I thought that restaurant was expensive; it turns out the prices are quite reasonable.
grammar: Ternyata = it turns out: saya kira mahal, ternyata murah = I thought it was expensive, turns out it's cheap.

target: Ternyata jalan kecil di belakang pasar lebih cepat daripada jalan utama.
english: It turns out the small road behind the market is faster than the main road.

target: Kami kira hotel itu jauh dari pantai, ternyata hanya lima menit jalan kaki.
english: We thought that hotel was far from the beach; it turns out it is only a five-minute walk.

target: Ternyata tetangga baru kami dokter di rumah sakit tempat ibu dirawat.
english: It turns out our new neighbor is a doctor at the hospital where mother is being treated.

target: Ponsel murah ini ternyata lebih awet daripada ponsel mahal saya yang dulu.
english: This cheap phone turns out to be more durable than my old expensive phone.
grammar: Awet = long-lasting, durable: lebih awet = lasts longer.

target: Setelah dicoba, resep nenek ternyata lebih enak daripada resep dari internet.
english: After trying it, grandma's recipe turns out to be tastier than the recipe from the internet.

target: Ternyata dia sudah pindah ke Surabaya sejak awal tahun lalu.
english: It turns out he already moved to Surabaya at the beginning of last year.

target: Paket yang saya tunggu seminggu ternyata tertinggal di kantor pos.
english: The package I waited a week for turned out to have been left behind at the post office.
grammar: Tertinggal = left behind by accident: paket ternyata tertinggal = the package got left behind.

target: Ternyata musim kemarau di daerah ini tetap sering hujan pada sore hari.
english: It turns out that in this area's dry season it still often rains in the afternoon.

target: Barang diskon itu ternyata stok lama, jadi saya batal membelinya.
english: That discounted item turned out to be old stock, so I ended up not buying it.

target: Saya pikir dia marah kepada saya, ternyata dia hanya lelah setelah lembur.
english: I thought he was angry at me; it turns out he was just tired after working overtime.

target: Ternyata kunci mobil ada di kantong jaket saya sejak tadi.
english: It turns out the car keys have been in my jacket pocket this whole time.
grammar: Sejak tadi = since earlier, all along: ada di sini sejak tadi = has been here all along.

target: Dia tetap memakai jaket tebal, padahal cuaca hari ini panas sekali.
english: He still wears a thick jacket, even though the weather today is very hot.
grammar: Padahal = even though / when in fact, for surprising contrast: padahal panas = even though it's hot.

target: Adik membeli ponsel baru lagi, padahal ponsel lamanya masih bagus.
english: My younger sibling bought a new phone again, even though his old phone is still fine.

target: Restoran itu selalu penuh, padahal menurut saya rasanya biasa saja.
english: That restaurant is always full, even though in my opinion the food tastes just average.

target: Dia berangkat tanpa payung, padahal langit sudah gelap sejak pagi.
english: He left without an umbrella, even though the sky had been dark since morning.

target: Harga kamar di situ mahal, padahal fasilitasnya sama dengan hotel sebelah.
english: The room rates there are expensive, even though the facilities are the same as the hotel next door.

target: Ayah masih menonton bola sampai larut, padahal besok dia harus bangun jam lima.
english: Father is still watching football until late, even though tomorrow he has to get up at five.

target: Saya lupa membawa dompet, padahal tas sudah saya cek dua kali.
english: I forgot to bring my wallet, even though I had already checked my bag twice.

target: Kota ini terasa sepi, padahal ini malam Minggu.
english: This city feels quiet, even though it is Saturday night.

target: Dia bilang sedang sibuk, padahal saya melihat dia duduk santai di kafe.
