english: He says he is busy, even though I saw him sitting relaxed at a cafe.

target: Buah di pasar pagi lebih segar, padahal harganya lebih murah daripada di supermarket.
english: The fruit at the morning market is fresher, even though it costs less than at the supermarket.

target: Anak itu bilang sudah kenyang, padahal makanannya baru habis setengah.
english: That child says he is already full, even though only half of his food is finished.

target: Kami hampir membatalkan piknik, padahal sore itu cuaca akhirnya cerah.
english: We almost canceled the picnic, when in fact the weather that afternoon finally turned out sunny.

target: Saya kira dia akan marah, justru dia tertawa mendengar cerita itu.
english: I thought he would be angry; on the contrary, he laughed hearing that story.
grammar: Justru = actually / on the contrary, flips an expectation: justru dia tertawa = on the contrary, he laughed.

target: Obat warung itu justru membuat kepala saya semakin pusing.
english: That corner-store medicine actually made my headache even worse.

target: Jangan berangkat siang; justru pagi-pagi jalanan lebih kosong.
english: Do not leave at midday; it is actually early in the morning that the roads are emptier.
grammar: Doubling a time word = really early/late: pagi-pagi = early in the morning.

target: Musim hujan justru waktu terbaik untuk menikmati kopi hangat di rumah.
english: The rainy season is actually the best time to enjoy warm coffee at home.

target: Barang yang lebih mahal itu justru rusak lebih dulu.
english: The more expensive item actually broke first.

target: Dia justru lebih tenang setelah mendengar hasil ujian itu.
english: He was actually calmer after hearing that exam result.

target: Di desa kecil itu, sinyal internet justru paling kuat di dekat sawah.
english: In that small village, the internet signal is actually strongest near the rice fields.

target: Saya justru suka rumah tua ini karena halamannya luas.
english: I actually like this old house because its yard is spacious.

target: Kritik dari pelanggan justru membantu toko kami maju.
english: Criticism from customers actually helps our store move forward.

target: Setelah pindah ke kota kecil, pengeluaran kami justru naik.
english: After moving to a small town, our expenses actually went up.

target: Hujan deras semalam justru membuat udara pagi ini segar sekali.
english: Last night's heavy rain actually made this morning's air very fresh.

target: Saya bekerja di perusahaan ini sejak tahun dua ribu dua puluh.
english: I have worked at this company since the year two thousand twenty.
grammar: Sejak = since a starting point: sejak tahun lalu = since last year. The verb itself does not change.

target: Kami tinggal di kompleks ini sejak anak pertama kami lahir.
english: We have lived in this housing complex since our first child was born.

target: Sejak pindah ke Jakarta, dia jarang pulang ke kampungnya.
english: Since moving to Jakarta, he rarely goes home to his hometown.

target: Hujan turun terus sejak subuh, jadi jalanan masih basah.
english: It has been raining nonstop since dawn, so the streets are still wet.
grammar: Terus after a verb = keeps on: hujan turun terus = it keeps raining.

target: Sejak rutin berolahraga pagi, tidur saya jauh lebih nyenyak.
english: Since exercising regularly in the morning, my sleep has been much more sound.

target: Dia belum makan apa-apa sejak siang karena rapatnya panjang sekali.
english: She hasn't eaten anything since midday because her meeting was very long.

target: Sejak harga bahan naik, ibu lebih sering memasak di rumah.
english: Since ingredient prices went up, Mom cooks at home more often.

target: Kami belum bertemu lagi sejak lulus kuliah lima tahun lalu.
english: We haven't met again since graduating from college five years ago.
grammar: Sejak also takes an event: sejak lulus = since graduating, sejak menikah = since getting married.

target: Sejak ada jalan tol baru, perjalanan ke bandara jauh lebih cepat.
english: Since there has been a new toll road, the trip to the airport is much faster.

target: Toko roti di ujung jalan itu sudah buka sejak jam enam pagi.
english: That bakery at the end of the street has been open since six this morning.
grammar: Sejak marks a running start point: sudah buka sejak jam enam = open since six. Daily hours use mulai.

target: Sejak kejadian itu, dia selalu mengunci pintu dua kali.
english: Since that incident, she always locks the door twice.

target: Adik saya suka menggambar sejak kecil, sekarang dia jadi desainer.
english: My little sister has liked drawing since she was small; now she has become a designer.

target: Selama musim hujan, kami jarang makan di luar rumah.
english: During the rainy season, we rarely eat outside the house.
grammar: Selama + time = during/for: selama liburan = during the holiday, selama dua jam = for two hours.

target: Dia bekerja di luar negeri selama tiga tahun sebelum kembali.
english: He worked abroad for three years before coming back.

target: Selama rapat tadi, semua ponsel peserta harus dimatikan.
english: During the meeting earlier, all the participants' phones had to be turned off.

target: Kami menginap di rumah paman selama liburan sekolah anak-anak.
english: We stayed at my uncle's house during the children's school holidays.

target: Selama saya di luar kota, tolong siram tanaman di teras.
english: While I am out of town, please water the plants on the terrace.

target: Jalan utama ditutup selama festival, jadi kami lewat gang kecil.
english: The main road is closed during the festival, so we go through a small alley.

target: Dia tidak boleh mengangkat barang berat selama tangannya belum sembuh.
english: He may not lift heavy things while his hand hasn't healed yet.
grammar: Selama + clause = while/as long as: selama tangannya belum sembuh = while his hand isn't healed yet.

target: Selama dua minggu ini, ayah harus ke dokter setiap hari Senin.
english: For these two weeks, Dad has to go to the doctor every Monday.

target: Listrik di rumah kami mati selama hampir lima jam kemarin.
english: The electricity at our house was out for almost five hours yesterday.

target: Selama mengantre di bank, saya sempat membaca satu bab novel.
english: While queuing at the bank, I managed to read one chapter of a novel.

target: Paket yang saya pesan minggu lalu belum datang sampai sekarang.
english: The package I ordered last week still hasn't arrived up to now.
grammar: Sampai sekarang = up to now: belum datang sampai sekarang = still hasn't come.

target: Kami berteman sejak sekolah dasar dan masih akrab sampai sekarang.
english: We have been friends since elementary school and are still close up to now.

target: Sampai sekarang saya belum berani menyetir sendiri di jalan tol.
english: Up to now I still haven't dared to drive alone on the toll road.

target: Resep sambal nenek masih dipakai keluarga kami sampai sekarang.
english: Grandma's sambal recipe is still used by our family to this day.

target: Dia sudah melamar ke banyak perusahaan, tapi belum ada jawaban sampai sekarang.
english: He has applied to many companies, but there has been no answer up to now.

target: Sampai sekarang, kunci gudang itu belum ketemu juga.
english: Up to now, that warehouse key still hasn't turned up.
grammar: Ketemu = everyday 'found/turn up': kuncinya belum ketemu = the key hasn't turned up.

target: Lagu itu terkenal sejak dulu dan masih sering diputar sampai sekarang.
english: That song has been famous since long ago and is still often played up to now.

target: Sampai sekarang nenek masih rutin berolahraga pagi di taman kompleks.
english: To this day Grandma still regularly exercises in the morning at the neighborhood park.

target: Kereta kami baru saja tiba di stasiun akhir.
english: Our train has just arrived at the final station.
grammar: Baru saja + verb = just did: baru saja tiba = just arrived.

target: Saya baru saja menutup laptop ketika bos menelepon.
english: I had just closed my laptop when the boss called.

target: Mereka baru saja pindah, jadi rumahnya masih penuh kardus.
english: They just moved, so their house is still full of cardboard boxes.

target: Barusan ada yang mengetuk pintu, tapi tidak ada orang di luar.
english: Just now someone knocked on the door, but there was no one outside.
grammar: Barusan = spoken 'just now'; in writing use baru saja. Barusan dia telepon. = He just called.

target: Kamu mendengar suara aneh itu barusan?
english: Did you hear that strange sound just now?
grammar: Mendengar = hear (it reaches your ears); mendengarkan = listen (on purpose).

target: Dia baru saja selesai mandi waktu tamunya datang.
english: She had just finished bathing when her guest arrived.

target: Barusan saya melihat dompetmu di atas meja makan.
english: Just now I saw your wallet on the dining table.

target: Kopi ini baru saja dibuat, hati-hati masih panas.
english: This coffee was just made; careful, it's still hot.

target: Baru saja hujan reda, sekarang mendung tebal lagi.
english: The rain just let up, and now it's heavily overcast again.

target: Barusan manajer mencari kamu di ruang rapat.
english: Just now the manager was looking for you in the meeting room.

target: Malam sebelumnya dia tidur larut, jadi pagi itu dia bangun kesiangan.
english: The night before, he had gone to sleep late, so that morning he overslept.
grammar: Sebelumnya after a time word = the ... before: malam sebelumnya = the night before.

target: Kami sarapan dulu di warung; sesudahnya kami langsung ke stasiun.
english: We had breakfast first at a food stall; after that we went straight to the station.
grammar: Sesudahnya = after that, linking two events: makan dulu, sesudahnya berangkat = eat first, then leave.

target: Sehari sebelumnya, semua dokumen sudah saya siapkan di map merah.
english: The day before, I had already prepared all the documents in a red folder.

target: Dia sempat ragu sebelumnya, tapi akhirnya dia menerima tawaran itu.
english: He was hesitant before, but in the end he accepted the offer.
grammar: Sempat = at some point managed/happened to: sempat ragu = did hesitate for a while.

target: Rapatnya selesai jam empat; sesudahnya kami minum kopi bersama.
english: The meeting ended at four; after that we drank coffee together.

target: Saya pernah datang ke kota ini sebelumnya, tapi hanya sebentar.
english: I have come to this city before, but only briefly.

target: Cuci tangan dulu; sesudahnya baru kita makan bersama.
english: Wash your hands first; only after that do we eat together.
grammar: Baru after a time link = only then: sesudahnya baru makan = only after that do we eat.

target: Seminggu sebelumnya, kami sudah memesan meja untuk acara ulang tahun ibu.
english: A week before, we had already booked a table for Mom's birthday event.

target: Filmnya seru, tapi saya sudah menonton versi lamanya sebelumnya.
english: The movie is exciting, but I had already watched the old version before.

target: Kami menandatangani kontrak pagi itu; sesudahnya kami berfoto bersama.
english: We signed the contract that morning; after that we took a photo together.

target: Dia minum obat batuk; sesudahnya tenggorokannya terasa lebih enak.
english: He took cough medicine; after that his throat felt better.

target: Sebelumnya saya minta maaf kalau suara saya kurang jelas.
english: First of all, I apologize if my voice is not clear enough.
grammar: Sebelumnya can open politely: Sebelumnya, minta maaf... = First of all, apologies...

target: Ketika saya masih kuliah, saya sering begadang sebelum ujian.
english: When I was still in college, I often stayed up all night before exams.
grammar: Ketika = when, common in writing; in everyday speech people usually say waktu: waktu saya kuliah.

target: Ketika pintu pesawat dibuka, para penumpang langsung berdiri.
english: When the plane door was opened, the passengers immediately stood up.
grammar: Para + people-noun = plural group: para penumpang = the passengers.

target: Waktu lampu mati semalam, kami makan malam dengan lilin.
english: When the lights went out last night, we had dinner by candlelight.

target: Ketika hasil ujian diumumkan, seluruh kelas langsung ramai.
english: When the exam results were announced, the whole class immediately got noisy.

target: Waktu saya kecil, ayah sering membacakan cerita sebelum tidur.
english: When I was small, Dad often read me stories before bed.
grammar: Membacakan = read out for someone: membacakan cerita = read a story aloud (for them).

target: Ketika krisis terjadi, banyak toko kecil terpaksa tutup.
english: When the crisis happened, many small shops were forced to close.

target: Waktu kami sampai di puncak, kabutnya justru makin tebal.
english: When we reached the peak, the fog actually got thicker.

target: Ketika presentasi dimulai, tolong matikan mikrofon kalau tidak sedang bicara.
english: When the presentation starts, please turn off your microphone if you are not speaking.

target: Waktu harga tiket turun, kami langsung membeli dua kursi untuk Desember.
english: When ticket prices dropped, we immediately bought two seats for December.

target: Ketika bayi tidur siang, ibu menyetrika sambil mendengarkan radio.
english: When the baby naps, Mom irons while listening to the radio.

target: Waktu gempa kecil terasa, kami keluar lewat tangga darurat.
english: When the small earthquake was felt, we went out via the emergency stairs.

target: Ketika wawancara kerja, jawab setiap pertanyaan dengan tenang dan jujur.
english: During a job interview, answer every question calmly and honestly.

target: Dia menyapu halaman sambil menunggu cucian di mesin selesai.
english: She sweeps the yard while waiting for the laundry in the machine to finish.
grammar: Sambil = while (same person doing both): menyapu sambil menunggu = sweep while waiting.

target: Saya mencatat pesanan pelanggan sambil menjawab telepon yang terus berbunyi.
english: I write down customers' orders while answering the phone that keeps ringing.

target: Kakak menonton drama Korea sambil melipat pakaian yang baru kering.
english: My older sister watches a Korean drama while folding the freshly dried clothes.
grammar: Baru + adjective = freshly/just became: baru kering = just dried.

target: Kami duduk di teras sambil menikmati pisang goreng buatan nenek.
english: We sit on the terrace while enjoying Grandma's homemade fried bananas.

target: Sopir menunggu di depan hotel sambil mendengarkan berita di radio.
english: The driver waits in front of the hotel while listening to the news on the radio.

target: Sambil menunggu hujan reda, kami minum teh dan main kartu.
english: While waiting for the rain to stop, we drink tea and play cards.

target: Ibu menelepon nenek sambil mengaduk sup di dapur.
english: Mom calls Grandma while stirring the soup in the kitchen.

target: Jangan membalas pesan sambil menyetir; berhenti dulu di tempat aman.
english: Don't reply to messages while driving; stop first in a safe place.

target: Pas saya keluar rumah, hujan turun deras sekali.
english: Right when I left the house, it started raining very hard.
grammar: Pas = colloquial 'right when': pas saya keluar = right as I left. Written form: ketika/waktu.

target: Dia datang pas makanannya baru saja habis.
english: He arrived right when the food had just run out.

target: Pas kami tiba di loket, tiketnya ternyata sudah habis.
english: Right when we got to the ticket counter, it turned out the tickets were sold out.
grammar: Ternyata = it turns out: ternyata sudah habis = turns out they were sold out.

target: Listrik mati pas filmnya sedang seru-serunya.
english: The power went out right when the movie was at its most exciting.
grammar: Sedang + doubled adjective + -nya = at its peak: sedang seru-serunya = at its most exciting.

target: Pas gajian, dia langsung membayar semua tagihannya.
english: Right on payday, he immediately pays all his bills.
grammar: Gajian = payday (from gaji, salary): pas gajian = right when the pay comes in.

target: Telepon saya berbunyi pas rapat baru dimulai.
english: My phone rang right when the meeting had just started.

target: Pas liburan kemarin, harga kamar hotel naik dua kali lipat.
english: Right during the last holidays, hotel room prices doubled.

target: Kami sampai di halte pas busnya berangkat, jadi harus menunggu lagi.
english: We got to the bus stop right as the bus was leaving, so we had to wait again.

target: Setelah menabung dua tahun, mereka akhirnya membeli rumah kecil di pinggir kota.
english: After saving for two years, they finally bought a small house on the edge of town.
grammar: Akhirnya = finally, after effort or waiting: akhirnya selesai juga! = it's finally done!

target: Akhirnya saya menemukan kacamata itu di bawah bantal sofa.
english: I finally found the glasses under the sofa cushion.

target: Setelah macet dua jam, kami akhirnya sampai di rumah nenek.
english: After being stuck in traffic for two hours, we finally arrived at Grandma's house.

target: Dia akhirnya berani mengajukan kenaikan gaji ke atasannya.
english: She finally dared to ask her boss for a raise.
grammar: Mengajukan = put forward/request: mengajukan kenaikan gaji = ask for a raise.

target: Setelah lama ragu, ayah akhirnya menjual motor tuanya.
english: After hesitating for a long time, Dad finally sold his old motorbike.

target: Antrean panjang itu akhirnya bergerak setelah loket kedua dibuka.
english: The long queue finally moved after the second counter was opened.
grammar: Antrean = the queue (antre + -an): antrean panjang = a long line.

target: Akhirnya kami menemukan warung yang masih buka setelah berkeliling hampir sejam.
english: We finally found a food stall that was still open after going around for almost an hour.

target: Setelah tiga kali gagal, dia akhirnya lulus ujian menyetir.
english: After failing three times, he finally passed the driving test.

target: Awalnya saya gugup, tapi akhirnya wawancaranya berjalan lancar.
english: At first I was nervous, but in the end the interview went smoothly.
grammar: Awalnya ... akhirnya frames a story: awalnya susah, akhirnya terbiasa = hard at first, used to it in the end.

target: Awalnya dia menolak, akhirnya dia ikut juga ke acara itu.
english: At first he refused; in the end he came along to the event after all.
grammar: Juga after the verb = after all/finally: ikut juga = ended up joining after all.

target: Awalnya kami tersesat, akhirnya seorang warga mengantar kami sampai jalan besar.
english: At first we got lost; in the end a local resident took us to the main road.

target: Awalnya rasanya aneh, tapi akhirnya saya malah suka makanan pedas.
english: At first it tasted strange, but in the end I actually came to like spicy food.
grammar: Malah = contrary to expectation: saya malah suka = I actually ended up liking it.

target: Awalnya mereka hanya berteman, akhirnya mereka menikah tahun lalu.
english: At first they were just friends; in the end they got married last year.

target: Awalnya proyek ini kecil, akhirnya seluruh tim ikut terlibat.
english: At first this project was small; in the end the whole team got involved.

target: Awalnya cuaca cerah, akhirnya kami pulang cepat karena angin kencang.
english: At first the weather was clear; in the end we went home early because of strong wind.

target: Awalnya adik takut naik sepeda, akhirnya dia bisa berkeliling kompleks sendiri.
english: At first my little brother was afraid to ride a bike; in the end he could ride around the complex alone.

target: Awalnya saya hanya mau melihat-lihat, akhirnya saya membeli dua pasang sepatu.
english: At first I only wanted to browse; in the end I bought two pairs of shoes.
grammar: Melihat-lihat = browse/look around: hanya mau melihat-lihat = just looking.

target: Awalnya hanya gerimis, akhirnya banjir kecil menutup jalan depan sekolah.
english: At first it was only drizzling; in the end a small flood covered the road in front of the school.

target: Dulu saya tinggal di Medan sebelum pindah ke Bogor.
english: I used to live in Medan before moving to Bogor.
grammar: Dulu at the start = used to: Dulu saya tinggal di Medan. = I used to live in Medan.

target: Dulu di sini sawah luas, sekarang sudah jadi perumahan besar.
english: There used to be wide rice fields here; now it has become a big housing estate.
grammar: Dulu ... sekarang contrasts past and present: dulu sepi, sekarang ramai = used to be quiet, now busy.

target: Ayah dulu perokok berat, sekarang dia rajin lari pagi.
english: Dad used to be a heavy smoker; now he diligently jogs in the morning.

target: Dulu kami harus mengantre di bank, sekarang semuanya lewat aplikasi.
english: We used to have to queue at the bank; now everything is via an app.
grammar: Lewat = via/through: lewat aplikasi = through an app.

target: Nenek dulu berjualan kue di pasar dekat stasiun.
english: Grandma used to sell cakes at the market near the station.
grammar: Berjualan = to sell as one's trade: berjualan kue = sell cakes (for a living).

target: Dulu tiket bioskop murah sekali, sekarang harganya naik terus.
english: Movie tickets used to be very cheap; now the price keeps going up.

target: Kakak dulu takut gelap, sekarang dia malah suka mendaki malam-malam.
english: My older brother used to be afraid of the dark; now he actually likes hiking late at night.

target: Dulu kantor kami hanya punya lima karyawan, sekarang sudah ratusan.
english: Our office used to have only five employees; now there are hundreds.

target: Dulu orang menulis surat panjang, sekarang semuanya lewat pesan singkat.
english: People used to write long letters; now everything is via short messages.

target: Dulu kampung ini sepi, sekarang ramai karena ada kampus baru.
english: This village used to be quiet; now it is busy because there is a new campus.

target: Saya dulu benci sayur, sekarang saya makan sayur setiap hari.
english: I used to hate vegetables; now I eat vegetables every day.

target: Dulu anak-anak kampung ini mandi di sungai setiap sore.
english: The children of this village used to bathe in the river every afternoon.

target: Tadi pagi saya bangun kesiangan, jadi saya berangkat tanpa sarapan.
english: This morning I woke up late, so I left without breakfast.
grammar: Kesiangan = too late in the morning: bangun kesiangan = overslept.

target: Kami berangkat subuh, istirahat sebentar di jalan, dan tiba di Bandung sebelum siang.
english: We left at dawn, rested a moment on the way, and arrived in Bandung before midday.

target: Awalnya dia hanya membantu di dapur, lama-lama dia belajar memasak, akhirnya dia membuka warung sendiri.
english: At first she only helped in the kitchen; over time she learned to cook; in the end she opened her own food stall.
grammar: Lama-lama = over time/gradually: lama-lama dia belajar = over time she learned.

target: Sejak pindah ke kota besar, dia jarang berolahraga, akhirnya badannya mudah lelah.
english: Since moving to the big city, he rarely exercises; in the end his body tires easily.

target: Waktu kecil saya sering menginap di rumah paman; sekarang rumah itu sudah dijual.
english: When I was small I often stayed over at my uncle's house; now that house has been sold.

target: Ketika tamu datang, ibu masih memasak, jadi saya yang membuka pintu.
english: When the guests arrived, Mom was still cooking, so it was I who opened the door.
grammar: Yang after the doer = the one who: saya yang membuka pintu = I'm the one who opened the door.

target: Saya menunggu sampai jam lima; sesudahnya saya pulang karena kantor sudah sepi.
english: I waited until five o'clock; after that I went home because the office was already quiet.
grammar: Sampai = until: menunggu sampai jam lima = wait until five.

target: Barusan hujan deras sekali; sekarang matahari muncul seperti tidak terjadi apa-apa.
english: Just now it rained very hard; now the sun has come out as if nothing happened.

target: Dulu kami satu sekolah, lalu dia pindah ke luar kota, dan minggu lalu kami bertemu lagi.
english: We used to be at the same school, then he moved out of town, and last week we met again.

target: Selama perjalanan pulang, anak-anak tidur, jadi suasana di mobil tenang sampai kami tiba.
english: During the trip home, the kids slept, so the mood in the car stayed calm until we arrived.

target: Pas saya mau membayar, saya sadar dompet saya tertinggal di kantor.
english: Right when I was about to pay, I realized my wallet had been left behind at the office.
grammar: Tertinggal = accidentally left behind: dompet saya tertinggal = my wallet got left behind.

target: Sejak sistem baru dipasang, laporan mingguan selesai lebih cepat dan tim jarang lembur.
english: Since the new system was installed, weekly reports get done faster and the team rarely works overtime.

target: Awalnya kami salah naik bus, akhirnya kami turun di terminal dan naik ojek ke hotel.
english: At first we took the wrong bus; in the end we got off at the terminal and took a motorbike taxi to the hotel.
grammar: Salah + verb = do wrongly: salah naik bus = take the wrong bus.

target: Ketika pesawat mendarat, hujan baru saja reda, jadi kami menunggu sebentar di dalam.
english: When the plane landed, the rain had just stopped, so we waited a moment inside.

target: Dulu saya menulis catatan harian setiap malam; sekarang saya menulis hanya kalau ada kejadian penting.
english: I used to write a diary every night; now I write only when something important happens.

target: Malam ini saya ingin makan nasi goreng spesial pakai telur.
english: Tonight I want to eat special fried rice with an egg.
grammar: Pakai adds toppings when ordering: pakai telur = with an egg.

target: Rendang daging di rumah makan Padang itu empuk sekali.
english: The beef rendang at that Padang restaurant is really tender.

target: Tadi kami memesan dua porsi sate kambing di warung sebelah.
english: Earlier we ordered two portions of goat satay at the warung next door.

target: Gado-gado itu sayuran rebus dengan bumbu kacang yang gurih.
english: Gado-gado is boiled vegetables with savory peanut sauce.
grammar: Gurih = savory-rich (coconut milk, broth, fried things) — a core taste word with no exact English match.

target: Bakso di sini kuahnya bening dan baksonya kenyal.
english: The bakso here has clear broth and springy meatballs.
grammar: Kenyal = springy-bouncy — the prized bakso texture; lembek bakso is a failed bakso.

target: Soto ayam biasanya disajikan dengan nasi putih dan kerupuk.
english: Chicken soto is usually served with white rice and crackers.

target: Saya lebih suka soto Lamongan daripada soto Betawi yang pakai santan.
english: I prefer Lamongan soto to Betawi soto, which uses coconut milk.

target: Warung nasi campur dekat pasar itu selalu ramai waktu jam makan siang.
english: That mixed-rice warung near the market is always busy at lunchtime.

target: Ayam bakarnya manis karena diolesi kecap sebelum dibakar.
english: The grilled chicken is sweet because it is brushed with kecap before grilling.
grammar: Kecap = soy sauce (kecap manis = sweet), not ketchup — English borrowed the word from Malay.

target: Kalau ke Yogyakarta, kamu harus mencoba gudeg yang manis itu.
english: If you go to Yogyakarta, you have to try that sweet gudeg.

target: Mie ayam di depan sekolah itu murah dan porsinya besar.
english: The chicken noodles in front of that school are cheap and the portions are big.

target: Saya pesan sate ayam sepuluh tusuk, bumbu kacangnya dipisah, ya.
english: I'll have ten skewers of chicken satay, with the peanut sauce separate, please.
grammar: Sate is counted in tusuk (skewers): sepuluh tusuk = ten skewers.

target: Nasi gorengnya pakai ayam atau udang, Kak?
english: Does the fried rice come with chicken or shrimp, miss?

target: Gulai kambing di sini kuahnya kental dan bumbunya terasa kuat.
english: The goat gulai here has thick broth and the spices really come through.

target: Pecel lele biasanya dijual di tenda kaki lima waktu malam.
english: Pecel lele — fried catfish with sambal — is usually sold at roadside tents at night.
grammar: Kaki lima = street vendors, named after the five-foot walkway (kaki lima) they occupy.

target: Setiap pagi ibu membeli lontong sayur dari penjual keliling.
english: Every morning Mom buys lontong sayur from a roving vendor.

target: Nasi uduk dengan telur balado cocok sekali untuk sarapan.
english: Nasi uduk with balado egg is just right for breakfast.

target: Saya belum pernah mencoba rawon, sup daging dengan kuah hitam itu.
english: I have never tried rawon, that beef soup with black broth.

target: Es cendol paling enak diminum siang hari waktu panas.
english: Iced cendol is most delicious drunk at midday when it is hot.

target: Martabak manis dengan keju dan cokelat itu makanan favorit anak saya.
english: Sweet martabak with cheese and chocolate is my child's favorite food.

target: Sambal di warung itu pedasnya bukan main.
english: The sambal at that warung is unbelievably spicy.
grammar: Bukan main = 'no joke', unbelievably: pedasnya bukan main = it is seriously spicy.

target: Kuah sotonya gurih karena pakai kaldu ayam asli.
english: The soto broth is savory because it uses real chicken stock.

target: Ikan asin goreng cocok dimakan dengan nasi hangat dan sambal.
english: Fried salted fish goes well with warm rice and sambal.

target: Kopi tanpa gula terasa pahit, tapi saya sudah terbiasa.
english: Coffee without sugar tastes bitter, but I am already used to it.
grammar: Ter- + biasa = terbiasa (used to it): sudah terbiasa = already used to it.

target: Sayur pare memang pahit, tapi banyak orang menyukainya.
english: Bitter gourd really is bitter, but many people like it.

target: Mangga muda rasanya asam, jadi biasanya dimakan dengan bumbu rujak.
english: Young mango tastes sour, so it is usually eaten with rujak seasoning.

target: Sup buatan saya kemarin hambar karena kurang garam.
english: The soup I made yesterday was bland because it lacked salt.
grammar: Hambar = bland. The fix is garam (salt): kurang garam = not enough salt.

target: Menurut ayah, tehnya kurang manis, jadi dia menambah gula.
english: According to Dad, the tea is not sweet enough, so he adds more sugar.

target: Rasa asam dari jeruk nipis membuat soto ini lebih segar.
english: The sour taste from the lime makes this soto fresher.

target: Masakan Padang terkenal gurih karena banyak memakai santan kental.
english: Padang cooking is famously savory because it uses a lot of thick coconut milk.

target: Keripik singkong ini asin dan renyah, cocok untuk teman minum teh.
english: These cassava chips are salty and crunchy, perfect to go with tea.

target: Jangan merebus sayur terlalu lama supaya tidak lembek.
english: Don't boil the vegetables too long so they don't go mushy.

target: Tahu goreng ini garing di luar dan lembut di dalam.
english: This fried tofu is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
grammar: Garing and renyah both mean crispy: garing for fried-dry crunch, renyah for fresh crunch.

target: Dagingnya direbus dulu berjam-jam sampai benar-benar empuk.
english: The meat is boiled for hours first until it is really tender.
grammar: Empuk = tender, soft to the bite: dagingnya empuk = the meat is tender.

target: Kerupuk cepat melempem kalau tidak disimpan di toples tertutup.
english: Crackers quickly go soggy if they are not kept in a closed jar.

target: Sate yang dibakar terlalu lama jadi alot dan kering.
english: Satay that is grilled too long turns tough and dry.
grammar: Alot = tough, chewy meat — the word for overcooked satay or cheap beef.

target: Telur setengah matang enak dimakan dengan roti bakar.
english: Soft-boiled eggs are tasty eaten with toast.
grammar: Setengah matang = half-cooked: soft-boiled eggs, rare steak. Matang = cooked/ripe.

target: Pisang gorengnya masih panas, renyah sekali di luar.
english: The fried bananas are still hot, really crispy on the outside.

target: Nasinya sudah matang, ayo kita makan sekarang.
english: The rice is done — come on, let's eat now.

target: Di rumah kami, ikan lebih sering dikukus daripada digoreng.
english: At our house, fish is steamed more often than fried.
grammar: Cooking talk loves di- passives: dikukus = steamed, digoreng = fried, direbus = boiled.

target: Dapur langsung wangi waktu ibu menumis bumbu halus.
english: The kitchen instantly smells fragrant when Mom sautés the spice paste.

target: Ayah lebih suka ikan bakar, sedangkan saya suka ikan goreng.
english: Dad prefers grilled fish, while I like fried fish.
grammar: Sedangkan contrasts two subjects: ayah suka A, sedangkan saya suka B = Dad likes A, while I like B.

target: Sisa rendang semalam dipanaskan lagi untuk makan siang hari ini.
english: Last night's leftover rendang is reheated for lunch today.

target: Tempe goreng buatan ibu selalu habis duluan di meja makan.
english: Mom's fried tempeh is always the first thing gone from the dinner table.

target: Sayur asem buatan nenek rasanya segar dan sedikit asam.
english: Grandma's sayur asem tastes fresh and slightly sour.

target: Ibu selalu mencicipi masakannya dulu sebelum disajikan ke meja.
english: Mom always tastes her cooking first before it is served at the table.

target: Kalau masak untuk banyak orang, bumbunya harus ditambah sedikit demi sedikit.
english: When cooking for many people, the seasoning has to be added little by little.
grammar: Sedikit demi sedikit = little by little; demi repeats units: satu demi satu = one by one.

target: Ayam kampung memang lebih mahal, tapi rasanya lebih gurih.
english: Free-range chicken really is more expensive, but it tastes richer.
grammar: Ayam kampung (lit. village chicken) = free-range chicken — pricier and tastier than broiler.

target: Nasi sisa kemarin digoreng dengan bawang putih dan kecap.
english: Yesterday's leftover rice is fried with garlic and kecap.

target: Ikan kecil ini digoreng kering supaya durinya ikut renyah.
english: These small fish are fried until dry so even the bones turn crispy.

target: Sebelum dibakar, ayamnya diungkep dulu supaya bumbunya meresap.
english: Before being grilled, the chicken is simmered in spices first so the seasoning soaks in.
grammar: Diungkep = simmered in the spice paste before frying/grilling — the step direbus doesn't capture.

target: Lontong dibuat dari beras yang dimasak di dalam daun pisang.
english: Lontong is made from rice cooked inside a banana leaf.
grammar: Beras = uncooked rice, nasi = cooked rice on the plate — lontong starts from beras.

target: Kata ibu, sup bening cocok untuk anak yang sedang sakit.
english: Mom says clear soup is right for a child who is sick.

target: Kami jarang menggoreng di rumah karena dapur jadi penuh asap.
english: We rarely deep-fry at home because the kitchen gets full of smoke.

target: Akhir pekan depan kami mau membakar ikan di halaman belakang.
english: Next weekend we want to grill fish in the backyard.
grammar: Grilling is bakar, never masak: membakar ikan = to grill fish. Masak = cooking in general.

target: Mas, nasi gorengnya pedasnya level berapa, ya?
english: Excuse me, what spice level is the fried rice?
grammar: -nya makes a quality the topic: pedasnya level berapa? = how spicy is it (its spiciness, what level)?

target: Saya minta level dua saja, saya tidak kuat pedas.
english: I'll take level two please — I can't handle spice.
grammar: Tidak kuat + noun = can't handle it: saya tidak kuat pedas = I can't take spice.

target: Teman saya kuat makan pedas, level lima pun masih kurang.
english: My friend can handle spicy food — even level five is not enough.
grammar: Pun after a word = even: level lima pun masih kurang = even level five is not enough.

target: Kalau tidak tahan pedas, jangan pesan ayam geprek di sini.
english: If you can't stand spice, don't order the ayam geprek here.

target: Sambalnya boleh dipisah supaya anak-anak juga bisa makan?
english: Can the sambal be separate so the kids can eat too?

target: Pedasnya baru terasa setelah suapan ketiga.
english: The heat only hits after the third bite.

target: Mukanya langsung merah karena sambal hijau Padang itu pedas sekali.
english: His face immediately turns red because that Padang green sambal is really spicy.

target: Minum es teh manis membantu kalau kamu kepedasan.
english: Drinking sweet iced tea helps when the spiciness is too much for you.
grammar: Ke-...-an = overcome by: kepedasan = too spicy to handle, kepanasan = overheated.

target: Orang sini biasa makan sambal sejak kecil, jadi lidahnya kuat.
english: People here are used to eating sambal from childhood, so their tongues are tough.

target: Makan di sini atau dibungkus, Kak?
english: For here or to go, miss?
grammar: The warung question: makan di sini atau dibungkus? = for here or to go? Bungkus = wrap up, take away.

target: Bungkus dua nasi campur, ya, sambalnya jangan lupa.
english: Two mixed rice to go, please — don't forget the sambal.

target: Di warung Tegal, kamu tinggal tunjuk lauk yang kamu mau.
english: At a Tegal warung, you just point at the side dishes you want.
grammar: Warteg (warung Tegal) = cheap point-and-choose rice stalls named after the town of Tegal.

target: Air putih di warung biasanya gratis, tinggal minta saja.
english: Plain water at a warung is usually free — you just have to ask.

target: Pembeli boleh mengambil sendiri kerupuk dari toples di meja.
english: Customers may take crackers themselves from the jars on the table.

target: Bayarnya nanti saja di kasir setelah selesai makan.
english: You pay later at the register, after you finish eating.
grammar: Warung habit: eat first, pay after — bayarnya nanti saja = just pay later.

target: Warung ini ramai terus karena masakannya seperti masakan rumah.
english: This warung is always busy because its food is like home cooking.

target: Sarapan bubur ayam di gerobak depan gang sudah jadi kebiasaan saya.
english: Chicken porridge at the cart in front of the alley has become my breakfast habit.

target: Tukang sate lewat depan rumah hampir setiap malam.
english: The satay seller passes in front of the house almost every night.
grammar: Tukang + food = the seller: tukang sate = satay man, tukang bakso pushes his cart around.

target: Kalau kamu mendengar suara ketukan kayu, itu tanda tukang bakso lewat.
english: If you hear the sound of wood knocking, that is a sign the bakso seller is passing.

target: Gorengan hangat paling laku waktu sore hujan seperti ini.
english: Warm fried snacks sell best on a rainy afternoon like this.
grammar: Gorengan = the family of street fried snacks: tempe, tahu, bakwan, pisang goreng.

target: Nasinya dicampur atau dipisah, Pak?
english: Would you like the rice mixed in or separate, sir?
grammar: Soto question at the counter: dicampur (rice in the bowl) atau dipisah (rice on the side)?

target: Waktu hujan begini, paling enak makan bakso yang kuahnya panas.
english: In rain like this, nothing beats bakso with hot broth.

target: Untuk minumnya, saya pesan es jeruk tanpa gula.
english: For the drink, I'll order iced orange juice without sugar.

target: Boleh minta sendok dan garpu lagi? Sendok saya jatuh.
english: May I have another spoon and fork? My spoon fell.

target: Pesanan kami kurang satu, sate kambingnya belum datang.
english: Our order is one short — the goat satay has not arrived yet.

target: Maaf, saya tidak makan daging sapi, ada menu ayam atau ikan?
english: Sorry, I don't eat beef — is there a chicken or fish dish?

target: Masakan ini pakai kacang tidak? Anak saya alergi kacang.
english: Does this dish use peanuts? My child is allergic to peanuts.

target: Saya vegetarian, jadi saya pesan gado-gado tanpa telur.
english: I'm vegetarian, so I'll order gado-gado without egg.

target: Tolong nasinya setengah porsi saja, saya tidak terlalu lapar.
english: Just half a portion of rice, please — I'm not very hungry.

target: Rendangnya tinggal dua potong, mau saya ambilkan dua-duanya?
english: There are only two pieces of rendang left — shall I get you both?
grammar: -kan can mean doing it for someone: ambilkan = fetch (for you).

target: Kalau sotonya kurang asin, tambahkan garam sendiri di meja.
english: If the soto is not salty enough, add salt yourself at the table.

target: Menu hari ini ayam goreng lengkuas dan sayur lodeh.
english: Today's menu is galangal fried chicken and lodeh vegetable stew.

target: Soto ayamnya ditambah perasan jeruk nipis supaya lebih segar.
english: The chicken soto gets a squeeze of lime added so it is fresher.

target: Jangan lupa aduk kopinya dulu, gulanya masih di bawah.
english: Don't forget to stir the coffee first — the sugar is still at the bottom.

target: Bakwan jagung paling enak dimakan selagi masih panas.
english: Corn fritters are most delicious eaten while they are still hot.
grammar: Selagi = while it lasts: selagi masih panas = while it is still hot.

target: Anak saya baru mau makan sayur kalau dicampur ke nasi goreng.
english: My child will only eat vegetables if they are mixed into fried rice.
grammar: Baru here = only then: baru mau makan = will only eat (once the condition is met).

target: Suami saya yang masak setiap akhir pekan, saya bagian cuci piring.
english: My husband is the one who cooks every weekend; I'm on dish duty.
grammar: Saya bagian X = X is my department: saya bagian cuci piring = I handle the dishes.

target: Kami menanam cabai di pot supaya tidak perlu sering membeli.
english: We grow chilies in pots so we don't have to buy them often.

target: Resep soto ini turun-temurun dari nenek buyut kami.
english: This soto recipe has been handed down from our great-grandmother.
grammar: Turun-temurun = handed down through the generations (turun = to descend).

target: Bau rendang dari dapur membuat semua orang cepat lapar.
english: The smell of rendang from the kitchen makes everyone hungry fast.

target: Kalau malas masak, kami tinggal pesan makanan lewat aplikasi.
english: When we don't feel like cooking, we just order food through an app.
grammar: Tinggal + verb = all that's left to do: tinggal pesan = just order.

target: Ibu memisahkan porsi adik dulu sebelum sambalnya dicampur.
english: Mom sets aside my little brother's portion first before the sambal is mixed in.

target: Kulkas kami penuh sisa makanan dari acara keluarga kemarin.
english: Our fridge is full of leftovers from yesterday's family gathering.

target: Setiap Lebaran, dapur rumah nenek penuh dengan panci besar.
english: Every Eid, Grandma's kitchen is full of big pots.

target: Ketupat dan opor ayam hampir selalu ada waktu Lebaran.
english: Ketupat and chicken opor are almost always around at Eid.

target: Totalnya berapa, Bu? Sekalian sama es tehnya.
english: How much is the total, ma'am? Together with the iced tea.
grammar: Sekalian = while we're at it, all together: sekalian sama es tehnya = including the iced tea.

target: Kita bagi dua saja, ya, biar gampang.
english: Let's just split it in two, okay, to keep things easy.
grammar: Biar = casual supaya (so that): biar gampang = so it's easy.

target: Kali ini saya yang bayar, kamu sudah traktir minggu lalu.
english: This time I'm paying — you already treated last week.
grammar: Traktir = treat someone (pay for them): aku traktir, ya = my treat.

target: Jangan rebutan bayar, lebih baik kita bagi rata saja.
english: Don't fight over paying — better we just split it evenly.
grammar: Bagi rata = split evenly (rata = flat, even): kita bagi rata = we split it equally.

target: Makanannya kita bayar masing-masing, minumnya biar saya.
english: We each pay for our own food; leave the drinks to me.

target: Uangnya kurang lima ribu, nanti saya ganti setelah ke ATM.
english: I'm five thousand short — I'll pay you back after going to the ATM.

target: Saya sudah jadi langganan warung itu sejak pindah ke sini.
english: I've been a regular at that warung since moving here.

target: Minta bonnya dipisah, ya, soalnya ini pakai uang kantor.
english: Please split the bill — this one is on office money.

target: Kemarin kami patungan untuk makan malam perpisahan tim.
english: Yesterday we chipped in together for the team's farewell dinner.
grammar: Patungan = pool money / chip in — the everyday word: patungan, yuk! = let's split it!

target: Siapa yang belum bayar? Masih kurang dua puluh ribu.
english: Who has not paid yet? We're still twenty thousand short.

target: Porsi bungkus nasi Padang biasanya lebih banyak daripada makan di tempat.
english: A takeaway portion of nasi Padang is usually bigger than eating in.
grammar: Porsi bungkus = takeaway portion; Padang stalls famously give extra rice when you bungkus.

target: Sate kambingnya masih setengah matang, tolong dibakar sebentar lagi.
english: The goat satay is still half-cooked — please grill it a little longer.

target: Kuah bakso di warung itu gurihnya beda dari yang lain.
english: The bakso broth at that warung has a savoriness unlike the others.

target: Di pasar malam kemarin, kami mencoba kerak telor untuk pertama kali.
english: At the night market yesterday, we tried kerak telor for the first time.

target: Sehabis berenang, paling enak minum es kelapa muda di pinggir pantai.
english: After swimming, nothing beats drinking iced young coconut by the beach.

target: Ayam gorengnya masih panas, hati-hati waktu menggigitnya.
english: The fried chicken is still hot — careful when biting into it.

target: Saya kurang suka petai, tapi suami saya doyan sekali.
english: I don't much like stink beans, but my husband loves them.
grammar: Doyan = really into a food (casual): doyan pedas = loves spicy food.

target: Durian itu baunya kuat, ada yang suka, ada yang tidak tahan.
english: Durian has a strong smell — some people love it, some can't stand it.
grammar: Ada yang ... ada yang ... = some ... others ...: ada yang suka, ada yang tidak = some do, some don't.

target: Teh di sini otomatis manis, kalau mau tanpa gula, minta teh tawar.
english: Tea here is automatically sweet — if you want it sugarless, ask for teh tawar.
grammar: Tawar = plain, unsweetened (and also 'to bargain'): teh tawar = unsweetened tea.

target: Setiap daerah di Indonesia punya soto dengan rasa yang berbeda.
english: Every region in Indonesia has soto with a different flavor.

target: Bumbu kacang gado-gado di sini diulek langsung di depan pembeli.
english: The gado-gado peanut sauce here is ground fresh right in front of the customer.
grammar: Diulek = ground on a stone mortar (ulekan) — what gives sambal its rough texture.

target: Perut saya sudah kenyang, tapi es campur ini menggoda sekali.
english: My stomach is already full, but this es campur is so tempting.

target: Setelah makan pedas, jangan langsung minum air dingin banyak-banyak.
english: After eating spicy food, don't immediately drink lots of cold water.

target: Oleh-oleh paling aman dibawa pulang itu keripik dan sambal botol.
english: The safest souvenirs to bring home are chips and bottled sambal.

target: Kalau kamu ke Solo, jangan lupa mencoba nasi liwet di sana.
english: If you go to Solo, don't forget to try nasi liwet there.

target: Bangun tidur, dia langsung mengecek HP-nya.
english: As soon as he wakes up, he immediately checks his phone.
grammar: HP (say ha-pe) is the everyday word for phone; ponsel sounds formal. Mengecek HP = check the phone.

target: Jangan main HP terus waktu makan malam bersama keluarga.
english: Don't be on your phone the whole time during dinner with the family.

target: Saya lupa menaruh HP di mana, tolong telepon nomor saya.
english: I forgot where I put my phone, please call my number.

target: Sebelum rapat mulai, matikan dulu suara HP kalian.
english: Before the meeting starts, turn off your phones' sound first.

target: Setiap malam dia memasang alarm di HP sebelum tidur.
english: Every night she sets the alarm on her phone before sleeping.
grammar: Setting an alarm is pasang (or setel): pasang alarm jam lima = set a 5 a.m. alarm.

target: Layar HP saya retak karena jatuh dari meja.
english: My phone screen is cracked because it fell off the table.

target: Anak-anak sekarang lebih suka main HP daripada main di luar.
english: Kids these days prefer playing on their phones to playing outside.

target: HP baru itu kameranya bagus untuk foto keluarga.
english: That new phone's camera is good for family photos.

target: Waktu rapat penting, HP saya selalu dalam mode getar.
english: During important meetings, my phone is always on vibrate mode.

target: Dia mengganti nada dering HP-nya dengan lagu daerah.
english: He changed his phone's ringtone to a regional song.
grammar: Nada dering = ringtone, literally 'ring tone': mengganti nada dering = change the ringtone.

target: Mata saya sakit karena terlalu lama melihat layar HP.
english: My eyes hurt from looking at the phone screen for too long.

target: Ayah baru bisa memakai HP layar sentuh tahun lalu.
english: Dad only learned to use a touchscreen phone last year.

target: HP saya sudah lama, jadi sering lambat sekali.
english: My phone is old, so it's often very slow.
grammar: Colloquially a slow phone or connection is lemot: HP saya lemot = my phone is laggy.

target: Simpan nomor penting di HP dan juga di buku kecil.
english: Save important numbers on your phone and also in a small notebook.

target: Dia menjatuhkan HP-nya ke dalam air waktu mencuci baju.
english: She dropped her phone into the water while washing clothes.

target: Mbak, boleh minta password wifi-nya, ya?
english: Miss, could I have the wifi password, please?
grammar: The standard cafe question: minta password wifi-nya = may I have the wifi password.

target: Password wifi di kafe ini panjang sekali.
english: The wifi password at this cafe is really long.

target: Wifi di rumah mati sejak tadi pagi.
english: The wifi at home has been down since this morning.

target: Sinyal wifi di kamar belakang lemah, jadi saya pindah ke ruang tamu.
english: The wifi signal in the back room is weak, so I moved to the living room.

target: Hotel ini wifi-nya cepat, cocok untuk kerja dari kamar.
english: This hotel's wifi is fast, good for working from the room.

target: Coba matikan router sebentar, lalu nyalakan lagi.
english: Try turning off the router for a moment, then turn it on again.

target: Internet di kantor putus, jadi kami menunda rapat online sebentar.
english: The internet at the office is down, so we postponed the online meeting for a while.

target: Banyak orang datang ke kafe ini karena wifi-nya gratis.
english: Many people come to this cafe because the wifi is free.

target: Kalau wifi lambat, saya memakai data HP saja.
english: When the wifi is slow, I just use my phone data.

target: Adik saya marah karena password wifi diganti tanpa bilang-bilang.
english: My little brother is angry because the wifi password was changed without a word to anyone.

target: Tolong sambungkan laptop saya ke wifi ruang rapat.
english: Please connect my laptop to the meeting room wifi.

target: Wifi gratis di stasiun kadang tidak bisa dipakai.
english: The free wifi at the station sometimes can't be used.

target: Baterainya habis, saya harus ngecas HP dulu.
english: The battery is dead, I have to charge my phone first.
grammar: Ngecas (root cas) = to charge; colloquial but universal — all ages say ngecas HP.

target: Jangan lupa bawa charger kalau menginap di rumah nenek.
english: Don't forget to bring your charger when you stay over at grandma's house.

target: Boleh saya numpang ngecas HP di sini sebentar?
english: May I charge my phone here for a moment?
grammar: Numpang = politely use someone's facility: numpang ngecas = charge here, if I may.

target: HP saya dicas semalaman, tapi baterainya tetap cepat habis.
english: My phone was charged all night, but the battery still drains fast.
grammar: Di- + cas = passive: dicas semalaman = charged overnight. Semalaman = all night long.

target: Baterai HP ini awet, bisa dipakai seharian penuh.
english: This phone's battery lasts long; it can be used for a whole day.
grammar: Awet = long-lasting: baterainya awet = the battery lasts. Also used for food and clothes.

target: Saya selalu membawa powerbank kalau bepergian jauh.
english: I always bring a power bank when traveling far.
grammar: Powerbank is used as-is; bepergian = to travel, from pergi (to go).

target: Charger saya ketinggalan di kantor, jadi saya meminjam punya adik.
english: My charger got left behind at the office, so I borrowed my little sister's.

target: Kabel charger ini sudah rusak, saya harus membeli yang baru.
english: This charger cable is already broken; I have to buy a new one.

target: Baterai HP saya tinggal sepuluh persen, sebentar lagi mati.
english: My phone battery is down to ten percent; it will die soon.
grammar: Tinggal = remaining: tinggal sepuluh persen = only ten percent left.

target: Di bandara ada tempat ngecas HP dekat pintu keberangkatan.
english: At the airport there is a phone-charging spot near the departure gate.

target: Jangan main game sambil ngecas, nanti HP kamu cepat panas.
english: Don't play games while charging; your phone will heat up quickly.

target: Dia lupa mencabut charger dari colokan tadi pagi.
english: He forgot to unplug the charger from the outlet this morning.

target: Ibu selalu ngecas HP-nya di dapur setiap malam.
english: Mom always charges her phone in the kitchen every night.

target: Tablet adik mati karena baterainya habis, jadi dia menangis.
english: My little brother's tablet died because the battery ran out, so he cried.

target: Kalau baterai hampir habis, HP saya menjadi sangat lambat.
english: When the battery is almost empty, my phone becomes very slow.

target: Saya baru mengunduh aplikasi untuk belajar bahasa Indonesia.
english: I just downloaded an app for learning Indonesian.
grammar: Mengunduh = download; in speech people also just say download: download aplikasinya.

target: Aplikasi bank saya minta update sebelum bisa dibuka.
english: My banking app is asking for an update before it can be opened.

target: Memori HP penuh, jadi saya menghapus beberapa aplikasi lama.
english: The phone storage is full, so I deleted some old apps.

target: Tolong pasang aplikasi peta ini sebelum kita berangkat.
english: Please install this map app before we leave.

target: Aplikasi ini gratis, tapi banyak iklan yang mengganggu.
english: This app is free, but there are a lot of annoying ads.

target: Nenek belajar memakai aplikasi chat supaya bisa membalas cucunya.
english: Grandma is learning to use a chat app so she can reply to her grandchildren.
grammar: Chat is used as-is: aplikasi chat, chat saya belum dibalas = my message hasn't been replied to.

target: Saya memesan makan siang lewat aplikasi karena hujan deras.
english: I ordered lunch through an app because it was raining hard.

target: Semua tiket kereta kami beli lewat aplikasi di HP.
english: We bought all the train tickets through an app on the phone.

target: Aplikasi belanja itu sering memberi diskon besar.
english: That shopping app often gives big discounts.
grammar: Diskon is the everyday word; potongan harga is what the poster says.

target: Kakak memakai aplikasi untuk mencatat pengeluaran setiap bulan.
english: My older sister uses an app to record her expenses every month.
grammar: Pengeluaran = expenses/spending, from keluar (go out) — money going out.

target: Jangan mengunduh aplikasi dari luar toko aplikasi resmi, itu berbahaya.
english: Don't download apps from outside the official app store; that's dangerous.

target: Aplikasi ojek online ini bisa dipakai untuk mengirim barang.
english: This motorbike-taxi app can be used to send goods.

target: Setelah update, tampilan aplikasinya berubah total.
english: After the update, the app's interface changed completely.
grammar: Tampilan = the look/display: tampilannya berubah = the interface changed.

target: Saya mengatur bahasa aplikasi ini menjadi bahasa Indonesia.
english: I set this app's language to Indonesian.

target: Anak saya mengunduh game baru tanpa izin kemarin.
english: My kid downloaded a new game without permission yesterday.

target: Aplikasi kamera ini bisa membuat foto lama kelihatan baru.
english: This camera app can make old photos look new.

target: Kantor kami memakai aplikasi khusus untuk absen setiap pagi.
english: Our office uses a special app for clocking in every morning.
grammar: Absen in Indonesia = to mark attendance (clock in), not to be absent.

target: Saya memesan ojek online supaya tidak terlambat ke stasiun.
english: I ordered an online motorbike taxi so I would not be late to the station.

target: Naik ojol lebih cepat daripada naik mobil kalau jalanan macet.
english: Taking an ojol is faster than going by car when the roads are jammed.
grammar: Ojol = short for ojek online, the app-booked motorbike taxi everyone uses.

target: Drivernya sudah dekat, tolong tunggu di depan pintu.
english: The driver is close by; please wait in front of the door.
grammar: In ride-hailing the rider is just driver: drivernya sudah dekat = the driver is nearby.

target: Menurut aplikasi, drivernya masih lima menit lagi dari sini.
english: According to the app, the driver is still five minutes away from here.

target: Ongkos ojek online biasanya naik kalau hujan turun.
english: Online motorbike-taxi fares usually go up when it rains.

target: Jangan lupa memberi bintang lima kalau drivernya ramah.
english: Don't forget to give five stars if the driver is friendly.
grammar: Beri bintang lima = give five stars — the app rating; drivers really depend on it.

target: Saya salah menulis alamat, jadi drivernya menunggu di tempat lain.
english: I wrote the address wrong, so the driver waited at a different place.

target: Kirim lokasi kamu lewat aplikasi supaya drivernya tidak bingung.
english: Send your location through the app so the driver does not get confused.
grammar: Kirim lokasi (or share lokasi) = share your location — standard in chat and ride apps.

target: Menurut peta di HP, kita belok kiri di lampu merah kedua.
english: According to the map on the phone, we turn left at the second traffic light.

target: Tanpa aplikasi peta, saya pasti tersesat di kota sebesar ini.
english: Without a map app, I would definitely get lost in a city this big.
grammar: Ter- for accidents: tersesat = to get lost (not on purpose), from sesat.

target: Aplikasi peta bilang jalannya macet, lebih baik lewat jalan kecil.
english: The map app says the road is jammed; better to take the small streets.

target: Kami memesan dua ojol supaya sampai lebih cepat ke acara keluarga.
english: We booked two ojol so we would get to the family event faster.

target: Bapak itu bekerja sebagai driver ojek online sejak tahun lalu.
english: That man has been working as an online motorbike-taxi driver since last year.

target: Di aplikasi ada promo makanan setiap hari Jumat.
english: There is a food promo in the app every Friday.

target: Titik jemputnya di depan minimarket sebelah kantor pos.
english: The pickup point is in front of the minimart next to the post office.
grammar: Titik jemput = pickup point in ride apps; jemput = to pick someone up.

target: Saya membatalkan pesanan ojol karena drivernya tidak bergerak dari tadi.
english: I canceled the ojol order because the driver had not moved for a while.

target: Pesan lewat aplikasi saja, antre di loket panjang sekali.
english: Just order through the app; the line at the counter is really long.

target: Peta di HP saya salah, untung ada orang yang menunjukkan jalan.
english: The map on my phone was wrong; luckily someone showed me the way.

target: Setiap akhir pekan kami video call dengan nenek di kampung.
english: Every weekend we video-call grandma in the village.
grammar: Video call is used as-is, noun or verb: video call dengan nenek = video-call grandma.

target: Waktu video call, sinyal di rumah nenek sering putus-putus.
english: During video calls, the signal at grandma's house often keeps cutting out.
grammar: Putus-putus = keeps cutting out; putus alone = cut off, disconnected.

target: Anak-anak suka menunjukkan mainan baru mereka lewat video call.
english: The kids like showing their new toys over video call.

target: Ibu selalu menangis sedikit setiap video call dengan kakak di luar negeri.
english: Mom always cries a little every video call with my older brother abroad.

target: Kami video call dengan tim Jakarta setiap Senin pagi.
english: We video-call the Jakarta team every Monday morning.
grammar: Video call is its own verb — no melakukan needed: kami video call setiap Senin.

target: Suara kamu putus-putus, coba matikan dulu kameranya.
english: Your voice keeps cutting out; try turning off your camera first.

target: Kakek belum tahu cara menerima video call dari cucunya.
english: Grandpa does not know yet how to answer a video call from his grandchildren.

target: Sebelum video call kerja, saya selalu merapikan meja dulu.
english: Before a work video call, I always tidy my desk first.

target: Video call keluarga besar kemarin ramai sekali, semua bicara bersama.
english: Yesterday's extended-family video call was really lively; everyone talked at once.

target: Kalau rindu rumah, saya langsung video call ibu di dapur.
english: When I miss home, I immediately video-call Mom in the kitchen.

target: Layar HP terlalu kecil, jadi kami memakai laptop untuk video call bersama.
english: The phone screen is too small, so we use the laptop to video-call together.

target: Dia lupa mematikan mikrofon waktu rapat online tadi pagi.
english: He forgot to turn off his microphone during the online meeting this morning.
grammar: Mematikan = turn off, menyalakan = turn on — from mati (dead) and nyala (lit).

target: Memori HP saya penuh karena terlalu banyak foto dan video.
english: My phone storage is full because of too many photos and videos.
grammar: Memori penuh = storage full — the standard phone complaint; memori = phone storage.

target: Saya menghapus video lama supaya ada tempat untuk foto baru.
english: I deleted old videos so there is room for new photos.

target: Foto-foto liburan kami tersimpan di HP dan juga di laptop.
english: Our vacation photos are stored on the phone and also on the laptop.
grammar: Ter- + simpan = stative: tersimpan = (safely) stored, with no one doing the storing.

target: Jangan hapus foto itu, itu satu-satunya foto kakek waktu muda.
english: Don't delete that photo; it's the only photo of grandpa when he was young.

target: Video ulang tahun anak saya terlalu besar untuk dikirim.
english: My child's birthday video is too big to send.

target: HP-nya sering mati sendiri karena memorinya hampir penuh.
english: The phone often shuts off by itself because its storage is almost full.

target: Saya memindahkan semua foto lama ke laptop di rumah.
english: I moved all the old photos to the laptop at home.

target: Setelah memorinya dibersihkan, HP saya menjadi cepat lagi.
english: After its storage was cleaned out, my phone became fast again.

target: Grup keluarga kami penuh ucapan selamat setiap ada yang ulang tahun.
english: Our family group chat is full of congratulations whenever someone has a birthday.

target: Saya mematikan notifikasi grup kantor setiap akhir pekan.
english: I turn off the office group notifications every weekend.
grammar: To mute a chat: matikan notifikasi grupnya = turn off the group's notifications.

target: Pesan di grup RT pagi ini penting, tolong dibaca.
english: The message in the neighborhood group this morning is important; please read it.
grammar: RT (rukun tetangga) = your neighborhood block; nearly every RT has its own grup.

target: Om dan tante paling rajin mengirim gambar selamat pagi di grup.
english: Uncles and aunts are the most diligent at sending good-morning images in the group.
grammar: Gambar selamat pagi — the flowery good-morning images older relatives send daily.

target: Jangan membahas politik di grup keluarga, nanti semua bertengkar.
english: Don't discuss politics in the family group, or everyone will end up fighting.

target: Ada dua ratus pesan baru di grup kantor setelah saya rapat dua jam.
english: There were two hundred new messages in the office group after my two-hour meeting.

target: Dia keluar dari grup itu karena terlalu banyak pesan tidak penting.
english: She left that group because there were too many unimportant messages.

target: Berita di grup itu belum tentu benar, cek dulu sebelum percaya.
english: News in that group is not necessarily true; check first before believing it.
grammar: Belum tentu = not necessarily: belum tentu benar = not necessarily true.

target: Tante saya sering percaya hoaks yang dikirim ke grup keluarga.
english: My aunt often believes the hoaxes sent to the family group.
grammar: Hoaks = hoax/fake news — an everyday Indonesian word for group-chat misinformation.

target: Tolong balas di grup supaya semua orang tahu jadwalnya.
english: Please reply in the group so everyone knows the schedule.

target: Stiker lucu itu dikirim adik saya ke semua grup.
english: That funny sticker was sent by my little sister to all the groups.
grammar: Passive di- + agent, no 'oleh' needed: dikirim adik saya = sent by my little sister.

target: Kami membuat grup baru khusus untuk acara pernikahan kakak.
english: We made a new group just for my older sister's wedding.

target: Jangan kirim foto itu ke grup besar, kirim ke saya saja.
english: Don't send that photo to the big group; just send it to me.

target: Pengumuman rapat besok sudah dikirim di grup kantor sore tadi.
english: The announcement for tomorrow's meeting was sent in the office group this afternoon.

target: Kirim foto KTP kamu lewat pesan, nanti saya daftarkan.
english: Send a photo of your ID card by message, and I'll register you.
grammar: KTP = the Indonesian ID card; kirim foto KTP is a routine request.

target: Foto yang kamu kirim semalam tidak bisa dibuka di HP saya.
english: The photo you sent last night won't open on my phone.

target: Lokasi restorannya saya kirim lewat pesan, ya.
english: I'll send the restaurant's location by message, okay?
grammar: Object first + saya kirim = everyday passive: lokasinya saya kirim = I'll send the location.

target: Paket data saya habis sebelum akhir bulan lagi.
english: My data plan ran out before the end of the month again.
grammar: Paket data = mobile data plan; kuota = your data allowance for the month.

target: Kuota internet cepat habis kalau sering menonton video.
english: Internet data runs out fast if you watch videos a lot.

target: Sinyal di kampung halaman saya sekarang sudah kuat.
english: The signal in my hometown is strong now.
grammar: Kampung halaman = hometown, where your family is from — not just any kampung.

target: Dia membagikan foto pemandangan itu ke media sosial.
english: She shared that scenery photo to social media.

target: Jangan menaruh nomor HP di media sosial, itu tidak aman.
english: Don't put your phone number on social media; it's not safe.

target: Saya lupa password email lama, jadi membuat akun baru.
english: I forgot my old email password, so I made a new account.
grammar: Password is the everyday word; kata sandi is what formal screens call it.

target: Belanja online memang mudah, tapi hati-hati dengan toko palsu.
english: Online shopping really is easy, but be careful with fake stores.

target: Barang yang saya beli online sampai dalam dua hari.
english: The item I bought online arrived within two days.

target: Kami menonton film lewat aplikasi karena bioskop jauh dari rumah.
english: We watch movies through an app because the cinema is far from home.

target: Internet di sini lambat, mengunggah video saja butuh satu jam.
english: The internet here is slow; just uploading a video takes an hour.
grammar: Mengunggah = upload, mengunduh = download; upload and download are also said as-is.

target: Anak muda sekarang lebih sering mengetik daripada menulis dengan tangan.
english: Young people now type more often than they write by hand.

target: Indonesia punya ribuan pulau, dari Sabang sampai Merauke.
english: Indonesia has thousands of islands, from Sabang to Merauke.
grammar: Dari Sabang sampai Merauke = 'all across Indonesia' — Sabang and Merauke are its far western and eastern ends.

target: Sawah di belakang desa itu hijau sekali setelah musim tanam.
english: The rice fields behind that village are very green after planting season.
grammar: Sawah = a flooded rice field; a dry field is ladang. Pemandangan sawah = rice-field scenery.

target: Kami berjalan kaki melewati sawah menuju air terjun di kaki gunung.
english: We walked past rice fields toward the waterfall at the foot of the mountain.

target: Hutan di pulau ini masih lebat dan penuh suara burung.
english: The forest on this island is still dense and full of bird sounds.

target: Dari puncak gunung, kami bisa melihat laut dan pulau-pulau kecil.
english: From the mountain peak, we can see the sea and the small islands.

target: Air sungai di dekat desa itu jernih dan dingin sekali.
english: The river water near that village is very clear and cold.

target: Nelayan berangkat melaut sebelum matahari terbit setiap pagi.
english: The fishermen set out to sea before sunrise every morning.
grammar: Melaut = to go out to sea (fishermen's verb): nelayan berangkat melaut. Matahari terbit = sunrise, terbenam = sunset.

target: Pasir di pantai sebelah timur pulau ini putih dan halus.
english: The sand on the beach on the east side of this island is white and fine.

target: Ombak di pantai selatan terlalu besar untuk berenang hari ini.
english: The waves at the south beach are too big for swimming today.

target: Petani mulai memanen padi di sawah minggu depan.
english: The farmers start harvesting the rice in the fields next week.
grammar: Rice has three names: padi in the field, beras raw in the bag, nasi cooked on your plate.

target: Kami menginap di desa kecil di kaki gunung berapi.
english: We stayed overnight in a small village at the foot of a volcano.
grammar: Gunung berapi = volcano, literally 'mountain with fire' (api = fire).

target: Danau di atas gunung itu dulunya kawah gunung berapi.
english: The lake on top of that mountain used to be a volcano's crater.

target: Udara di pegunungan jauh lebih sejuk daripada di pantai.
english: The air in the mountains is much cooler than at the beach.
grammar: pe-…-an turns a noun into its whole area: gunung = mountain, pegunungan = mountain range.

target: Banyak monyet liar tinggal di hutan kecil dekat pura itu.
english: Many wild monkeys live in the small forest near that temple.

target: Jalan ke desa itu sempit dan berkelok-kelok di lereng gunung.
english: The road to that village is narrow and winding on the mountainside.

target: Sungai besar itu menjadi jalan utama untuk warga di pedalaman.
english: That big river serves as the main road for people in the interior.

target: Kami menyewa perahu kecil untuk keliling danau sore itu.
english: We rented a small boat to go around the lake that afternoon.

target: Pemandangan matahari terbenam di pantai barat pulau ini terkenal indah.
english: The sunset view on this island's west coast is famously beautiful.

target: Air terjun itu tersembunyi di dalam hutan, satu jam jalan kaki dari desa.
english: That waterfall is hidden inside the forest, an hour's walk from the village.

target: Di musim kemarau, sawah di daerah kami sering kekurangan air.
english: In the dry season, the rice fields in our area often lack water.
grammar: ke-…-an around kurang (less) = to be short of something: kekurangan air = short of water.

target: Anak-anak desa berenang di sungai setiap sore setelah pulang sekolah.
english: The village children swim in the river every afternoon after coming home from school.

target: Kabut turun cepat sekali di gunung, jadi kami turun sebelum gelap.
english: The fog comes down very fast on the mountain, so we went down before dark.

target: Pantai di dekat pelabuhan kotor, lebih baik pergi ke teluk sebelah.
english: The beach near the harbor is dirty; better to go to the next bay over.

target: Orang sini percaya hutan itu harus dijaga karena dianggap keramat.
english: People here believe that forest must be protected because it is considered sacred.
grammar: Keramat = sacred, spiritually charged — said of old trees, graves, and forests people leave undisturbed.

target: Setiap pulau di Indonesia punya bahasa dan makanan khasnya sendiri.
english: Every island in Indonesia has its own distinctive language and food.
grammar: -nya sendiri = its own: makanan khasnya sendiri = its own signature food.

target: Setiap pagi saya berangkat jam enam supaya tidak kena macet.
english: Every morning I leave at six o'clock so I don't get caught in traffic.
grammar: Kena = to get hit by something unpleasant: kena macet = stuck in traffic, kena hujan = caught in the rain.

target: Macet di kota ini sudah biasa, semua orang punya cerita macetnya sendiri.
english: Traffic jams in this city are normal; everyone has their own traffic-jam story.

target: Kalau hujan deras satu jam saja, jalan depan kantor langsung banjir.
english: If it rains hard for just an hour, the street in front of the office floods immediately.

target: Musim hujan berarti musim banjir untuk warga di pinggir sungai.
english: The rainy season means flood season for residents along the river.

target: Polusi udara di kota besar makin parah pada musim kemarau.
english: Air pollution in big cities gets worse and worse in the dry season.
grammar: Makin = increasingly: makin parah = getting worse. Doubled: makin lama makin parah = worse and worse.

target: Banyak orang memakai masker karena polusi udara hari ini buruk sekali.
english: Many people are wearing masks because the air pollution today is really bad.

target: Saya lebih suka naik transportasi umum daripada menyetir sendiri di kota.
english: I prefer taking public transportation to driving myself in the city.
grammar: Umum = public/shared: transportasi umum = public transport, toilet umum = public toilet.

target: Naik kereta ke pusat kota lebih cepat daripada naik mobil.
english: Taking the train downtown is faster than going by car.

target: Bus kota di sini murah, tapi jadwalnya tidak bisa diandalkan.
english: The city buses here are cheap, but their schedule can't be relied on.

target: Kami pindah ke pinggir kota supaya dekat dengan stasiun kereta.
english: We moved to the edge of the city to be close to the train station.

target: Ojek online sangat membantu kalau kamu buru-buru di jam sibuk.
english: App-based motorbike taxis really help when you're in a hurry at rush hour.
grammar: Jam sibuk = rush hour ('busy hours'): berangkat sebelum jam sibuk = leave before rush hour.

target: Trotoar di jalan ini penuh pedagang kaki lima setiap sore.
english: The sidewalk on this street is full of street vendors every afternoon.
grammar: Pedagang kaki lima = street vendor, literally 'five-foot trader', from the five-foot colonial walkway.

target: Suara klakson di jalan besar itu hampir tidak pernah berhenti.
english: The sound of horns on that main road almost never stops.

target: Di jam pulang kantor, kereta ke arah selatan selalu penuh sesak.
english: At the end of the workday, trains heading south are always packed.

target: Kota ini terasa lebih tenang saat libur Lebaran karena banyak warga mudik.
english: This city feels calmer during the Lebaran holiday because many residents go back to their hometowns.

target: Harga rumah di pusat kota terlalu mahal untuk keluarga muda.
english: House prices in the city center are too expensive for young families.

target: Lampu merah di simpang itu lama sekali, bisa sampai tiga menit.
english: The red light at that intersection is really long; it can last up to three minutes.

target: Warga kompleks kami kerja bakti membersihkan selokan setiap bulan.
english: The residents of our housing complex do communal volunteer work cleaning the drains every month.
grammar: Kerja bakti = the neighborhood work day: everyone comes out to clean drains and cut grass together.

target: Selokan yang penuh sampah membuat banjir makin sering terjadi.
english: Drains full of garbage make floods happen more and more often.

target: Kalau banjir datang, warga memindahkan motor mereka ke tempat yang lebih tinggi.
english: When the floods come, residents move their motorbikes to higher ground.

target: Selama musim hujan, banyak keluarga menyimpan barang penting di lantai dua.
english: During the rainy season, many families keep important belongings on the second floor.

target: Setiap tahun ada gedung tinggi baru di pusat kota.
english: Every year there are new tall buildings in the city center.

target: Angkot di kota kecil berhenti di mana saja kalau dipanggil.
english: Minibuses in small towns stop anywhere when hailed.
grammar: Angkot (angkutan kota) = the shared minibus; passengers shout 'Kiri!' (left!) to get dropped off.

target: Suara azan terdengar dari beberapa masjid sekaligus waktu magrib.
english: The call to prayer can be heard from several mosques at once at sunset prayer time.

target: Setiap Minggu pagi, pasar kaget muncul di lapangan dekat rumah kami.
english: Every Sunday morning, a pop-up market appears on the field near our house.
grammar: Pasar kaget = pop-up market, literally 'startled market' — it appears out of nowhere and vanishes within hours.

target: Banyak warga kota besar menghabiskan dua jam sehari di jalan.
english: Many big-city residents spend two hours a day on the road.

target: Pemerintah kota menanam pohon baru di sepanjang jalan utama tahun ini.
english: The city government is planting new trees along the main road this year.

target: Parkir di pusat perbelanjaan itu susah sekali pada akhir pekan.
english: Parking at that shopping mall is really difficult on weekends.

target: Taman kota baru itu ramai keluarga setiap Minggu pagi.
english: That new city park is crowded with families every Sunday morning.

target: Meskipun macet dan gerah, saya tetap sayang kota ini.
english: Even though it's jammed with traffic and muggy, I still love this city.

target: Tolong buang sampah pada tempatnya, jangan ke selokan.
english: Please throw trash where it belongs, not into the drain.
grammar: Buang sampah pada tempatnya ('bin your trash') is the sign painted on walls all over Indonesia.

target: Sampah plastik dari kota sering berakhir di laut dan pantai.
english: Plastic waste from the city often ends up in the sea and on beaches.

target: Kami membawa tas belanja sendiri supaya tidak memakai kantong plastik.
english: We bring our own shopping bags so we don't use plastic bags.

target: Di sekolah, anak-anak belajar memisahkan sampah basah dan sampah kering.
english: At school, the children learn to separate wet trash and dry trash.
grammar: Trash sorts by wetness: sampah basah = wet (food) waste, sampah kering = dry (paper, plastic) waste.

target: Botol dan kaleng bekas ini bisa didaur ulang jadi barang baru.
english: These used bottles and cans can be recycled into new things.
grammar: Daur ulang = recycle ('re-cycle'): bisa didaur ulang = can be recycled.

target: Bapak itu memungut botol plastik di pantai setiap pagi.
english: That man collects plastic bottles on the beach every morning.

target: Sedotan plastik sekarang diganti sedotan kertas di banyak kafe.
english: Plastic straws are now replaced with paper straws in many cafes.

target: Jangan bakar sampah di halaman, asapnya mengganggu tetangga.
english: Don't burn trash in the yard; the smoke bothers the neighbors.

target: Truk sampah lewat di kompleks kami setiap Selasa dan Jumat pagi.
english: The garbage truck comes through our complex every Tuesday and Friday morning.

target: Air bersih makin susah didapat di beberapa daerah saat kemarau panjang.
