english: Clean water is getting harder to find in some areas during a long dry season.

target: Kami menampung air hujan untuk menyiram tanaman di halaman.
english: We collect rainwater to water the plants in the yard.

target: Matikan lampu dan AC kalau ruangan tidak dipakai, hemat listrik.
english: Turn off the lights and the AC when the room isn't in use — save electricity.
grammar: Hemat = economical, to save on: hemat listrik = save electricity, hemat air = save water.

target: Sungai di tengah kota itu mulai bersih lagi setelah warga berhenti membuang sampah.
english: The river in the middle of the city is getting clean again after residents stopped dumping garbage.

target: Pabrik di hulu sungai itu didenda karena mencemari air.
english: The factory upstream on that river was fined for polluting the water.
grammar: Hulu = upstream, hilir = downstream: pabrik di hulu = a factory upstream.

target: Banyak hewan laut mati karena menelan sampah plastik.
english: Many sea animals die from swallowing plastic waste.

target: Kampung ini terkenal karena warganya rajin mendaur ulang sampah.
english: This neighborhood is famous because its residents diligently recycle their trash.

target: Penebangan hutan di gunung membuat banjir makin parah di daerah hilir.
english: Logging the forests in the mountains makes floods worse and worse in the downstream areas.

target: Pemandu wisata meminta kami tidak meninggalkan sampah apa pun di gunung.
english: The tour guide asked us not to leave any trash at all on the mountain.

target: Udara segar dan air jernih sekarang terasa makin mahal di kota besar.
english: Fresh air and clear water now feel more and more costly in big cities.

target: Lingkungan yang bersih dimulai dari kebiasaan kecil di rumah sendiri.
english: A clean environment starts with small habits in your own home.

target: Nyamuk di kamar ini banyak sekali, saya tidak bisa tidur semalaman.
english: There are so many mosquitoes in this room, I couldn't sleep all night.
grammar: Nyamuk (mosquito) complaints are national small talk: Nyamuknya banyak, ya! = so many mosquitoes, huh!

target: Jangan lupa pakai obat nyamuk sebelum tidur, ya.
english: Don't forget to put on mosquito repellent before bed, okay?
grammar: Obat covers any remedy: obat nyamuk = mosquito repellent, literally 'mosquito medicine'.

target: Saya digigit nyamuk sepuluh kali waktu duduk di teras tadi malam.
english: I got bitten by mosquitoes ten times while sitting on the porch last night.

target: Kucing kampung itu setiap pagi menunggu di depan warung ikan.
english: That street cat waits in front of the fish stall every morning.
grammar: Kampung after an animal = local/free-range: kucing kampung = street cat, ayam kampung = village chicken.

target: Ayam tetangga berkokok jam empat pagi, lebih pagi daripada alarm saya.
english: The neighbor's rooster crows at four in the morning, earlier than my alarm.

target: Ayam kampung nenek berjalan bebas di halaman sepanjang hari.
english: Grandma's free-range chickens walk around the yard freely all day.

target: Cicak di dinding itu makan nyamuk, jadi jangan diusir.
english: The geckos on the wall eat mosquitoes, so don't chase them away.
grammar: Cicak = the little house gecko on every Indonesian wall — a welcome guest, it eats mosquitoes.

target: Suara cicak kadang membuat tamu asing kaget pada malam hari.
english: The sound of the geckos sometimes startles foreign guests at night.

target: Kami memelihara dua ekor kucing dan beberapa ekor ayam.
english: We keep two cats and several chickens.
grammar: Ekor (tail) counts animals: dua ekor kucing = two cats, seekor ayam = one chicken.

target: Anjing tetangga menggonggong setiap kali tukang pos datang.
english: The neighbor's dog barks every time the mail carrier comes.

target: Ikan di kolam belakang rumah paman besar-besar sekali.
english: The fish in the pond behind my uncle's house are all really big.
grammar: Doubling an adjective for a plural subject = all of them: besar-besar = all big.

target: Burung-burung kecil ribut sekali di pohon mangga setiap pagi.
english: The little birds are very noisy in the mango tree every morning.

target: Kambing milik pak RT makan rumput di lapangan kompleks.
english: The goats belonging to the neighborhood head graze on the field in the complex.
grammar: Pak RT = head of the smallest neighborhood unit (Rukun Tetangga) — the person everyone knows.

target: Sapi-sapi itu menyeberang jalan pelan-pelan, semua mobil menunggu.
english: The cows cross the road slowly; all the cars wait.

target: Monyet di dekat candi suka mengambil kacamata dan topi turis.
english: The monkeys near the temple like to take tourists' glasses and hats.

target: Hati-hati, monyet di sana berani merebut makanan dari tangan kamu.
english: Be careful — the monkeys there are bold enough to snatch food right out of your hand.

target: Suara katak terdengar keras dari sawah waktu musim hujan.
english: The sound of frogs can be heard loudly from the rice fields in the rainy season.

target: Semut langsung datang kalau ada makanan manis di meja.
english: Ants come right away if there's sweet food on the table.

target: Tikus di plafon berisik sekali, tapi kucing kami hanya tidur.
english: The mice in the ceiling are really noisy, but our cat just sleeps.

target: Kupu-kupu warna-warni datang ke bunga di halaman setiap pagi.
english: Colorful butterflies come to the flowers in the yard every morning.

target: Bapak itu menjual burung dan sangkarnya di pasar hewan.
english: That man sells birds and their cages at the animal market.

target: Anak saya takut kecoak, padahal dia berani memegang ular kecil.
english: My child is afraid of cockroaches, yet dares to hold a small snake.
grammar: Padahal = even though / when in fact — it flags a surprising contrast between two facts.

target: Ular sawah kadang masuk ke halaman rumah waktu musim panen.
english: Rice-field snakes sometimes come into the yard during harvest season.

target: Di pasar burung, suara ratusan burung terdengar dari jauh.
english: At the bird market, the sound of hundreds of birds can be heard from far away.

target: Nyamuk demam berdarah biasanya menggigit pada pagi dan sore hari.
english: Dengue mosquitoes usually bite in the morning and late afternoon.
grammar: Demam berdarah (DBD) = dengue fever, literally 'bleeding fever' — a rainy-season worry.

target: Hari ini gerah sekali, baju saya basah padahal hanya duduk saja.
english: It's really muggy today; my shirt is soaked even though I'm just sitting.
grammar: Gerah = muggy, hot-and-sticky (how you feel); panas = hot in general: hari ini gerah = it's sticky today.

target: Kalau gerah begini, biasanya sebentar lagi hujan deras turun.
english: When it's this muggy, usually heavy rain comes down before long.

target: Sudah seminggu mendung terus, jemuran tidak pernah kering.
english: It's been overcast nonstop for a week; the laundry never dries.
grammar: Terus after a verb or adjective = keeps on: mendung terus = overcast nonstop, hujan terus = keeps raining.

target: Langit mendung terus dari pagi, tapi hujannya tidak turun-turun.
english: The sky has been overcast since morning, but the rain just won't fall.
grammar: Doubling after tidak = just won't: tidak turun-turun = (the rain) never actually falls.

target: Sekarang musim pancaroba, pagi panas sekali, sore hujan angin.
english: It's the transition season now — mornings are very hot, afternoons bring wind and rain.
grammar: Musim pancaroba = the unstable switch between wet and dry seasons: sunny mornings, stormy afternoons.

target: Banyak orang kena flu pada musim pancaroba seperti ini.
english: Lots of people catch the flu in a transition season like this.

target: Angin kencang semalam menumbangkan pohon besar di ujung jalan.
english: Last night's strong wind knocked down the big tree at the end of the street.

target: Petir keras sekali tadi, sampai anak-anak lari masuk rumah.
english: The thunder was really loud just now — the kids even ran into the house.

target: Cabut kabel televisi kalau ada petir, itu kebiasaan ibu saya.
english: Unplug the TV cable when there's lightning — that's my mother's habit.

target: Gerimis begini biasanya berhenti sendiri sebelum sore.
english: Drizzle like this usually stops on its own before late afternoon.

target: Hujan angin kemarin membuat listrik mati tiga jam di daerah kami.
english: Yesterday's rainstorm knocked the power out for three hours in our area.
grammar: Mati works for power and machines: listrik mati = the power is out, lampunya mati = the light is off.

target: Setelah hujan semalaman, udara pagi ini segar dan sejuk sekali.
english: After it rained all night, the air this morning is really fresh and cool.

target: Awan gelap datang dari arah laut, nelayan cepat-cepat pulang.
english: Dark clouds are coming from the direction of the sea; the fishermen hurry home.

target: Debu jalanan makin tebal pada akhir musim kemarau seperti sekarang.
english: The road dust gets thicker and thicker at the end of the dry season, like now.

target: Ramalan cuaca bilang minggu ini hujan setiap sore.
english: The weather forecast says it will rain every afternoon this week.

target: Jangan percaya langit cerah di musim pancaroba, bawa payung terus.
english: Don't trust a clear sky in the transition season — always carry an umbrella.

target: Banjir besar biasanya datang waktu hujan deras bertemu air laut pasang.
english: Big floods usually come when heavy rain meets a high tide.
grammar: Pasang = high tide: air laut pasang = the tide is in. The opposite is surut = the tide is out.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini datang terlambat, para petani mulai khawatir.
english: The rainy season came late this year; the farmers are starting to worry.

target: Sore-sore begini enaknya minum teh hangat sambil melihat hujan.
english: On a late afternoon like this, the nice thing to do is drink warm tea while watching the rain.
grammar: Enaknya + verb = the nice thing to do is: enaknya minum teh = it'd be lovely to have tea.

target: Baju yang dijemur dari pagi belum kering juga karena mendung.
english: The clothes that have been hung out since morning still aren't dry because it's overcast.
grammar: Juga after belum = STILL not: belum kering juga = still not dry (and it's getting annoying).

target: Kata orang tua, kalau semut pindah rumah, hujan besar akan datang.
english: According to the elders, when ants move house, a big rain is coming.

target: Suhu di kota pantai jarang turun di bawah dua puluh lima derajat.
english: The temperature in coastal cities rarely drops below twenty-five degrees.

target: Kalau kemarau panjang, warga desa antre air bersih dari truk tangki.
english: In a long dry season, villagers line up for clean water from tanker trucks.

target: Hujan pertama setelah kemarau panjang membuat jalanan bau tanah.
english: The first rain after a long dry season makes the streets smell of earth.
grammar: Bau + noun = smells of: bau tanah = smells of earth, bau asap = smells of smoke.

target: Cuaca boleh gerah, tapi es kelapa muda selalu jadi penyelamat.
english: The weather may be muggy, but young coconut ice is always the savior.
grammar: Boleh here = 'may well be': cuaca boleh gerah, tapi... = the weather may be muggy, but...

target: Penerbangan kami ditunda dua jam, padahal kami sudah tiba di bandara sejak subuh.
english: Our flight is delayed two hours, even though we already arrived at the airport at dawn.
grammar: Padahal = even though / and yet: padahal kami sudah tiba = even though we had already arrived.

target: Menurut petugas maskapai, pesawat pengganti baru mendarat jam sembilan malam.
english: According to the airline staff, the replacement plane only lands at nine in the evening.

target: Kami hampir saja ketinggalan penerbangan lanjutan di Jakarta tadi siang.
english: We very nearly missed the connecting flight in Jakarta earlier this afternoon.
grammar: Hampir saja = very nearly (a close call): hampir saja ketinggalan = very nearly missed it.

target: Para penumpang tujuan Denpasar dimohon segera menuju pintu tujuh.
english: Passengers bound for Denpasar are requested to proceed to gate seven immediately.
grammar: Dimohon = are requested to, the announcement passive: para penumpang dimohon = passengers are requested.

target: Meskipun antrean transit panjang, kami masih sempat mengejar penerbangan berikutnya.
english: Even though the transit line was long, we still managed to catch the next flight.

target: Yang paling melelahkan dari perjalanan ini adalah menunggu enam jam di bandara.
english: The most tiring part of this trip is waiting six hours at the airport.
grammar: Yang X adalah Y spotlights one thing: Yang paling melelahkan adalah menunggu = the most tiring part is the waiting.

target: Koper saya sempat hilang di bandara transit, tapi akhirnya ditemukan.
english: My suitcase was lost for a while at the transit airport, but it was finally found.

target: Petugas bilang bahwa koper yang rusak bisa diganti oleh maskapai.
english: The staff member said that a damaged suitcase can be replaced by the airline.

target: Jangan-jangan koper kita masuk ke pesawat yang salah lagi.
english: I'm afraid our suitcase may have gone onto the wrong plane again.
grammar: Jangan-jangan voices a worry: jangan-jangan masuk pesawat yang salah = what if it got on the wrong plane.

target: Kami mohon pengertian Bapak dan Ibu atas keterlambatan penerbangan sore ini.
english: We ask for your understanding, ladies and gentlemen, for this afternoon's flight delay.
grammar: Kami mohon pengertian... = the apology formula of airport announcements — language you hear, not speak.

target: Antrean di imigrasi pagi ini makan waktu hampir dua jam.
english: The line at immigration this morning took up almost two hours.
grammar: Makan waktu = eats time, i.e. takes long: makan waktu dua jam = takes up two hours.

target: Pesawat sudah penuh, sehingga kami dipindahkan ke penerbangan sore tanpa biaya tambahan.
english: The plane was already full, so we were moved to the afternoon flight at no extra charge.

target: Petugas bertanya apakah kami mau menunggu atau minta uangnya dikembalikan.
english: The staff member asked whether we wanted to wait or ask for the money back.

target: Penumpang yang pesawatnya dibatalkan boleh menginap di hotel yang dibayar maskapai.
english: Passengers whose plane was canceled may stay overnight in a hotel paid for by the airline.

target: Tagihan kami naik dua ratus ribu, padahal kami tidak membuka minibar sama sekali.
english: Our bill went up two hundred thousand, even though we didn't open the minibar at all.

target: Resepsionis bilang bahwa biaya sarapan sudah termasuk dalam harga kamar.
english: The receptionist said that the breakfast cost is already included in the room price.

target: Kami sudah selesai berkemas, tinggal menunggu uang jaminan dikembalikan.
english: We have finished packing; all that's left is waiting for the deposit to be returned.
grammar: Tinggal + verb = all that's left is: tinggal menunggu = just waiting now.

target: Mohon dicek kembali, sepertinya kami ditagih dua kali untuk malam terakhir.
english: Please check again; it seems we were charged twice for the last night.
grammar: Mohon di- + verb = a very polite request. With hotel staff, Tolong dicek lagi is the everyday equivalent.

target: Yang membuat kami kecewa adalah biaya tambahan yang muncul tanpa penjelasan.
english: What makes us disappointed is the extra charge that appeared without explanation.

target: Kami minta check-out lebih siang, namun sistem tetap menagih biaya satu malam penuh.
english: We asked for a later check-out, yet the system still charged the cost of one full night.

target: Seandainya kami tahu kolam renangnya berbayar, kami pasti memilih hotel lain.
english: If we had known the swimming pool cost extra, we would certainly have chosen another hotel.
grammar: Seandainya = if only / supposing (unreal): seandainya kami tahu = if we had known.

target: Manajer akhirnya turun tangan setelah kami menunggu satu jam di lobi.
english: The manager finally stepped in after we waited an hour in the lobby.
grammar: Turun tangan = to step in personally: manajer turun tangan = the manager steps in himself.

target: Menurut resepsionis, uang jaminan kembali ke kartu kami dalam tujuh hari.
english: According to the receptionist, the deposit returns to our card within seven days.

target: Kami terlanjur membayar tagihan itu sebelum melihat ada biaya aneh.
english: We had already paid that bill before seeing there was a strange charge.
grammar: Terlanjur = already done, too late to undo: terlanjur membayar = already paid before realizing.

target: Biaya laundry yang tidak pernah kami pesan itu akhirnya dihapus dari tagihan.
english: That laundry charge we never ordered was finally removed from the bill.

target: Dengan senang hati kami kirimkan rincian tagihan ke email Bapak.
english: With pleasure, we will send the bill details to your email, sir.
grammar: Kami kirimkan (kami + bare verb, no meN-) = polished service register: 'we will send it for you'. Staff language.

target: Kamarnya bagus, tapi proses check-out lama sekali sampai kami hampir terlambat.
english: The room was nice, but the check-out process was so long that we were almost late.

target: Mudah-mudahan hotel ini memperbaiki sistem tagihannya sebelum kami datang lagi.
english: Hopefully this hotel fixes its billing system before we come again.

target: Katanya pantai di ujung desa ini lebih sepi daripada pantai utama.
english: They say the beach at the end of this village is quieter than the main beach.
grammar: Katanya = they say / I heard: katanya lebih sepi = I hear it's quieter.

target: Semakin lama tinggal di sini, semakin berat rasanya untuk pulang.
english: The longer we stay here, the harder it feels to go home.
grammar: Semakin X, semakin Y = the more X, the more Y: semakin lama, semakin berat = the longer, the harder.

target: Jangan lupa beli buah tangan untuk keluarga sebelum pulang ke negara kamu.
english: Don't forget to buy souvenirs for the family before going home to your country.
grammar: Buah tangan ('hand fruit') = a small trip gift — the polite word; in everyday speech you will mostly hear oleh-oleh.

target: Kalau boleh tahu, Ibu sudah berapa lama tinggal di desa ini?
english: If I may ask, how long have you lived in this village, ma'am?

target: Siapa tahu tahun depan kami bisa kembali ke pulau ini lagi.
english: Who knows, maybe next year we can come back to this island again.
grammar: Siapa tahu = who knows, maybe: siapa tahu kami bisa kembali = who knows, we might come back.

target: Di sini orang santai soal waktu, kami menyebutnya jam karet.
english: Here people are relaxed about time; we call it rubber time.
grammar: Jam karet = rubber time, the famously stretchy attitude to schedules across Indonesia.

target: Sambil menunggu hujan reda, kami mengobrol dengan pemilik warung kopi.
english: While waiting for the rain to ease, we chatted with the coffee stall owner.

target: Menurut warga di sini, air terjun itu paling indah waktu musim hujan.
english: According to the residents here, that waterfall is most beautiful during the rainy season.

target: Walaupun bahasa Indonesia saya masih kacau, orang di sini sabar sekali.
english: Even though my Indonesian is still a mess, people here are very patient.

target: Yang membuat kami betah di sini adalah orangnya yang ramah dan santai.
english: What makes us feel at home here is the people, who are friendly and relaxed.

target: Kami mulai terbiasa makan pakai tangan seperti orang lokal di warung.
english: We are starting to get used to eating with our hands like locals at food stalls.

target: Semoga besok cerah supaya kalian bisa melihat matahari terbit dari bukit.
english: Hopefully tomorrow is clear so you all can see the sunrise from the hill.

target: Kami capek setengah mati setelah mendaki gunung itu semalaman.
english: We are dead tired after climbing that mountain all night.
grammar: Setengah mati = half dead, i.e. extremely: capek setengah mati = dead tired.

target: Pemilik penginapan berjanji akan mengantar kami ke pelabuhan besok pagi.
english: The guesthouse owner promised to take us to the harbor tomorrow morning.

target: Menurut saya, rencana peluncuran ini terlalu cepat untuk tim kecil kita.
english: In my opinion, this launch plan is too fast for our small team.
grammar: Menurut saya = in my opinion: menurut saya terlalu cepat = in my view it's too fast.

target: Saya rasa usul dari tim pemasaran itu masuk akal juga.
english: I feel that suggestion from the marketing team makes sense too.

target: Bapak dan Ibu sekalian, rapat kita mulai dengan laporan penjualan bulan lalu.
english: Ladies and gentlemen, we begin our meeting with last month's sales report.
grammar: Sekalian after Bapak dan Ibu addresses the whole room: Bapak dan Ibu sekalian = ladies and gentlemen.

target: Saya setuju dengan idenya, namun anggaran kita belum tentu cukup.
english: I agree with the idea; however, our budget is not necessarily enough.

target: Yang perlu kita putuskan hari ini adalah tanggal peluncuran produk baru.
english: What we need to decide today is the launch date of the new product.

target: Kalau menurut Bapak, bagian mana yang paling berisiko dari rencana ini?
english: In your opinion, sir, which part of this plan is the riskiest?

target: Sebelum memutuskan, kita coba dengarkan dulu pendapat tim lapangan.
english: Before deciding, let's first hear out the field team's opinion.
grammar: Coba before a verb softens it into a suggestion: kita coba dengarkan = let's just hear them out.

target: Datanya menarik, akan tetapi kesimpulannya masih terlalu berani menurut saya.
english: The data is interesting; however, the conclusion is still too bold in my opinion.

target: Dia selalu mencari muka di depan direktur setiap kali rapat besar.
english: He always sucks up in front of the director every time there's a big meeting.
grammar: Mencari muka = to seek face, i.e. to suck up: mencari muka di depan bos = curry favor with the boss.

target: Usul yang kamu tolak kemarin itu justru dipuji oleh kantor pusat.
english: The suggestion you rejected yesterday was actually praised by the head office.

target: Mohon pendapat Ibu tentang rencana anggaran yang kami kirim kemarin.
english: We request your opinion, ma'am, on the budget plan we sent yesterday.
grammar: Mohon + noun = a formal written request ('we request your...'), standard in office emails to superiors.

target: Kami sempat membahas ide itu tahun lalu, tapi akhirnya berhenti di tengah jalan.
english: We did discuss that idea last year, but it eventually stopped midway.

target: Seandainya semua divisi setuju, proyek ini bisa dimulai bulan depan.
english: If all divisions agreed, this project could be started next month.

target: Sebagian tim mendukung usul itu, sedangkan sisanya masih ragu-ragu.
english: Part of the team supports that suggestion, whereas the rest are still hesitant.
grammar: Sedangkan contrasts two halves: A mendukung, sedangkan B ragu = A supports it, whereas B has doubts.

target: Semakin dekat tenggat, semakin sering klien mengubah permintaan mereka.
english: The closer the deadline, the more often the client changes their requests.

target: Klien minta supaya laporan akhir dikirim hari Kamis, bukan hari Jumat.
english: The client asks that the final report be sent on Thursday, not Friday.

target: Padahal timnya tinggal dua orang, target bulan ini malah dinaikkan.
english: Even though the team is down to two people, this month's target was raised instead.

target: Kami gagal mengejar tenggat kemarin karena data dari cabang datang terlambat.
english: We missed yesterday's deadline because the data from the branch arrived late.

target: Kalau saja tenggatnya mundur seminggu, hasilnya pasti jauh lebih rapi.
english: If only the deadline moved back a week, the result would surely be far neater.
grammar: Kalau saja = if only (wishing things were different): kalau saja tenggatnya mundur = if only the deadline slipped.

target: Dengan hormat, kami memohon perpanjangan waktu sampai akhir bulan ini.
english: Respectfully, we request an extension of time until the end of this month.
grammar: Dengan hormat = respectfully, the standard opener of formal letters and requests.

target: Laporannya hampir selesai, tinggal menunggu angka terakhir dari bagian keuangan.
english: The report is almost finished; all that's left is waiting for the final numbers from finance.

target: Atasan saya berjanji akan bicara dengan klien soal jadwal yang mustahil itu.
english: My boss promised to talk with the client about that impossible schedule.

target: Lembur sampai tengah malam sudah jadi makanan sehari-hari di tim kami.
english: Working overtime until midnight has become daily fare on our team.

target: Yang membuat jadwal ini berantakan adalah permintaan tambahan yang datang setiap minggu.
english: What makes this schedule a mess is the additional requests that come every week.

target: Kami berani berjanji selesai hari Jumat asalkan tidak ada permintaan baru lagi.
english: We dare to promise it's done by Friday as long as there are no more new requests.
grammar: Asalkan = as long as, provided that: asalkan tidak ada permintaan baru = provided nothing new is added.

target: Tim desain terpaksa berhenti mengerjakan proyek lain demi tenggat ini.
english: The design team is forced to stop working on other projects for the sake of this deadline.

target: Mudah-mudahan revisi kali ini benar-benar revisi yang terakhir.
english: Hopefully this revision really is the last revision.

target: Katanya direktur sudah setuju tenggatnya digeser ke awal bulan depan.
english: Word is the director has agreed the deadline be shifted to early next month.

target: Internet kantor mati sejak pagi, sehingga rapat online kami pindah ke kafe.
english: The office internet has been down since morning, so our online meeting moved to a cafe.

target: Saya sedang asyik menulis laporan waktu laptop tiba-tiba mati total.
english: I was deep in writing the report when the laptop suddenly died completely.
grammar: Sedang asyik + verb = absorbed in doing it: sedang asyik menulis = deep in writing.

target: Kata bagian IT, server kantor baru normal lagi besok siang.
english: According to the IT department, the office server will only be back to normal tomorrow afternoon.

target: Saya angkat tangan kalau disuruh memperbaiki printer tua itu lagi.
english: I give up if I'm told to fix that old printer again.
grammar: Angkat tangan = raise your hands, i.e. give up: saya angkat tangan = I give up.

target: File yang kamu cari itu sudah saya pindahkan ke folder bersama.
english: That file you're looking for, I have already moved to the shared folder.
grammar: Object + saya + bare verb is the polished passive: sudah saya pindahkan = I have moved it.

target: Biasakan menyimpan pekerjaan setiap beberapa menit karena listrik sering padam.
english: Make it a habit to save your work every few minutes because the power often goes out.

target: Aplikasi barunya memang canggih, namun banyak rekan belum terbiasa memakainya.
english: The new app is indeed sophisticated; however, many colleagues aren't used to using it yet.

target: Semoga kata sandi baru ini tidak saya lupakan seperti yang kemarin.
english: Hopefully I won't forget this new password like the one before.

target: Bagian IT bertanya apakah masalah email kamu sudah beres atau belum.
english: The IT department asked whether your email problem is sorted out yet or not.

target: Baik laptop lama maupun laptop baru sama-sama lambat kalau membuka aplikasi itu.
english: Both the old laptop and the new laptop are equally slow when opening that app.
grammar: Baik A maupun B = both A and B: baik lama maupun baru sama-sama lambat = old and new are equally slow.

target: Panggilan videonya sempat terputus tiga kali karena sinyal naik turun.
english: The video call briefly cut out three times because the signal kept going up and down.

target: Kami sampaikan bahwa sistem absensi baru mulai dipakai hari Senin depan.
english: We hereby announce that the new attendance system starts being used next Monday.
grammar: Kami sampaikan bahwa... = the office-memo opener ('we hereby inform'); used in announcements, never casual talk.

target: Anak magang itu sekarang jadi tangan kanan kepala bagian IT.
english: That intern is now the right hand of the head of the IT department.
grammar: Tangan kanan = right hand, the most trusted helper: tangan kanan kepala bagian = the boss's right-hand person.

target: Seandainya kantor kita pindah ke sistem baru, semua data lama harus disalin dulu.
english: If our office moved to the new system, all the old data would have to be copied first.

target: Adik saya bilang bahwa dia kadang merasa kesepian di perantauan.
english: My younger sibling says that he sometimes feels lonely living away from home.

target: Ibu berhenti bertanya soal nilai setelah melihat wajah lelah adik saya.
english: Mom stopped asking about grades after seeing my younger sibling's tired face.

target: Ayah jarang bicara soal perasaannya, padahal dia orang yang paling peduli.
english: Dad rarely talks about his feelings, even though he is the person who cares the most.

target: Jangan berkecil hati, nilai satu ujian tidak menentukan masa depan kamu.
english: Don't be discouraged; the grade of one exam doesn't determine your future.
grammar: Berkecil hati = small-hearted, i.e. discouraged: jangan berkecil hati = don't lose heart.

target: Semoga kakak cepat pulih dan bisa berkumpul lagi dengan kita waktu Lebaran.
english: Hopefully my older sibling recovers soon and can gather with us again at Lebaran.

target: Yang paling ibu khawatirkan adalah pola tidur kamu yang berantakan.
english: What Mom worries about most is your messy sleep schedule.

target: Nenek mulai betah di rumah baru walaupun jauh dari cucu-cucunya.
english: Grandma is starting to feel at home in the new house even though it's far from her grandchildren.

target: Kata ibu, ayah diam-diam bangga sekali dengan pekerjaan baru kamu.
english: According to Mom, Dad is secretly very proud of your new job.

target: Kalau saja rumah kita lebih dekat, aku bisa menengok mama setiap minggu.
english: If only our houses were closer, I could visit Mom every week.

target: Sejak menang lomba itu, sepupu saya jadi sedikit besar kepala.
english: Since winning that competition, my cousin has become a little big-headed.
grammar: Besar kepala = big-headed, arrogant: jadi besar kepala setelah menang = got cocky after winning.

target: Ayah pura-pura sibuk membaca koran supaya tidak terlihat menangis di pernikahan kakak.
english: Dad pretended to be busy reading the paper so he wouldn't be seen crying at big sister's wedding.
grammar: Pura-pura + verb = to pretend: pura-pura sibuk membaca = pretending to be busy reading.

target: Aku senang kamu mau jujur soal perasaan kamu, walaupun ceritanya berat.
english: I'm glad you're willing to be honest about your feelings, even though the story is heavy.

target: Anak yang dulu takut gelap itu sekarang berani tidur sendiri di kamarnya.
english: The child who used to be afraid of the dark now dares to sleep alone in his room.

target: Kami sekeluarga mengucapkan selamat atas kelahiran putri pertama kalian.
english: Our whole family congratulates you on the birth of your first daughter.

target: Nenek tetap memasak rendang sendiri walaupun banyak yang menjualnya dekat rumah.
english: Grandma still cooks rendang herself even though many people sell it near the house.

target: Semakin tua, ayah semakin suka makanan pahit seperti pare.
english: The older he gets, the more Dad likes bitter food like bitter gourd.

target: Menurut anak-anak, makanan cepat saji lebih enak daripada sayur bening buatan ibu.
english: According to the kids, fast food tastes better than Mom's clear vegetable soup.

target: Adik bungsu malas mencoba makanan baru kalau bentuknya aneh.
english: The youngest sibling is reluctant to try new food if its shape looks strange.

target: Sambal buatan ibu memang tidak ada duanya di keluarga kami.
english: Mom's homemade sambal truly has no equal in our family.
grammar: Tidak ada duanya = there is no second one, i.e. one of a kind: sambal ibu tidak ada duanya.

target: Kakek tidak suka makanan pedas, sedangkan cucu-cucunya berlomba menambah sambal.
english: Grandpa doesn't like spicy food, whereas his grandchildren compete to add more sambal.

target: Siapa tahu adik mau makan sayur kalau dia ikut memasaknya.
english: Who knows, maybe the little one will want to eat vegetables if he helps cook them.

target: Kata dokter, kakek harus mengurangi gula dalam kopi dan teh manisnya.
english: According to the doctor, Grandpa has to cut down the sugar in his coffee and sweet tea.

target: Makanan yang paling sering diminta cucu-cucu adalah ayam goreng buatan nenek.
english: The food most often requested by the grandchildren is Grandma's fried chicken.

target: Ibu berhasil membuat adik mau makan ikan dengan mencampurnya ke nasi goreng.
english: Mom managed to get the little one to eat fish by mixing it into fried rice.

target: Nasi sudah menjadi bubur, kue ulang tahunnya terlanjur gosong.
english: The rice has turned to porridge — the birthday cake is already burnt beyond saving.
grammar: Nasi sudah menjadi bubur = the rice is already porridge: what's done cannot be undone.

target: Kami sekeluarga baru saja mencoba restoran Korea yang buka dekat rumah.
english: Our whole family just tried the Korean restaurant that opened near the house.

target: Ayah bilang masakan Padang terlalu berminyak, padahal piringnya selalu bersih.
english: Dad says Padang food is too oily, yet his plate is always clean.

target: Mudah-mudahan tahun ini semua sepupu pulang supaya meja makan penuh lagi.
english: Hopefully this year all the cousins come home so the dining table is full again.

target: Kata sepupu, berita yang om kirim di grup itu ternyata hoaks.
english: According to my cousin, the news Uncle sent in the group turned out to be a hoax.

target: Ibu baru belajar memakai stiker, sekarang setiap pesannya penuh stiker bunga.
english: Mom just learned to use stickers; now every message of hers is full of flower stickers.

target: Grup keluarga ramai sekali menjelang Lebaran, sehingga ponsel saya berbunyi terus.
english: The family group gets really busy in the run-up to Lebaran, so my phone keeps buzzing.

target: Foto yang nenek kirim terbalik, tapi tidak ada yang berani memberi tahu beliau.
english: The photo Grandma sent is upside down, but no one dares to tell her.
grammar: Beliau = respectful he/she for elders: memberi tahu beliau = tell her (politely).

target: Ayah bertanya apakah panggilan video hari Minggu jadi atau pindah ke sore.
english: Dad asked whether Sunday's video call is still on or moving to the afternoon.

target: Adik sering membaca pesan grup tanpa pernah membalas satu kata pun.
english: Little brother often reads the group messages without ever replying a single word.
grammar: Pun after a noun stresses not even one: satu kata pun = not even a single word.

target: Setiap pagi grup keluarga banjir ucapan selamat pagi bergambar bunga.
english: Every morning the family group is flooded with good-morning greetings decorated with flowers.
grammar: Banjir used figuratively = flooded with: grup banjir ucapan = the group is flooded with greetings.

target: Jangan-jangan mama salah kirim, foto belanjaan masuk ke grup kantor papa.
english: Mom may well have missent it; the shopping photo went into Dad's office group.

target: Atas nama keluarga besar, kami mengundang semua anggota grup ke syukuran nenek.
english: On behalf of the extended family, we invite all group members to Grandma's thanksgiving celebration.
grammar: Atas nama = on behalf of: atas nama keluarga besar = on behalf of the extended family.

target: Kakak jarang muncul di grup, namun selalu datang kalau ada acara keluarga.
english: Big sister rarely shows up in the group; however, she always comes when there's a family event.

target: Nenek akhirnya berhasil mengirim pesan suara setelah diajari cucunya berkali-kali.
english: Grandma finally managed to send a voice message after being taught by her grandchild many times.

target: Yang paling rajin membalas pesan di grup keluarga justru kakek kami.
english: The one most diligent about replying to messages in the family group is actually our grandpa.

target: Semoga grup keluarga ini tetap ramai sampai cucu-cucu kita besar nanti.
english: May this family group stay lively until our grandchildren are grown someday.

target: Si Budi selalu punya cerita lucu setiap kali kami berkumpul.
english: Budi always has a funny story every time we get together.
grammar: Si before a name marks warmth among friends: si Budi ≈ 'good old Budi'. Casual only — never for elders.

target: Kemarin si kecil menangis karena balonnya terbang ke atas pohon.
english: Yesterday the little one cried because her balloon flew up into a tree.
grammar: Si + adjective names someone by a trait: si kecil = the little one, si sulung = the eldest.

target: Di kantor, si pendiam itu ternyata paling pandai bercerita.
english: At the office, the quiet one turns out to be the best at telling stories.

target: Si sulung suka mengatur adik-adiknya seperti ibu kedua.
english: The eldest likes to boss her younger siblings around like a second mother.

target: Setiap sore si bungsu menunggu ayah pulang di depan pagar.
english: Every afternoon the youngest waits for dad to come home in front of the gate.

target: Kucing kami dipanggil si belang karena bulunya hitam putih.
english: Our cat is called Spots because its fur is black and white.
grammar: Pets often get si + trait as a name: si belang = the stripey one, si putih = the white one.

target: Waktu SD, teman-teman memanggil saya si kacamata.
english: In elementary school, my friends called me 'glasses'.

target: Si Tono datang paling akhir, tetapi ceritanya paling panjang.
english: Tono arrived last, but his story was the longest.

target: Semua orang di kampung kenal si penjual bakso itu.
english: Everyone in the village knows that meatball seller.

target: Si pemalu di kelas kami sekarang menjadi pembawa acara terkenal.
english: The shy one in our class is now a famous host.

target: Si rambut panjang itu dulu sering mampir ke warung nenek saya.
english: That long-haired one used to often drop by my grandma's food stall.

target: Anak-anak menyebut anjing itu si galak karena suka menggonggong.
english: The kids call that dog 'the fierce one' because it likes to bark.

target: Si Sari lagi-lagi lupa membawa kunci rumahnya sendiri.
english: Sari has yet again forgotten to bring her own house key.
grammar: Lagi-lagi = 'yet again' (mild exasperation): Lagi-lagi hujan = It's raining yet again.

target: Dulu kami takut pada si satpam, padahal dia sebenarnya ramah sekali.
english: We used to be scared of the security guard, even though he was actually very friendly.

target: Si juara kelas itu sekarang mengajar matematika di sekolah kami.
english: That class champion now teaches mathematics at our school.

target: Katanya dulu di sini ada pasar malam setiap akhir pekan.
english: They say there used to be a night market here every weekend.
grammar: Katanya = 'they say / I heard' — marks retold info: Katanya dia pindah = I heard he moved.

target: Dia tidak datang kemarin, katanya motornya mogok di tengah jalan.
english: He didn't come yesterday; he said his motorbike broke down in the middle of the road.

target: Kata Ibu, dulu ayah pernah tersesat di kota ini selama dua hari.
english: According to Mom, Dad once got lost in this city for two days.
grammar: Kata + person = 'according to': Kata Ibu, ... = Mom says ... Katanya alone = generic hearsay.

target: Ceritanya dia mau memberi kejutan, tetapi kuenya jatuh di tangga.
english: The story goes that he wanted to give a surprise, but the cake fell on the stairs.
grammar: Ceritanya = 'the story goes' — opens an anecdote: Ceritanya mau kejutan = supposedly a surprise was planned.

target: Kata tetangga, rumah kosong itu akhirnya laku juga bulan lalu.
english: According to the neighbors, that empty house finally sold last month.

target: Katanya paman pernah bertemu orang terkenal di pasar ikan.
english: They say Uncle once met a famous person at the fish market.

target: Ceritanya kami mau mendaki gunung, tetapi semua orang bangun kesiangan.
english: The story was that we were going to hike the mountain, but everyone woke up late.

target: Katanya begitu, tetapi saya belum pernah melihatnya sendiri.
english: That's what they say, but I've never seen it myself.

target: Menurut cerita kakek, sumur tua itu tidak pernah kering.
english: According to grandpa's story, that old well has never run dry.

target: Katanya antrean di sana panjang, ternyata kami dilayani cepat sekali.
english: They said the line there was long; it turned out we were served very quickly.

target: Teman saya bercerita bahwa dia pernah salah masuk rumah tetangga.
english: My friend told me that he once went into the neighbor's house by mistake.

target: Katanya film itu seram sekali, jadi kami menonton sambil menutup mata.
english: They say that movie is really scary, so we watched while covering our eyes.

target: Ceritanya panjang, pokoknya kami baru sampai rumah jam dua pagi.
english: It's a long story; anyway, we didn't get home until two in the morning.
grammar: Pokoknya = 'anyway, bottom line' — skips the details: Pokoknya kami selamat = Anyway, we made it.

target: Kata sopir angkot, jalan ke pasar ditutup karena ada pawai.
english: According to the angkot driver, the road to the market is closed because there's a parade.

target: Katanya dia menang lomba masak, ternyata itu hanya mimpi.
english: He said he won a cooking contest; it turned out it was only a dream.

target: Setiap kali kami berkumpul, om suka mengulang cerita masa mudanya.
english: Every time we get together, my uncle likes to repeat stories from his youth.

target: Katanya resep sambal nenek tidak pernah diberikan kepada siapa pun.
english: They say grandma's sambal recipe has never been given to anyone.

target: Ceritanya aku mau berhemat bulan ini, tetapi ada diskon besar di mana-mana.
english: The story was I was going to save money this month, but there were big discounts everywhere.

target: Kabarnya pasangan itu bertemu pertama kali di halte bus.
english: Word has it that couple first met at a bus stop.
grammar: Kabarnya = 'word has it' — rumor from no one in particular: Kabarnya mereka pindah = Word is they moved.

target: Semua itu baru kata orang, belum tentu benar kejadiannya.
english: All that is just hearsay; what happened isn't necessarily true.
grammar: Kata orang = 'people say', hearsay: baru kata orang = it's only hearsay, not confirmed.

target: Saya sedang menonton berita, tiba-tiba listrik di rumah padam.
english: I was watching the news when suddenly the electricity at home went out.
grammar: Tiba-tiba = sudden, you see it happen; tahu-tahu = you only notice the result: Tahu-tahu sudah malam.

target: Tahu-tahu sudah jam dua belas dan tugas saya belum selesai.
english: Before I knew it, it was already twelve o'clock and my assignment wasn't finished.
grammar: Tahu-tahu = 'before you know it': Tahu-tahu sudah pagi = Suddenly it was morning (time slipped by).

target: Kami sedang asyik mengobrol, tiba-tiba hujan turun deras sekali.
english: We were deep in conversation when suddenly it started raining very hard.

target: Anak itu tadi ada di sebelah saya, tahu-tahu dia sudah di atas pohon.
english: That kid was next to me just now; next thing I knew he was already up the tree.

target: Tiba-tiba semua lampu mati, dan kami menyalakan lilin sambil melanjutkan cerita.
english: Suddenly all the lights went out, and we lit candles while continuing the story.

target: Saya menutup mata sebentar di bus, tahu-tahu kami sudah sampai terminal.
english: I closed my eyes for a moment on the bus; next thing I knew we had already reached the terminal.

target: Dia tiba-tiba berdiri dan berteriak bahwa dia lupa mematikan kompor.
english: She suddenly stood up and shouted that she forgot to turn off the stove.

target: Tahu-tahu gelas di ujung meja sudah pecah di lantai, padahal tidak ada orang.
english: Next thing we knew, the glass at the edge of the table had shattered on the floor, even though no one was there.

target: Waktu itu kami sedang berfoto bersama, tiba-tiba seekor monyet mengambil topi ayah.
english: At that moment we were taking a photo together, when suddenly a monkey grabbed dad's hat.

target: Saya meninggalkan gorengan sebentar di dapur, tahu-tahu sudah habis dimakan kucing.
english: I left the fried snacks in the kitchen for a moment; next thing I knew the cat had eaten them all.

target: Tiba-tiba ban sepeda saya kempis, padahal perjalanan masih jauh sekali.
english: Suddenly my bicycle tire went flat, even though the journey was still very long.

target: Kemarin sore langit masih cerah, tahu-tahu malamnya air hujan masuk ke teras.
english: Yesterday afternoon the sky was still clear; before we knew it, that night rainwater came onto the porch.

target: Adik tiba-tiba menangis keras karena es krimnya jatuh ke pasir.
english: My little brother suddenly cried loudly because his ice cream fell into the sand.

target: Kami baru bicara tentang Pak Tono, tahu-tahu beliau muncul di pintu.
english: We had just been talking about Mr. Tono; next thing we knew he appeared at the door.
grammar: Beliau = respectful 'he/she' for elders and bosses: Beliau sudah datang = He (respected) has arrived.

target: Tiba-tiba ada suara keras dari dapur, ternyata tumpukan panci jatuh.
english: Suddenly there was a loud sound from the kitchen; it turned out a stack of pots had fallen.

target: Saya menaruh kue itu di meja, tahu-tahu tinggal bungkusnya saja.
english: I put the cake on the table; next thing I knew only the wrapper was left.
grammar: Tinggal here = 'only ... left': tinggal bungkusnya = only the wrapper is left; tinggal satu = one left.

target: Musim hujan datang tiba-tiba tahun ini, lebih cepat daripada biasanya.
english: The rainy season arrived suddenly this year, earlier than usual.

target: Dulu dia sering datang ke warung ini, tahu-tahu sekarang sudah menjadi orang terkenal.
english: He used to come to this food stall often; before we knew it, he has now become famous.

target: Kami lama memilih tempat makan, ujung-ujungnya kami memasak di rumah.
english: We took a long time choosing a place to eat; in the end we cooked at home.
grammar: Ujung-ujungnya = 'in the end (predictably)': Ujung-ujungnya saya yang membayar = In the end, of course, I paid.

target: Dia bilang mau diet, ujung-ujungnya dia pesan dua porsi bakso.
english: He said he wanted to diet; in the end he ordered two portions of meatballs.

target: Setiap liburan kami mau bangun pagi, ujung-ujungnya semua bangun siang.
english: Every holiday we intend to wake up early; in the end everyone wakes up late.

target: Rapatnya panjang sekali, ujung-ujungnya keputusannya tetap sama seperti kemarin.
english: The meeting was very long; in the end the decision stayed the same as yesterday.

target: Anak-anak minta hewan peliharaan, ujung-ujungnya ibu yang memberi makan setiap hari.
english: The kids asked for a pet; in the end it's mom who feeds it every day.

target: Kami membandingkan harga di lima toko, ujung-ujungnya kembali ke toko pertama.
english: We compared prices at five shops; in the end we went back to the first shop.

target: Katanya dia cuma mau melihat-lihat, ujung-ujungnya dia pulang membawa tiga kantong belanja.
english: She said she just wanted to look around; in the end she went home carrying three shopping bags.
grammar: Doubling a verb makes it aimless/casual: melihat-lihat = just browsing, jalan-jalan = stroll around.

target: Mereka bertengkar soal arah jalan, ujung-ujungnya dua-duanya salah.
english: They argued about which way to go; in the end both of them were wrong.
grammar: Dua-duanya = both of them: dua-duanya salah = both are wrong; tiga-tiganya = all three.

target: Saya coba memperbaiki keran sendiri, ujung-ujungnya kami tetap memanggil tukang.
english: I tried to fix the tap myself; in the end we still called a repairman.

target: Ujung-ujungnya semua cerita kakek selalu kembali ke masa mudanya di desa.
english: In the end, all of grandpa's stories always come back to his youth in the village.

target: Untung saya sempat memotret pelangi itu sebelum hilang di balik awan.
english: Luckily I managed to photograph that rainbow before it disappeared behind the clouds.
grammar: Sempat = managed to fit it in: sempat memotret = got the chance to snap it before it was too late.

target: Tadi pagi dia hanya sempat minum teh sebelum berangkat kerja.
english: This morning he only had time to drink tea before leaving for work.

target: Kami sempat bingung mencari pintu keluar di mal sebesar itu.
english: We were briefly confused looking for the exit in a mall that big.
grammar: Sempat + feeling = briefly felt it: sempat bingung = was confused for a moment (then it passed).

target: Sebelum pindah ke luar kota, mereka sempat berpamitan ke semua tetangga.
english: Before moving out of town, they had the chance to say goodbye to all the neighbors.

target: Saya sempat berpikir kami tersesat, ternyata hotelnya memang di gang kecil itu.
english: I briefly thought we were lost; it turned out the hotel really was in that little alley.

target: Untung kamu sempat mencatat nomor teleponnya sebelum ponselmu mati.
english: Luckily you managed to write down his phone number before your phone died.

target: Dia sempat bekerja sebagai pemandu wisata waktu tinggal di Bali.
english: He worked for a while as a tour guide when he lived in Bali.
grammar: Sempat also = 'at some point did': sempat bekerja di Bali = worked in Bali for a time.

target: Kemarin kami tidak sempat mampir karena jalanan macet parah.
english: Yesterday we didn't get a chance to stop by because the traffic was terribly jammed.

target: Sebelum pesawat lepas landas, saya sempat mengirim pesan kepada ibu.
english: Before the plane took off, I managed to send a message to my mother.

target: Anak-anak sempat bermain hujan sebentar sebelum disuruh masuk oleh neneknya.
english: The kids got to play in the rain for a bit before being told to come inside by their grandma.

target: Saya sempat malu karena memanggil orang asing dengan nama teman saya.
english: I was embarrassed for a moment because I called a stranger by my friend's name.

target: Kami sempat mengira acaranya batal karena panggungnya masih kosong.
english: We briefly thought the event was canceled because the stage was still empty.

target: Untung dia sempat menangkap gelas itu sebelum jatuh ke lantai.
english: Luckily he managed to catch that glass before it fell to the floor.

target: Waktu antre di kasir, saya sempat lupa nomor PIN kartu sendiri.
english: While queuing at the checkout, I briefly forgot my own card's PIN number.

target: Dia sempat tinggal setahun di rumah kami waktu kuliah dulu.
english: He lived at our house for a year back when he was in college.

target: Disuruh mematikan televisi, adik malah menyalakan semua lampu di rumah.
english: Told to turn off the TV, my little brother instead turned on all the lights in the house.
grammar: Malah = does the opposite of expected: disuruh tidur, dia malah menonton = told to sleep, he watches instead.

target: Obat itu tidak mengurangi batuk saya, malah membuat saya tidur seharian.
english: That medicine didn't reduce my cough; instead it made me sleep all day.

target: Kami datang untuk menghibur dia, dia malah menghibur kami dengan leluconnya.
english: We came to cheer him up; instead he cheered us up with his jokes.

target: Sudah diberi jalan lebih dekat, dia malah memilih jalan memutar.
english: He'd already been given a shorter route; instead he chose the long way around.

target: Hujan sudah berhenti, tetapi banjir di jalan kami malah makin tinggi.
english: The rain has stopped, but the flood on our street is actually getting higher.

target: Saya yang salah, tetapi dia malah meminta maaf lebih dulu.
english: I was the one in the wrong, but he apologized first instead.

target: Niatnya menghemat uang, kami malah membeli oleh-oleh untuk satu kampung.
english: The intention was to save money; instead we bought souvenirs for a whole village.

target: Ban mobil sudah diganti, sekarang mesinnya malah berbunyi aneh.
english: The car tire has been replaced; now the engine is making a strange noise instead.

target: Kami pindah supaya lebih tenang, di rumah baru malah lebih ramai.
english: We moved so things would be calmer; at the new house it's actually noisier.

target: Adik disuruh menjaga kue, dia malah menghabiskan setengahnya sendiri.
english: Little brother was told to guard the cake; instead he finished half of it himself.

target: Saya bertanya arah kepada orang itu, dia malah ikut bingung.
english: I asked that person for directions; instead he got confused too.

target: Sudah memakai peta, kami malah makin jauh dari tempat acara.
english: Even though we were using a map, we instead got farther from the venue.

target: Waktu saya sampai, dia kaget dan bilang, "Lho, kamu bukannya di Bandung?"
english: When I arrived, she was startled and said, "Huh, aren't you supposed to be in Bandung?"
grammar: Lho = spoken surprise particle, heard everywhere: 'Lho, kamu di sini?' Understand it — no need to use it.

target: Penjaga warung tertawa dan bertanya, "Kok kamu kembali lagi, ada yang ketinggalan?"
english: The stall keeper laughed and asked, "How come you're back again — did you leave something behind?"
grammar: Kok (spoken) = 'how come?': 'Kok belum tidur?' = How come you're not asleep? Kenapa is the neutral word.

target: Gara-gara salah baca jadwal, saya menunggu bus yang tidak pernah datang.
english: Because I misread the schedule, I waited for a bus that never came.
grammar: Gara-gara = 'all because of' (blaming tone): gara-gara macet = all because of the traffic jam.

target: Kemarin saya salah naik angkot dan baru sadar setelah setengah jam.
english: Yesterday I took the wrong angkot and only realized after half an hour.
grammar: Salah + verb = did it wrong: salah naik = took the wrong one, salah kirim = sent it to the wrong person.

target: Dia salah kirim pesan cinta ke grup keluarga besar.
english: He sent a love message to the extended-family group by mistake.

target: Saya menyapa orang asing di mal karena saya kira dia teman kantor.
english: I greeted a stranger at the mall because I thought he was a coworker.

target: Sepatu saya tertukar dengan sepatu tamu lain di acara pernikahan.
english: My shoes got swapped with another guest's shoes at the wedding.
grammar: Ter- often means 'by accident': tertukar = got swapped, tertinggal = got left behind.

target: Kami terkunci di luar rumah, padahal makanan masih di atas kompor.
english: We were locked out of the house, even though food was still on the stove.

target: Saya baru sadar kaus saya terbalik setelah seharian jalan-jalan.
english: I only realized my T-shirt was inside out after strolling around all day.

target: Waktu mati lampu, saya menyikat gigi dengan krim wajah.
english: During the blackout, I brushed my teeth with face cream.

target: Ceritanya saya mau tampil rapi, ternyata saya memakai kaus kaki yang berbeda warna.
english: The story was I wanted to look neat; it turned out I was wearing socks of different colors.

target: Saya tertidur di kereta dan terbangun tiga stasiun setelah tujuan saya.
english: I fell asleep on the train and woke up three stations past my destination.

target: Untungnya ada penumpang yang membangunkan saya sebelum kereta kembali berangkat.
english: Luckily there was a passenger who woke me before the train departed again.
grammar: Untungnya = 'luckily' — introduces the rescue: Untungnya ada yang menolong = Luckily someone helped.

target: Dompet saya tertinggal di warung, untungnya penjualnya jujur dan menyimpannya.
english: My wallet got left behind at the food stall; luckily the seller was honest and kept it.

target: Saya pernah membalas lambaian orang yang ternyata melambai ke orang di belakang saya.
english: I once waved back at someone who turned out to be waving at the person behind me.
grammar: Membalas = return/reply: membalas lambaian = wave back, membalas pesan = reply to a message.

target: Pas saya mau membayar, mesin kasir mati dan antrean makin panjang.
english: Right when I was about to pay, the register died and the line got longer.
grammar: Pas (spoken) = 'right when / just as': pas saya mau membayar = just as I was about to pay.

target: Saya bicara satu jam di telepon dengan semangat, rupanya sambungannya sudah lama terputus.
english: I talked on the phone enthusiastically for an hour; apparently the connection had long been cut.
grammar: Rupanya = 'apparently, so it turns out' — the moment truth clicks: Rupanya dia sudah tahu = Turns out he knew.

target: Sampai-sampai tetangga ikut keluar karena mendengar kami tertawa terlalu keras.
english: So much so that the neighbors came out too, because they heard us laughing too loudly.
grammar: Sampai-sampai = 'so much so that': sampai-sampai dia menangis = to the point that he cried.

target: Kisah ayah jatuh ke kolam ikan masih ditertawakan sampai sekarang.
english: The story of dad falling into the fish pond is still laughed about to this day.

target: Kami tertawa sampai sakit perut mendengar cerita masa kecil paman.
english: We laughed until our stomachs hurt hearing uncle's childhood stories.

target: Dia menahan tawa waktu melihat bos salah memakai kacamata orang lain.
english: He held back laughter when he saw the boss mistakenly put on someone else's glasses.

target: Anehnya, kunci yang hilang itu muncul lagi di dalam kulkas.
english: Strangely, the lost key turned up again inside the fridge.
grammar: Adjective + -nya opens a comment: Anehnya = the strange thing is..., Lucunya = the funny part is...

target: Lucunya, kami berdua membeli kado yang sama untuk orang yang sama.
english: The funny thing is, the two of us bought the same gift for the same person.
grammar: Ber- + number = a group of people: kami berdua = the two of us, mereka bertiga = the three of them.

target: Pokoknya malam itu semua rencana kami berantakan, tetapi kami pulang sambil tertawa.
english: Anyway, that night all our plans fell apart, but we went home laughing.

target: Saya pura-pura tenang, padahal saya baru saja menumpahkan kopi di laporan bos.
english: I pretended to be calm, even though I had just spilled coffee on the boss's report.
grammar: Pura-pura = to pretend: pura-pura tenang = pretend to be calm, pura-pura tidur = pretend to sleep.

target: Sopir taksi itu terus bercerita sepanjang jalan sampai kami lupa soal macet.
english: That taxi driver kept telling stories the whole way until we forgot about the traffic jam.

target: Waktu kecil, saya percaya cerita kakak bahwa semangka bisa tumbuh di perut.
english: When I was little, I believed my brother's story that watermelons could grow in your stomach.

target: Setiap ada tamu, ikan dalam cerita ayah makin lama makin besar.
english: Every time there are guests, the fish in dad's story gets bigger and bigger.
grammar: Makin lama makin X = more and more X over time: makin lama makin besar = keeps getting bigger.

target: Kami salah masuk gedung dan ikut rapat kantor orang selama sepuluh menit.
english: We entered the wrong building and sat in on someone else's office meeting for ten minutes.

target: Ternyata sepanjang wawancara ada sisa sambal di ujung bibir saya.
english: It turned out that throughout the interview there was leftover chili sauce on the corner of my lips.

target: Saya tidak menyangka kebohongan kecil itu akan diingat teman-teman bertahun-tahun.
english: I never expected that little lie would be remembered by my friends for years.
grammar: Tidak menyangka = never expected: Saya tidak menyangka dia datang = I didn't expect him to come.

target: Gara-gara tertawa di saat hening, saya menjadi pusat perhatian satu ruangan.
english: Because I laughed during a silent moment, I became the center of attention for the whole room.

target: Sekarang setiap kali lewat jembatan itu, kami pasti ingat kejadian topi ayah.
english: Now every time we pass that bridge, we always remember the incident with dad's hat.

target: Ceritakan lagi bagian waktu kamu melompati pagar karena takut anjing kecil itu.
english: Tell again the part when you jumped over the fence because you were afraid of that little dog.
grammar: Commands drop meN-: Ceritakan! = Tell it! In statements the full form returns: Dia menceritakan...

target: Dari semua cerita liburan kami, salah naik kapal ke pulau lain tetap juara.
english: Of all our vacation stories, taking the wrong boat to another island is still the champion.

target: Apa pun yang terjadi besok, kami tetap berangkat pagi-pagi.
english: Whatever happens tomorrow, we are still leaving early in the morning.
grammar: Pun is written separately after question words: apa pun = anything/whatever, siapa pun = anyone.

target: Siapa pun boleh ikut kelas memasak ini tanpa mendaftar dulu.
english: Anyone may join this cooking class without registering first.

target: Kapan pun kamu butuh bantuan, telepon saja saya.
english: Whenever you need help, just call me.

target: Di mana pun kami makan, adik selalu memesan mi goreng.
english: Wherever we eat, my little brother always orders fried noodles.
grammar: Di mana pun = wherever: di mana pun kami makan = wherever we eat.

target: Ke mana pun dia pindah, buku-buku lamanya selalu ikut dibawa.
english: Wherever he moves, his old books always get brought along.

target: Saya tidak membawa uang tunai satu lembar pun hari ini.
english: I am not carrying even a single bill of cash today.
grammar: With a negative, satu + noun + pun = not even one: satu lembar pun = not even one bill.

target: Dia tidak menjawab satu pertanyaan pun dalam wawancara tadi.
english: He did not answer even one question in the interview earlier.

target: Saya belum pernah terlambat sekali pun selama bekerja di sini.
english: I have never been late even once while working here.
grammar: Sekali pun (two words) = even once: belum terlambat sekali pun = never late, not even once.

target: Bahkan hujan deras pun tidak membatalkan pertandingan sore itu.
english: Even the heavy rain did not cancel the match that afternoon.

target: Turis asing pun sering ikut upacara bendera di desa kami.
english: Even foreign tourists often join the flag ceremony in our village.

target: Jangan menyerah, sesulit apa pun soal ujiannya.
english: Don't give up, no matter how difficult the exam questions are.
grammar: Se- + adjective + apa pun = no matter how: sesulit apa pun = no matter how difficult.

target: Dia berangkat tanpa pamit kepada siapa pun di rumah.
english: He left without saying goodbye to anyone at home.
grammar: Tanpa ... siapa pun = without anyone at all: tanpa pamit kepada siapa pun.

target: Kata dokter, ayah tidak boleh minum kopi sedikit pun dulu.
english: According to the doctor, Dad may not drink even a little coffee for now.

target: Kapan pun ada diskon besar, toko itu langsung ramai.
english: Whenever there is a big sale, that store immediately gets crowded.

target: Apa pun menunya, masakan nenek selalu habis duluan.
english: Whatever is on the menu, Grandma's cooking always runs out first.

target: Bahkan anak-anak kecil di kampung ini bisa berenang di sungai.
english: Even the small children in this village can swim in the river.

target: Harga cabai naik terus, bahkan pedagang pun ikut mengeluh.
english: Chili prices keep rising; even the vendors are complaining too.
grammar: Bahkan = even, introduces the strongest example: bahkan pedagang pun = even the vendors.

target: Dia hafal semua nama pelanggan, bahkan nama anak-anak mereka.
english: She knows all the customers' names by heart, even their children's names.

target: Kakak saya rajin sekali; bahkan pada hari libur dia tetap bangun jam lima.
english: My older brother is very diligent; even on days off he still gets up at five.

target: Bahkan setelah dua kali dijelaskan, saya masih bingung dengan aturan pajak ini.
english: Even after it was explained twice, I am still confused by these tax rules.

target: Restoran itu selalu penuh, bahkan pada Selasa malam.
english: That restaurant is always full, even on Tuesday nights.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini panjang, bahkan bulan Juni masih sering banjir.
english: The rainy season this year is long; even in June it still floods often.

target: Dia belum pernah ke Bali, bahkan belum pernah naik pesawat sama sekali.
english: He has never been to Bali; in fact he has never even been on a plane at all.

target: Bahkan bos kami ikut membantu mengangkat kursi untuk acara besok.
english: Even our boss joined in helping carry the chairs for tomorrow's event.

target: Ibu ingat semua tanggal penting, bahkan tanggal pernikahan tetangga.
english: Mom remembers all the important dates, even the neighbors' wedding date.

target: Saya cuma mau memastikan jadwal rapat besok tidak berubah.
english: I just want to make sure tomorrow's meeting schedule hasn't changed.
grammar: Cuma = only/just, the everyday spoken word; hanya means the same but sounds more careful.

target: Tenang, ini cuma latihan, bukan gempa sungguhan.
english: Relax, this is only a drill, not a real earthquake.
grammar: Cuma X, bukan Y contrasts: cuma latihan, bukan gempa = just a drill, not an earthquake.

target: Kami cuma punya waktu lima belas menit sebelum toko tutup.
english: We only have fifteen minutes before the store closes.

target: Dia cuma bercanda, jangan diambil hati.
english: He is only joking, don't take it to heart.

target: Hanya penumpang dengan tiket kelas satu yang boleh masuk ruang tunggu ini.
english: Only passengers with first-class tickets may enter this waiting lounge.
grammar: Hanya X yang ... = only X (and no one else): hanya penumpang ini yang boleh masuk.

target: Hadiah ini hanya untuk pelanggan yang belanja di atas seratus ribu.
english: This gift is only for customers who spend over one hundred thousand.

target: Dari semua lamaran itu, hanya tiga orang yang dipanggil wawancara.
english: Out of all those applications, only three people were called for an interview.

target: Saya cuma sempat sarapan roti tawar sebelum berangkat tadi pagi.
english: I only had time to eat plain bread for breakfast before leaving this morning.

target: Obat ini hanya boleh diminum setelah makan, ya.
english: This medicine may only be taken after eating, okay?

target: Masalahnya cuma satu: kami belum menemukan tempat parkir yang aman.
english: There is only one problem: we haven't found a safe parking spot yet.

target: Hanya karena satu ulasan buruk, dia hampir menutup warungnya.
english: Just because of one bad review, she almost closed her food stall.

target: Cuma orang sabar yang tahan mengantre selama itu.
english: Only patient people can stand queuing that long.

target: Kamu bisa datang kapan saja, pintu rumah kami selalu terbuka.
english: You can come any time; the door of our house is always open.
grammar: Question word + saja = any-: kapan saja = anytime, apa saja = anything, siapa saja = anyone.

target: Ambil kue mana saja yang kamu suka dari meja itu.
english: Take whichever cake you like from that table.

target: Di kota besar, makanan apa saja bisa dipesan lewat aplikasi.
english: In a big city, any food can be ordered through an app.

target: Siapa saja boleh menyumbang buku untuk perpustakaan kecil kami.
english: Anyone may donate books to our little library.

target: Dia pergi begitu saja tanpa meninggalkan pesan apa pun.
english: He left just like that without leaving any message at all.
grammar: Begitu saja = just like that: pergi begitu saja = left just like that, no explanation.

target: Jangan percaya begitu saja pada berita yang belum jelas sumbernya.
english: Don't just blindly believe news whose source isn't clear yet.

target: Kami baru saja membicarakan proyek itu ketika listrik mati.
english: We had just been discussing that project when the electricity went out.

target: Adik baru saja tidur, tolong kecilkan suara televisinya.
english: The little one just fell asleep; please turn the TV volume down.
grammar: Baru saja = just (moments ago): baru saja tidur = just fell asleep.

target: Anggap saja rumah sendiri, jangan malu-malu.
english: Just treat it like your own home, don't be shy.
grammar: Anggap saja = just consider it: anggap saja rumah sendiri = make yourself at home.

target: Kalau bingung, tanya saja petugas di pintu masuk.
english: If you're confused, just ask the staff at the entrance.

target: Sisanya bungkus saja, sayang kalau dibuang.
english: Just wrap up the leftovers; it would be a waste to throw them away.

target: Perasaan saya saja, atau ruangan ini memang lebih dingin dari biasanya?
english: Is it just my imagination, or is this room really colder than usual?
grammar: X saja can mean 'it's just (my) X': perasaan saya saja = it's just my imagination.

target: Undangannya lewat pesan singkat saja, tidak perlu mencetak kartu.
english: The invitations can just go by text message; there's no need to print cards.

target: Tulis saja dulu semua ide yang muncul, kita bisa memilihnya nanti.
english: Just write down all the ideas that come up first; we can choose among them later.

target: Baru saja kami membahas cara hemat listrik, tiba-tiba lampu kantor padam.
english: We had just been discussing how to save electricity when suddenly the office lights went out.

target: Santai saja, hasil tesnya baru keluar minggu depan.
english: Just relax; the test results only come out next week.

target: Setelah tiga kali gagal, akhirnya dia lulus ujian menyetir juga.
english: After failing three times, he finally passed the driving test at last.
grammar: Akhirnya ... juga = finally, at last: akhirnya lulus juga = finally passed (after all that).

target: Sudah jam sembilan malam, paket saya belum diantar juga.
english: It's already nine at night and my package still hasn't been delivered.
grammar: Belum ... juga = STILL not: belum diantar juga = still hasn't been delivered.

target: Ternyata kamu suka kopi tanpa gula juga, sama seperti saya.
english: It turns out you like coffee without sugar too, just like me.

target: Selain murah, kos ini dekat stasiun juga.
english: Besides being cheap, this boarding house is close to the station too.

target: Dipikir-pikir, tinggal di kota kecil enak juga.
english: Come to think of it, living in a small town is actually pretty nice.
grammar: Juga can soften an opinion: enak juga = actually pretty nice (a mild, pleasant surprise).

target: Kalau kamu ikut, saya ikut juga.
english: If you're going, I'm going too.

target: Ternyata belajar bahasa baru itu melelahkan juga.
english: It turns out learning a new language is actually tiring.

target: Dia bukan hanya pintar memasak, tetapi pintar mengatur uang juga.
english: She is not only good at cooking, but good at managing money too.
grammar: Bukan hanya X, tetapi Y juga = not only X but also Y.

target: Ditunggu sampai sore, tukang ledengnya tidak datang juga.
english: We waited until the afternoon, but the plumber still didn't come.

target: Anak bungsu kami akhirnya berani tampil di panggung juga.
english: Our youngest child finally dared to perform on stage after all.

target: Setelah dibujuk lama, kakek mau memakai kursi roda juga.
english: After much persuading, Grandpa was finally willing to use the wheelchair.

target: Harga bensin naik, jadi ongkos ojek naik juga.
english: Fuel prices went up, so motorcycle-taxi fares went up too.

target: Katanya sedang diet, tapi dia memesan es krim juga.
english: She says she's on a diet, but she ordered ice cream anyway.

target: Pelan-pelan, akhirnya bahasa Indonesianya lancar juga.
english: Little by little, his Indonesian finally became fluent after all.

target: Sejak kuliah di luar kota, dia belajar mengatur uangnya sendiri.
english: Since studying in another city, she has learned to manage her money by herself.
grammar: Sendiri after a verb phrase = by oneself: mengatur uangnya sendiri = manage her money herself.

target: Jangan hanya percaya cerita orang, coba buktikan sendiri.
english: Don't just believe other people's stories; try to prove it yourself.

target: Kami membangun rumah kecil ini sendiri selama dua tahun.
english: We built this little house ourselves over two years.

target: Nenek masih mencuci bajunya sendiri walaupun sudah ada mesin cuci.
english: Grandma still washes her clothes herself even though there is a washing machine.

target: Lampu teras itu mati sendiri setiap tengah malam.
english: That porch light turns off by itself every midnight.
grammar: Sendiri can mean 'by itself': mati sendiri = went off on its own, nobody touched it.

target: Setiap karyawan bertanggung jawab atas meja kerjanya sendiri.
english: Every employee is responsible for his or her own desk.
grammar: Noun + -nya sendiri = one's own: meja kerjanya sendiri = his own desk.

target: Dia lebih suka bepergian sendiri karena bebas mengatur jadwal.
english: He prefers traveling alone because he is free to set his own schedule.

target: Anak itu sudah bisa memakai sepatunya sendiri sejak umur tiga tahun.
english: That child has been able to put on her own shoes since age three.

target: Saya suka masakan pedas, tetapi suami saya punya selera sendiri.
english: I like spicy food, but my husband has his own taste.

target: Pintu garasi itu bisa menutup sendiri kalau tidak ditahan.
english: That garage door can close by itself if it isn't held.

target: Sejak SMA, kakak sudah punya penghasilan sendiri dari mengajar les.
english: Since high school, my older sister has had her own income from tutoring.

target: Dia memilih tinggal sendiri supaya lebih fokus menulis bukunya.
english: He chose to live alone so he could focus more on writing his book.

target: Kami menanam sayur sendiri di belakang rumah sejak tahun lalu.
english: We have been growing our own vegetables behind the house since last year.

target: Setelah rapat, kami kembali ke ruangan masing-masing.
english: After the meeting, we returned to our respective rooms.
grammar: Masing-masing = each/respective: ruangan masing-masing = each person's own room.

target: Peserta lomba membawa alat masak masing-masing dari rumah.
english: The contest participants bring their own cooking utensils from home.

target: Setiap daerah punya cara masing-masing untuk merayakan panen.
english: Every region has its own way of celebrating the harvest.

target: Anak-anak menyimpan uang jajan masing-masing di celengan.
english: The children keep their own pocket money in piggy banks.

target: Masing-masing kelompok mendapat waktu sepuluh menit untuk presentasi.
english: Each group gets ten minutes for the presentation.

target: Kami membayar tiket masing-masing supaya tidak repot menghitung nanti.
english: We each pay for our own tickets so we don't have the hassle of calculating later.

target: Silakan isi formulir sesuai data masing-masing.
english: Please fill in the form according to your own information.

target: Dua koki itu terkenal dengan resep sambal masing-masing.
english: Those two chefs are famous for their respective sambal recipes.

target: Hotelnya bersih, murah, dan dekat pantai pula.
english: The hotel is clean, cheap, and close to the beach as well.
grammar: Pula = 'as well/what's more' — a slightly bookish juga: dekat pantai pula = close to the beach too.

target: Dia datang terlambat, tanpa membawa laporan pula.
english: He arrived late, and without bringing the report, no less.

target: Jalan menuju air terjun itu jauh, licin pula ketika hujan.
english: The path to that waterfall is far, and slippery too when it rains.

target: Ujian ini panjang, sulit pula, jadi siapkan tenaga.
english: This exam is long, and difficult as well, so get your energy ready.

target: Harganya naik dua kali lipat, stoknya terbatas pula.
english: The price doubled, and the stock is limited as well.

target: Anak itu rajin, sopan pula kepada semua guru.
english: That child is diligent, and polite to all the teachers as well.

target: Kemarin dia lupa dompet, hari ini lupa kunci pula.
english: Yesterday he forgot his wallet; today he forgot his keys as well.

target: Acaranya mulai malam, tempatnya jauh pula, jadi kami menginap di sana.
english: The event starts at night, and the venue is far too, so we are staying over there.

target: Memang saya yang salah kemarin, dan saya sudah minta maaf.
english: It really was me who was wrong yesterday, and I have already apologized.
grammar: Memang = indeed/admittedly, confirms a fact: memang saya yang salah = it really was my fault.

target: Kereta ekonomi memang lebih lambat, tetapi pemandangannya indah.
english: The economy train is indeed slower, but the scenery is beautiful.

target: Kamu benar, durian memang bukan buah untuk semua orang.
english: You're right, durian is indeed not a fruit for everyone.

target: Dia memang jarang bicara, tapi kalau bicara isinya selalu penting.
english: He indeed rarely speaks, but when he does, what he says is always important.

target: Rumah di pinggir sawah itu memang terlihat tenang.
english: The house at the edge of the rice field does look peaceful.

target: Memang benar kata ibu, membawa payung itu tidak pernah rugi.
english: Mom was right indeed: bringing an umbrella never hurts.

target: Pekerjaan di dapur restoran memang berat, apalagi saat akhir pekan.
english: Work in a restaurant kitchen is indeed hard, especially on weekends.

target: Soal macet, kota ini memang juaranya.
english: When it comes to traffic jams, this city is truly the champion.
grammar: Soal X = when it comes to X: soal macet = as for traffic jams.

target: Saya memang belum lama kenal dia, tapi saya percaya dia jujur.
english: I admittedly haven't known him long, but I believe he is honest.

target: Ongkos hidup di ibu kota memang tinggi, tetapi gajinya juga lebih tinggi.
english: The cost of living in the capital is indeed high, but the salaries are also higher.

target: Filmnya bagus sih, cuma terlalu panjang untuk saya.
english: The movie is good, I admit, it's just too long for me.
grammar: Sih adds a casual spoken nuance you will hear everywhere: bagus sih = it's good, I admit.

target: Motor ini bisa diparkir di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan.
english: This motorbike can be parked anywhere as long as it doesn't block the road.
grammar: Asal = as long as: di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan = anywhere, provided it doesn't block.

target: Sekecil apa pun sumbangannya, panitia pasti mencatat dengan rapi.
english: No matter how small the donation, the committee will definitely record it neatly.

target: Kami tidak menyangka kamu datang jauh-jauh hanya untuk makan bakso.
english: We didn't expect you to come all this way just to eat meatballs.

target: Bahkan di musim liburan, pantai ini tetap sepi dan bersih.
english: Even in the holiday season, this beach stays quiet and clean.

target: Undian ini terbuka untuk siapa saja, termasuk karyawan baru.
english: This prize draw is open to anyone, including new employees.

target: Saya sendiri belum pernah mencoba durian goreng itu.
english: I myself have never tried that fried durian.
grammar: Pronoun + sendiri = myself/himself (emphasis): saya sendiri = I myself.

target: Bapak kos kami memang baik; bahkan sering mengantar tamu ke stasiun.
