english: Our landlord is truly kind; he even often takes guests to the station.

target: Musim kemarau pun, sumur di desa ini tidak pernah kering.
english: Even in the dry season, the well in this village never runs dry.
grammar: Noun + pun = even: musim kemarau pun = even (in) the dry season.

target: Dia menghabiskan akhir pekan hanya untuk menonton ulang serial lama.
english: He spent the weekend just rewatching an old series.

target: Kalian berdua saja yang berangkat duluan, saya menyusul nanti.
english: Just the two of you go ahead first; I'll follow later.
grammar: Berdua saja = just the two (of you/us): kalian berdua saja = just you two.

target: Setiap pagi dia menyapu halaman rumahnya sendiri sebelum berangkat kerja.
english: Every morning he sweeps his own front yard before leaving for work.

target: Tiket konser itu habis dalam lima menit saja.
english: The concert tickets sold out in just five minutes.
grammar: Number + saja = just/only that much: lima menit saja = in a mere five minutes.

target: Bukan cuma anak-anak, orang dewasa juga suka taman hiburan ini.
english: It's not just kids; adults like this amusement park too.

target: Berita itu memang mengejutkan, tetapi kami mencoba tetap tenang.
english: The news was indeed shocking, but we tried to stay calm.

target: Masing-masing pihak sudah menandatangani surat perjanjian sewa.
english: Each party has signed the rental agreement.

target: Jangankan naik gunung, jalan ke warung pun dia malas.
english: Let alone climbing a mountain; he's too lazy even to walk to the food stall.
grammar: Jangankan X, Y pun ... = let alone X, even Y: jangankan lari, jalan pun malas.

target: Kami berdua memesan menu yang sama, minumannya saja yang berbeda.
english: The two of us ordered the same dish; only the drinks were different.
grammar: X saja yang ... = only X (is what differs): minumannya saja yang berbeda = only the drinks differ.

target: Pelan tapi pasti, usaha kecilnya akhirnya dikenal orang juga.
english: Slowly but surely, his small business finally became known to people after all.

target: Para penumpang dimohon segera naik ke pesawat melalui pintu tiga.
english: Passengers are requested to board the plane immediately through gate three.
grammar: Announcement style: dimohon = 'are requested to' — in speech you'd just hear tolong or harap.

target: Kereta menuju Bandung akan segera berangkat dari jalur dua.
english: The train to Bandung will depart shortly from track two.
grammar: Station style: menuju = formal 'bound for' — in conversation people just say ke Bandung.

target: Pesawat tujuan Surabaya mengalami keterlambatan sekitar tiga puluh menit.
english: The flight to Surabaya is experiencing a delay of about thirty minutes.
grammar: Announcement verb: mengalami keterlambatan = 'is delayed' — spoken: pesawatnya telat.

target: Mohon perhatian, pintu kereta akan segera ditutup.
english: Attention please, the train doors will close shortly.
grammar: Mohon perhatian = 'attention please', the standard announcement opener; mohon is a formal 'please'.

target: Para penumpang dimohon tetap duduk sampai pesawat berhenti dengan sempurna.
english: Passengers are requested to remain seated until the plane has stopped completely.
grammar: Cabin formula: berhenti dengan sempurna = 'come to a complete stop' — spoken: benar-benar berhenti.

target: Penumpang kereta dimohon berdiri di belakang garis kuning.
english: Train passengers are requested to stand behind the yellow line.
grammar: Platform announcement register: dimohon berdiri — a friend would simply say tolong berdiri.

target: Kami mohon maaf atas keterlambatan kereta ini.
english: We apologize for the delay of this train.
grammar: Official apology: kami mohon maaf atas ... — spoken: maaf ya, keretanya telat.

target: Pesawat akan segera mendarat, mohon kencangkan sabuk pengaman Anda.
english: The plane will land shortly; please fasten your seatbelt.
grammar: Cabin formula: kencangkan sabuk pengaman = 'fasten your seatbelt'; mohon works like 'please'.

target: Para penumpang tujuan Yogyakarta dipersilakan menuju pintu keberangkatan lima.
english: Passengers bound for Yogyakarta are invited to proceed to departure gate five.
grammar: dipersilakan = formal 'are invited to' — everyday version: silakan ke pintu lima.

target: Harap tidak meninggalkan barang bawaan Anda tanpa pengawasan.
english: Please do not leave your luggage unattended.
grammar: harap = formal 'please' of signs and announcements — softer than dilarang, stiffer than tolong.

target: Kereta terakhir menuju Bogor berangkat pukul sebelas malam.
english: The last train to Bogor departs at eleven at night.
grammar: pukul sebelas = formal clock time in announcements — in conversation everyone says jam sebelas.

target: Penumpang yang membawa anak kecil dipersilakan naik terlebih dahulu.
english: Passengers with small children are invited to board first.
grammar: terlebih dahulu = formal 'first, beforehand' — spoken Indonesian says duluan or lebih dulu.

target: Mohon periksa kembali barang bawaan Anda sebelum turun dari kereta.
english: Please check your belongings again before getting off the train.
grammar: barang bawaan = official 'belongings, luggage' — casually people just say barang or tas.

target: Demi keselamatan bersama, penumpang dilarang bersandar pada pintu.
english: For everyone's safety, passengers are forbidden to lean on the doors.
grammar: demi keselamatan bersama = 'for our shared safety' — a fixed announcement opener.

target: Pesawat dari Denpasar telah mendarat di terminal dua.
english: The plane from Denpasar has landed at terminal two.
grammar: telah = the formal 'sudah' of announcements and news — in speech, always sudah.

target: Perjalanan kereta ini akan memakan waktu sekitar dua jam.
english: This train journey will take about two hours.
grammar: memakan waktu = formal 'to take (time)' — spoken: perjalanannya kira-kira dua jam.

target: Para penumpang dimohon mempersiapkan tiket untuk diperiksa petugas.
english: Passengers are requested to have their tickets ready to be checked by the officer.
grammar: mempersiapkan = formal menyiapkan — announcements love memper- verbs; spoken: siapkan tiketnya.

target: Karena cuaca buruk, semua penerbangan sore ini ditunda.
english: Due to bad weather, all flights this afternoon are postponed.
grammar: Announcement passive: ditunda = 'are postponed' — a staff member would say diundur.

target: Penumpang transit dimohon menunggu di ruang tunggu utama.
english: Transit passengers are requested to wait in the main waiting lounge.
grammar: ruang tunggu = 'waiting lounge' — official signage; in speech: tempat nunggu.

target: Mohon jaga jarak aman dari tepi peron.
english: Please keep a safe distance from the edge of the platform.
grammar: peron = 'platform', a station word; mohon jaga jarak = official 'keep your distance'.

target: Pengumuman ini juga berlaku untuk penumpang kelas ekonomi.
english: This announcement also applies to economy class passengers.
grammar: berlaku = formal 'applies, is valid' — you will see it on tickets, rules and notices everywhere.

target: Para penumpang yang terhormat, selamat datang di Stasiun Gambir.
english: Dear passengers, welcome to Gambir Station.
grammar: yang terhormat = 'esteemed, dear' — the polite address of announcements and letters.

target: Anak-anak harap selalu didampingi oleh orang tua selama perjalanan.
english: Children should always be accompanied by their parents during the journey.
grammar: didampingi = formal 'be accompanied' — spoken: anaknya harus sama orang tuanya.

target: Nomor penerbangan Anda dapat dilihat pada layar informasi.
english: Your flight number can be seen on the information screen.
grammar: In announcements dapat = 'can' — in conversation this is always bisa: bisa dilihat.

target: Kepada seluruh penumpang, kami ucapkan selamat jalan dan terima kasih.
english: To all passengers, we bid you a good journey and thank you.
grammar: kami ucapkan = ceremonial 'we express' — spoken: makasih ya, hati-hati di jalan.

target: Dengan hormat, kami sampaikan jadwal rapat bulan depan.
english: Dear Sir or Madam, we hereby convey next month's meeting schedule.
grammar: Dengan hormat = 'Dear Sir/Madam', the fixed opener of every official Indonesian letter.

target: Bersama surat ini kami lampirkan daftar harga terbaru.
english: With this letter we attach the latest price list.
grammar: bersama surat ini = 'enclosed with this letter' — pure letter language, never spoken.

target: Atas perhatian Bapak, kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: For your attention, Sir, we express our thanks.
grammar: Atas perhatian ... terima kasih = the fixed letter closer, 'thank you for your attention'.

target: Hormat kami, bagian pemasaran PT Maju Bersama.
english: Yours faithfully, the marketing department of PT Maju Bersama.
grammar: Hormat kami = 'yours faithfully' — the letter sign-off from a team or company.

target: Saya menulis surat ini untuk mengajukan permohonan cuti.
english: I am writing this letter to submit a leave request.
grammar: mengajukan permohonan = 'to submit a request' — office language; spoken: minta cuti.

target: Dengan ini saya mengajukan pengunduran diri dari jabatan saya.
english: I hereby submit my resignation from my position.
grammar: dengan ini = 'hereby' — a signal of formal writing; nobody says it out loud.

target: Mohon konfirmasi kehadiran Anda paling lambat hari Jumat.
english: Please confirm your attendance by Friday at the latest.
grammar: paling lambat = 'at the latest' — the deadline phrase of letters and forms.

target: Kami mohon maaf atas kesalahan penulisan pada surat sebelumnya.
english: We apologize for the writing error in the previous letter.
grammar: kesalahan penulisan = 'clerical error', letter-speak — spoken: ada salah ketik.

target: Surat lamaran dan riwayat hidup dapat dikirim melalui email kantor.
english: Application letters and CVs can be sent via the office email.
grammar: riwayat hidup = 'curriculum vitae' — job-application word; people just say CV.

target: Demikian surat ini kami buat, atas kerja samanya kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: Thus we have written this letter; we thank you for your cooperation.
grammar: Demikian ... = 'thus ends this letter', the classic closing line of official letters.

target: Kepada Yang Terhormat Ibu Sari di tempat.
english: To the Honorable Mrs. Sari, at her address.
grammar: di tempat on an envelope = 'at your address' — used when the writer skips the full address.

target: Kami sampaikan bahwa kantor akan tutup selama libur Lebaran.
english: We hereby inform you that the office will be closed during the Lebaran holiday.
grammar: bahwa = 'that' introducing a clause — written style; conversation usually drops it.

target: Mohon hadir tepat waktu karena rapat akan dimulai pukul sembilan.
english: Please be present on time because the meeting will start at nine.
grammar: hadir = formal 'datang' — meeting language; spoken: datang ya, jangan telat.

target: Berdasarkan hasil rapat, kegiatan tahunan akan diadakan bulan Agustus.
english: Based on the meeting results, the annual event will be held in August.
grammar: berdasarkan = 'based on' — report language; spoken: dari hasil rapat.

target: Kami mengharapkan balasan Bapak dalam waktu tujuh hari kerja.
english: We await your reply, Sir, within seven working days.
grammar: hari kerja = 'working days' — the official way offices count deadlines.

target: Perusahaan kami bergerak di bidang jasa pengiriman barang.
english: Our company operates in the field of goods delivery services.
grammar: bergerak di bidang = 'operates in the field of' — company-profile phrase, letters only.

target: Mohon maaf, permintaan Bapak belum dapat kami penuhi saat ini.
english: We are sorry, Sir; we cannot yet fulfill your request at this time.
grammar: belum dapat kami penuhi = the polite refusal of letters; spoken: maaf, belum bisa.

target: Segala biaya perjalanan akan ditanggung oleh pihak perusahaan.
english: All travel costs will be borne by the company.
grammar: pihak = 'party, side' (pihak perusahaan = the company) — contract wording, not speech.

target: Apabila ada pertanyaan, silakan hubungi bagian administrasi kami.
english: If there are any questions, please contact our administration department.
grammar: apabila = formal 'if' — letters and rules; in conversation always kalau.

target: Surat keterangan kerja ini dibuat untuk dipakai sebagaimana mestinya.
english: This employment certificate is issued to be used as appropriate.
grammar: sebagaimana mestinya = 'as it should be used' — boilerplate closing official certificates.

target: Dilarang merokok di seluruh area gedung ini.
english: Smoking is prohibited throughout this building.
grammar: Sign register: dilarang = 'it is prohibited' — spoken: tidak boleh merokok di sini.

target: Harap antre dengan tertib di belakang garis ini.
english: Please queue in an orderly manner behind this line.
grammar: dengan tertib = 'in an orderly way' — sign language; spoken: antre yang rapi ya.

target: Mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya, lift sedang dalam perbaikan.
english: We apologize for the inconvenience; the elevator is under repair.
grammar: ketidaknyamanan = 'inconvenience' — apology-notice word built from tidak nyaman.

target: Dilarang membuang sampah di sungai, pelanggar akan didenda.
english: Throwing trash in the river is forbidden; violators will be fined.
grammar: pelanggar = 'violator', from melanggar (break a rule) — sign and law vocabulary.

target: Isilah formulir ini dengan huruf cetak dan tinta hitam.
english: Fill in this form in block letters and black ink.
grammar: -lah on isilah = polite written command — forms say isilah, people say tolong diisi.

target: Kolom tanda tangan harap diisi oleh pemohon sendiri.
english: The signature field should be filled in by the applicant themselves.
grammar: pemohon = 'the applicant', from memohon — form vocabulary; spoken: yang mengajukan.

target: Lampirkan fotokopi kartu identitas pada formulir pendaftaran Anda.
english: Attach a photocopy of your identity card to your registration form.
grammar: Form verb: lampirkan = 'attach (as an enclosure)' — you meet it on every application.

target: Dilarang berjualan di sepanjang trotoar ini.
english: Selling is prohibited along this sidewalk.
grammar: Street-sign pattern: dilarang + verb = 'no ...-ing'; berjualan = to sell as a trade.

target: Harap tenang, ujian sedang berlangsung di ruangan ini.
english: Please be quiet; an exam is in progress in this room.
grammar: sedang berlangsung = 'is in progress' — notice-board phrase; spoken: lagi ada ujian.

target: Jagalah kebersihan lingkungan demi kesehatan kita bersama.
english: Keep the environment clean for the sake of our shared health.
grammar: demi = 'for the sake of' — slogan word on public signs and campaigns.

target: Pengunjung dilarang membawa makanan dan minuman ke dalam museum.
english: Visitors are forbidden to bring food and drinks into the museum.
grammar: Signs pair formal nouns with dilarang: pengunjung = visitors — spoken: tidak boleh bawa makanan.

target: Area ini khusus untuk pemegang kartu anggota.
english: This area is exclusively for membership card holders.
grammar: pemegang kartu = 'card holder' — peN- turns pegang (hold) into the person who holds.

target: Mohon lepas alas kaki sebelum memasuki musala.
english: Please remove your footwear before entering the prayer room.
grammar: alas kaki = 'footwear', the sign word — everyone actually says sepatu dan sandal.

target: Dilarang parkir di depan pintu darurat ini.
english: Parking is prohibited in front of this emergency door.
grammar: darurat = 'emergency' — pintu darurat, keadaan darurat; a word from signs and news.

target: Kawasan ini bebas asap rokok mulai bulan ini.
english: This area is smoke-free starting this month.
grammar: kawasan = official 'zone, area' — signs say kawasan bebas rokok; spoken: daerah.

target: Simpan barang berharga Anda di dalam loker yang tersedia.
english: Store your valuables in the lockers provided.
grammar: yang tersedia = 'that are provided, available' — notice phrasing; spoken: yang ada.

target: Harap matikan telepon genggam selama pertunjukan berlangsung.
english: Please switch off mobile phones while the performance is in progress.
grammar: telepon genggam = official 'mobile phone' — in real life everyone says HP (ha-pe).

target: Pintu ini hanya untuk keadaan darurat, jangan dibuka sembarangan.
english: This door is only for emergencies; do not open it carelessly.
grammar: keadaan darurat = 'an emergency situation' — keadaan makes nouns sound official.

target: Setiap pengunjung wajib mengenakan masker di dalam rumah sakit.
english: Every visitor is required to wear a mask inside the hospital.
grammar: wajib = 'must (by rule)' — sign word; spoken: harus pakai masker.

target: Dilarang mengambil foto dengan lampu kilat di galeri ini.
english: Taking photos with flash is prohibited in this gallery.
grammar: lampu kilat = 'camera flash', the sign word — everyone just says flash.

target: Tulis nama lengkap Anda sesuai kartu identitas.
english: Write your full name as it appears on your identity card.
grammar: sesuai = 'in accordance with' — form instruction; spoken: sama seperti di KTP.

target: Formulir yang sudah diisi harap diserahkan ke loket satu.
english: Completed forms should be handed in at counter one.
grammar: diserahkan = formal 'be handed over' — counter language; spoken: kasih ke loket satu.

target: Dilarang masuk tanpa izin dari petugas keamanan.
english: No entry without permission from the security officer.
grammar: petugas keamanan = official 'security officer' — everyone actually says satpam.

target: Pakailah tangga darurat apabila terjadi kebakaran.
english: Use the emergency stairs if a fire occurs.
grammar: terjadi = formal 'happens, occurs' — news and signs; spoken: kalau ada kebakaran.

target: Harap tutup kembali pintu pagar setelah Anda lewat.
english: Please close the gate again after you pass through.
grammar: kembali after a verb = 'back, again' in notices: tutup kembali — spoken: tutup lagi.

target: Pemerintah mengumumkan kenaikan harga bahan bakar mulai minggu depan.
english: The government announces a fuel price increase starting next week.
grammar: News style: kenaikan harga = 'a price increase' — spoken: harganya naik.

target: Harga beras di pasar tradisional naik sejak awal bulan ini.
english: The price of rice at traditional markets has risen since the start of this month.
grammar: Headline verbs stand bare: naik = 'has risen' — news drops sudah; add it when speaking.

target: Presiden meresmikan jembatan baru di Kalimantan pagi tadi.
english: The president inaugurated a new bridge in Kalimantan this morning.
grammar: meresmikan = 'to officially open', from resmi (official) — the ceremony verb of news.

target: Hujan deras menyebabkan banjir di beberapa wilayah ibu kota.
english: Heavy rain caused flooding in several areas of the capital.
grammar: wilayah = the news word for 'area, region' — in conversation people say daerah.

target: Warga diminta waspada terhadap cuaca ekstrem minggu ini.
english: Residents are asked to be alert to extreme weather this week.
grammar: News passive diminta = '(people) are asked to' — spoken: tolong hati-hati ya.

target: Jumlah wisatawan asing meningkat tajam pada liburan tahun baru.
english: The number of foreign tourists rose sharply during the New Year holidays.
grammar: meningkat = news 'to increase' — spoken: naik; meningkat tajam = rose sharply.

target: Polisi menangkap dua pelaku pencurian sepeda motor semalam.
english: Police arrested two motorcycle theft perpetrators last night.
grammar: pelaku = 'perpetrator' (from laku, act) — crime-news vocabulary; spoken: pencurinya.

target: Sekolah di daerah banjir diliburkan selama tiga hari.
english: Schools in the flooded area are closed for three days.
grammar: diliburkan = 'are given days off', official passive — spoken: sekolahnya libur.

target: Menteri kesehatan mengunjungi rumah sakit umum di Medan kemarin.
english: The health minister visited the public hospital in Medan yesterday.
grammar: rumah sakit umum = 'public hospital' — umum marks public services in official language.

target: Harga cabai turun setelah panen besar di Jawa Timur.
english: Chili prices fell after a big harvest in East Java.
grammar: Headline word order: topic first — Harga cabai turun; spoken: harga cabainya sudah turun.

target: Pemerintah kota membangun taman baru di pusat kota.
english: The city government is building a new park in the city center.
grammar: pemerintah kota = 'city government' — headlines often shorten it to pemkot.

target: Ribuan orang menghadiri festival budaya di Solo akhir pekan lalu.
english: Thousands of people attended the cultural festival in Solo last weekend.
grammar: akhir pekan = news 'weekend' — in conversation everyone says weekend or Sabtu-Minggu.

target: Jalan utama menuju pelabuhan ditutup karena perbaikan jembatan.
english: The main road to the harbor is closed due to bridge repairs.
grammar: pelabuhan = 'harbor', from labuh — pe-...-an builds place nouns in formal Indonesian.

target: Tim nasional berhasil menang dua kosong atas Malaysia tadi malam.
english: The national team managed to win two-nil over Malaysia last night.
grammar: atas after menang = 'over (an opponent)' — sports-news phrasing; spoken: lawan Malaysia.

target: Bank sentral menurunkan suku bunga untuk mendorong ekonomi.
english: The central bank lowered interest rates to encourage the economy.
grammar: suku bunga = 'interest rate', a finance-news term — bunga alone is flower or interest.

target: Kebakaran hutan kembali muncul di beberapa titik di Sumatera.
english: Forest fires have appeared again at several points in Sumatra.
grammar: kembali before a verb = formal 'again' — news: kembali muncul; speech: muncul lagi.

target: Pemerintah menyiapkan bantuan untuk korban gempa di Sulawesi.
english: The government is preparing aid for earthquake victims in Sulawesi.
grammar: bantuan = 'aid', the noun of bantu (help) — -an turns verbs into things given.

target: Harga tiket pesawat diperkirakan naik menjelang hari raya.
english: Airplane ticket prices are expected to rise ahead of the holiday.
grammar: diperkirakan = 'is expected, estimated' — the forecast verb of news; spoken: kayaknya naik.

target: Kota Bandung menjadi tuan rumah lomba robot tingkat nasional.
english: The city of Bandung is hosting the national-level robot competition.
grammar: tuan rumah = 'host (city, team)', literally 'master of the house' — sports-news idiom.

target: Cuaca panas ekstrem melanda beberapa kota besar di Jawa.
english: Extreme hot weather has struck several big cities in Java.
grammar: melanda = news 'to strike, sweep' (weather, floods) — never for people hitting things.

target: Petani mengeluh karena harga pupuk semakin mahal tahun ini.
english: Farmers complain because fertilizer prices are increasingly expensive this year.
grammar: mengeluh = 'to complain', root keluh — the news standard for quoting unhappy groups.

target: Jumlah penduduk ibu kota mencapai sebelas juta jiwa tahun ini.
english: The capital's population reached eleven million people this year.
grammar: jiwa (soul) counts people in statistics: sebelas juta jiwa = eleven million people.

target: Pameran buku nasional dibuka untuk umum mulai hari Rabu.
english: The national book fair opens to the public starting Wednesday.
grammar: untuk umum = 'for the public' — notice and news phrase; umum also means 'general'.

target: Angka kecelakaan lalu lintas menurun selama bulan puasa.
english: The number of traffic accidents declined during the fasting month.
grammar: angka = 'figure, number' in statistics news: angka kecelakaan = accident numbers.

target: Perusahaan teknologi lokal membuka seribu lapangan kerja baru.
english: A local technology company is opening a thousand new jobs.
grammar: lapangan kerja = 'jobs, employment' (literally 'work field') — economy-news collocation.

target: Kami mengundang Bapak dan Ibu untuk hadir pada acara pernikahan putri kami.
english: We invite you, Sir and Madam, to attend our daughter's wedding ceremony.
grammar: Invitation style: mengundang Bapak/Ibu = formal 'you' — never kamu on an invitation.

target: Acara akan diadakan pada hari Minggu, pukul sepuluh pagi.
english: The event will be held on Sunday at ten in the morning.
grammar: diadakan = 'will be held', invitation passive — spoken: acaranya hari Minggu jam sepuluh.

target: Kami mengharapkan kehadiran Saudara pada rapat warga bulan ini.
english: We look forward to your presence at this month's residents' meeting.
grammar: Saudara = very formal 'you' on invitations and forms — heard almost only in officialese.

target: Acara syukuran akan bertempat di kediaman Bapak Rahmat.
english: The thanksgiving celebration will take place at Mr. Rahmat's residence.
grammar: kediaman = formal 'residence' — invitations say kediaman, everyone else says rumah.

target: Mohon doa restu untuk pernikahan putra kami bulan depan.
english: We ask for your blessing for our son's wedding next month.
grammar: doa restu = 'prayers and blessing' — a fixed wedding-invitation phrase.

target: Atas kehadiran dan doa Bapak Ibu, kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: For your presence and prayers, we express our thanks.
grammar: Invitation closer: atas kehadiran ... terima kasih — thanks given before the event happens.

target: Kami mohon kehadiran Bapak tepat waktu karena acara dimulai sore hari.
english: We request your presence on time because the event begins in the late afternoon.
grammar: mohon kehadiran = 'we request your presence' — spoken this is just: datang ya.

target: Turut mengundang keluarga besar Wijaya dan rekan kantor.
english: Also extending the invitation: the extended Wijaya family and office colleagues.
grammar: Turut mengundang = 'also inviting' — the line listing extra hosts at the bottom of invitations.

target: Kehadiran Bapak dan Ibu akan menjadi kehormatan bagi keluarga kami.
english: Your presence will be an honor for our family.
grammar: bagi = formal 'untuk' (for) — invitation and news word; spoken: untuk keluarga kami.

target: Acara dilanjutkan dengan makan siang bersama di ruang utama.
english: The event continues with a shared lunch in the main hall.
grammar: dilanjutkan dengan = 'followed by' — programme wording on invitations.

target: Kami mengundang seluruh warga untuk mengikuti kerja bakti hari Minggu pagi.
english: We invite all residents to join the community work day on Sunday morning.
grammar: kerja bakti = 'community work day' — a fixed term on neighborhood invitations.

target: Mohon kehadiran Ibu pada pertemuan orang tua murid hari Sabtu.
english: We request your presence, Madam, at the parents' meeting on Saturday.
grammar: pertemuan = formal 'meeting', from bertemu — schools write pertemuan, parents say rapat.

target: Undangan ini berlaku untuk dua orang termasuk anak-anak.
english: This invitation is valid for two people, including children.
grammar: termasuk = 'including' — the ter- form of masuk; common in rules and invitations.

target: Besar harapan kami Bapak dapat hadir dan memberikan sambutan.
english: It is our great hope that you can attend and give a speech.
grammar: Besar harapan kami = 'it is our great hope' — a super-polite invitation formula.

target: Kami menantikan kehadiran Anda sekeluarga pada acara ulang tahun perusahaan.
english: We look forward to the presence of you and your family at the company anniversary event.
grammar: menantikan = 'to look forward to, await' — the formal menunggu; invitations love it.

target: Nasabah dimohon mengambil nomor antrean sebelum menuju loket.
english: Customers are requested to take a queue number before proceeding to the counter.
grammar: nasabah = 'bank customer' — only banks use it; shops say pelanggan or pembeli.

target: Kantor cabang kami buka setiap hari kerja mulai pukul delapan.
english: Our branch office is open every working day from eight o'clock.
grammar: kantor cabang = 'branch office' — cabang is the branch of a tree, a bank, a company.

target: Biaya administrasi sebesar lima ribu rupiah dikenakan untuk setiap transaksi.
english: An administration fee of five thousand rupiah is charged for each transaction.
grammar: sebesar = 'in the amount of' (se- + besar) — money notices use it before every figure.

target: Mesin ATM di lantai satu sedang dalam perbaikan sementara.
english: The ATM on the first floor is temporarily under repair.
grammar: sedang dalam perbaikan = 'under repair', notice formula — spoken: lagi diperbaiki.

target: Mohon jangan memberikan kata sandi Anda kepada siapa pun.
english: Please do not give your password to anyone.
grammar: kata sandi = official 'password' — most Indonesians just say password; sandi = code.

target: Layanan pelanggan kami dapat dihubungi dua puluh empat jam.
english: Our customer service can be reached twenty-four hours a day.
grammar: layanan = formal 'service', from melayani — notices write layanan, speech often servis.

target: Rapat seluruh karyawan akan diadakan hari Jumat pukul dua siang.
english: An all-staff meeting will be held on Friday at two in the afternoon.
grammar: karyawan = 'employee', the office word — casual speech says pegawai or orang kantor.

target: Seluruh karyawan diwajibkan mengikuti pelatihan keselamatan kerja bulan depan.
english: All employees are required to attend the occupational safety training next month.
grammar: diwajibkan = 'are required to', HR passive — spoken: semua harus ikut.

target: Kartu yang tertelan mesin dapat diambil di kantor cabang terdekat.
english: A card swallowed by the machine can be collected at the nearest branch office.
grammar: tertelan = 'accidentally swallowed' — ter- marks accidents: kartunya tertelan mesin.

target: Harap simpan bukti pembayaran ini sebagai tanda terima yang sah.
english: Please keep this proof of payment as a valid receipt.
grammar: sah = 'valid, legal' — stamp-and-signature word: tanda terima yang sah = a valid receipt.

target: Pengambilan uang di atas sepuluh juta harap dilaporkan sehari sebelumnya.
english: Withdrawals above ten million should be reported one day in advance.
grammar: pengambilan uang = 'withdrawal', teller language — spoken: mau ambil uang.

target: Sistem kami akan diperbarui malam ini mulai pukul sebelas.
english: Our system will be updated tonight starting at eleven.
grammar: diperbarui = 'be updated, renewed', from baru (new) — memper- means 'make more X'.

target: Selama jam istirahat, pelayanan di loket dua dihentikan sementara.
english: During the break, service at counter two is temporarily suspended.
grammar: dihentikan sementara = 'temporarily suspended', notice-speak — spoken: loketnya tutup dulu.

target: Mohon maaf, layanan transfer antarbank sedang mengalami gangguan.
english: We apologize; the interbank transfer service is currently experiencing a disruption.
grammar: mengalami gangguan = 'experiencing a disruption', outage-notice formula — spoken: lagi error.

target: Terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda kepada bank kami selama ini.
english: Thank you for your trust in our bank all this time.
grammar: atas after terima kasih = formal 'for': terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda — speech drops atas.

target: Aku nggak bisa datang ke acara kantor besok malam.
english: I can't make it to the office event tomorrow night.
grammar: Heard everywhere in speech: nggak = tidak. Nggak bisa = tidak bisa (can't). In writing, use tidak.

target: Dia nggak suka kopi, jadi kami pesan teh manis.
english: He doesn't like coffee, so we ordered sweet tea.
grammar: Nggak is spoken tidak: nggak suka = tidak suka (doesn't like).

target: Kenapa kamu nggak bilang dari kemarin kalau mau pinjam motor?
english: Why didn't you say since yesterday that you wanted to borrow the motorbike?
grammar: Nggak bilang = tidak bilang. Nggak is how 'not' sounds in everyday talk.

target: Tenang, jalan ke stasiun nggak jauh, paling lima menit.
english: Relax, the walk to the station isn't far, five minutes tops.
grammar: Nggak jauh = tidak jauh (not far) — nggak is the everyday spoken 'not'.

target: Maaf ya, aku nggak sempat balas pesanmu tadi pagi.
english: Sorry, I didn't get a chance to reply to your message this morning.
grammar: Nggak sempat = tidak sempat (didn't get a chance). Spoken form of tidak.

target: Kalau hujan begini, dia biasanya nggak mau keluar rumah.
english: When it rains like this, he usually doesn't want to leave the house.
grammar: Nggak mau = tidak mau (doesn't want to) — you'll hear nggak far more than tidak.

target: Kata penjualnya, sambal di warung ini nggak terlalu pedas.
english: According to the seller, the sambal at this food stall isn't too spicy.
grammar: Nggak terlalu pedas = tidak terlalu pedas. Nggak is casual speech only.

target: Kamu nggak capek setelah lembur tiga hari berturut-turut?
english: Aren't you tired after working overtime three days in a row?
grammar: Nggak capek? = tidak capai? (not tired?) — everyday spoken register.

target: Mereka nggak jadi pindah ke Surabaya karena anaknya betah di sini.
english: They ended up not moving to Surabaya because their kid feels at home here.
grammar: Nggak jadi = tidak jadi: 'ended up not happening'. Nggak = spoken tidak.

target: Nggak apa-apa, besok kita coba lagi dari awal.
english: It's okay, tomorrow we'll try again from the start.
grammar: Nggak apa-apa = tidak apa-apa ('it's okay') — one of the most common spoken phrases.

target: Kamu udah makan belum? Aku baru mau pesan nasi goreng.
english: Have you eaten yet? I was just about to order fried rice.
grammar: Udah = sudah in speech: udah makan? = sudah makan? (eaten yet?)

target: Tenang, tiketnya udah aku bayar dari minggu lalu.
english: Relax, I already paid for the tickets last week.
grammar: Udah aku bayar = sudah saya bayar. Udah is how sudah sounds in conversation.

target: Dia udah berangkat ke bandara sejak jam lima pagi.
english: She already left for the airport at five in the morning.
grammar: Udah berangkat = sudah berangkat (already left). Spoken form; write sudah.

target: Laporanmu udah aku kirim ke bos tadi siang.
english: I already sent your report to the boss this afternoon.
grammar: Udah aku kirim = sudah saya kirim (already sent). Everyday spoken sudah.

target: Udah malam, ayo kita pulang sebelum hujan turun.
english: It's late already, come on, let's go home before the rain starts.
grammar: Udah malam = sudah malam ('it's late already'). Udah = spoken sudah.

target: Anak-anak udah tidur, jadi jangan berisik di ruang tamu.
english: The kids are already asleep, so don't be noisy in the living room.
grammar: Anak-anak udah tidur = sudah tidur. Udah is heard everywhere; sudah is written.

target: Filmnya udah mulai sepuluh menit yang lalu, kita telat.
english: The movie already started ten minutes ago, we're late.
grammar: Udah mulai = sudah mulai (already started) — spoken sudah.

target: Aku udah tiga kali telepon, tapi dia belum angkat juga.
english: I've already called three times, but she still hasn't picked up.
grammar: Udah tiga kali = sudah tiga kali (three times already). Casual speech.

target: Duduk di sini aja, dekat jendela biar adem.
english: Just sit here, near the window so it's cooler.
grammar: Aja = saja (just): di sini aja = di sini saja (just here).

target: Kalau bingung pilih menu, pesan yang biasa aja.
english: If you can't decide on the menu, just order the usual.
grammar: Yang biasa aja = yang biasa saja — 'just the usual'. Aja is spoken saja.

target: Kamu tanya aja langsung ke petugas di loket dua.
english: Just go ask the officer at counter two directly.
grammar: Tanya aja = tanya saja ('just ask'). Aja follows the word it limits.

target: Santai aja, rapatnya baru mulai jam dua nanti.
english: Just relax, the meeting doesn't start until two.
grammar: Santai aja = santai saja ('just relax'). Spoken form of saja.

target: Bilang aja ke ibu kalau kamu pulang telat malam ini.
english: Just tell Mom you're coming home late tonight.
grammar: Bilang aja = bilang saja ('just tell her'). Everyday speech; write saja.

target: Naik ojek aja dari stasiun, lebih cepat daripada jalan kaki.
english: Just take a motorbike taxi from the station, it's faster than walking.
grammar: Naik ojek aja = naik ojek saja ('just take an ojek'). Aja = spoken saja.

target: Ambil aja kuenya, masih banyak di dapur.
english: Go ahead and take the cake, there's still plenty in the kitchen.
grammar: Ambil aja = ambil saja ('go ahead, take it').

target: Kita ketemu di depan mal aja jam tujuh, ya?
english: Let's just meet in front of the mall at seven, okay?
grammar: Di depan mal aja = di depan mal saja ('let's just meet at the mall').

target: Macetnya parah banget tadi pagi di jalan ke kantor.
english: The traffic was really terrible this morning on the way to the office.
grammar: Banget = sekali/sangat: parah banget = parah sekali (really bad). Spoken only.

target: Kue buatan nenek enak banget, aku makan tiga potong.
english: Grandma's homemade cake is so good, I ate three slices.
grammar: Enak banget = enak sekali (so tasty). Banget follows the adjective.

target: Hari ini panas banget, jangan lupa bawa topi.
english: It's really hot today, don't forget to bring a hat.
grammar: Panas banget = panas sekali. Banget is everyday Jakarta-flavored speech.

target: Aku senang banget akhirnya kamu bisa ikut liburan bareng.
english: I'm so happy you can finally come along on the trip.
grammar: Senang banget = senang sekali (so happy). In writing use sangat/sekali.

target: Harga kamar hotel itu mahal banget waktu musim liburan.
english: That hotel room is really expensive during holiday season.
grammar: Mahal banget = mahal sekali (so expensive) — heard everywhere in speech.

target: Dia pintar banget matematika, selalu juara di kelasnya.
english: She's really good at math, always top of her class.
grammar: Pintar banget = pintar sekali. Banget = spoken 'very'.

target: Filmnya seru banget, kami sampai lupa waktu.
english: The movie was so exciting we completely lost track of time.
grammar: Seru banget = seru sekali (so much fun). Casual intensifier.

target: Kopi di kedai baru itu pahit banget menurutku.
english: The coffee at that new cafe is way too bitter, if you ask me.
grammar: Pahit banget = pahit sekali. In writing use sekali or sangat.

target: Gimana kabar orang tuamu di kampung?
english: How are your parents doing back in the village?
grammar: Gimana = bagaimana (how): gimana kabar…? = bagaimana kabar…?

target: Gimana kalau kita berangkat lebih pagi supaya tidak kena macet?
english: How about we leave earlier so we don't get stuck in traffic?
grammar: Gimana kalau…? = bagaimana kalau…? ('how about…?'). Spoken form.

target: Terus gimana hasil wawancara kerjamu kemarin?
english: So how did your job interview go yesterday?
grammar: Gimana hasilnya? = bagaimana hasilnya? Everyday spoken 'how'.

target: Gimana caranya pesan taksi lewat aplikasi ini?
english: How do you order a taxi through this app?
grammar: Gimana caranya? = bagaimana caranya? ('how do I…?'). Casual speech.

target: Kalau tiba-tiba hujan deras, gimana kita pulangnya?
english: If it suddenly pours, how are we getting home?
grammar: Gimana pulangnya? = bagaimana pulangnya? — spoken register.

target: Gimana rasanya tinggal jauh dari keluarga untuk pertama kali?
english: What's it like living far from family for the first time?
grammar: Gimana rasanya? = bagaimana rasanya? ('what's it like?').

target: Jangan bicara gitu ke adikmu, nanti dia sedih.
english: Don't talk like that to your little sibling, you'll make her sad.
grammar: Gitu = begitu (like that): bicara gitu = bicara begitu.

target: Kalau gitu, kita ketemu langsung di restoran jam delapan.
english: In that case, let's just meet at the restaurant at eight.
grammar: Kalau gitu = kalau begitu ('in that case'). Spoken shortening.

target: Cuacanya gini terus dari pagi, mendung tapi belum hujan.
english: The weather's been like this since morning, overcast but no rain yet.
grammar: Gini = begini (like this): cuacanya gini = the weather's like this.

target: Caranya gini: tekan tombol hijau, lalu pilih bahasa.
english: Here's how: press the green button, then choose a language.
grammar: Gini opens explanations: caranya gini = 'here's how'. Spoken begini.

target: Dari dulu memang gitu, pasar ini selalu ramai hari Minggu.
english: It's always been that way, this market is always packed on Sundays.

target: Dia memang suka bercanda gitu, jangan tersinggung.
english: He just likes to joke around like that, don't take offense.
grammar: Sentence-final gitu ≈ 'like that, you know'. Spoken begitu.

target: Kalau macet gini, lebih baik kita lewat jalan kecil.
english: With traffic jammed like this, we're better off taking the small roads.
grammar: Macet gini = macet begini (jammed like this). Gini/gitu = spoken begini/begitu.

target: Dia sering pulang larut gitu, ibunya sampai khawatir.
english: He often comes home late like that; his mom's getting worried.

target: Suaranya kayak penyanyi terkenal, padahal dia cuma karyawan biasa.
english: His voice is like a famous singer's, even though he's just a regular employee.
grammar: Kayak = seperti (like): kayak penyanyi = seperti penyanyi.

target: Rasanya kayak sup buatan ibuku di rumah.
english: It tastes like the soup my mom makes at home.

target: Kamu kelihatan lelah, kayak belum tidur semalaman.
english: You look worn out, like you haven't slept all night.

target: Langitnya gelap, kayaknya sebentar lagi hujan deras.
english: The sky's dark; looks like it's going to pour any minute.
grammar: Kayaknya = 'looks like/seems': kayaknya hujan = sepertinya hujan.

target: Kamu lagi ngapain di dapur malam-malam begini?
english: What are you doing in the kitchen this late at night?
grammar: Ngapain = spoken 'doing what?': lagi ngapain? = sedang apa?

target: Ngapain kamu bawa payung? Di luar cerah begini.
english: Why'd you bring an umbrella? It's perfectly sunny out.
grammar: Ngapain + verb = 'why bother': ngapain bawa payung? = why bring an umbrella?

target: Dia tanya aku lagi ngapain akhir pekan ini.
english: She asked what I was up to this weekend.
grammar: Lagi ngapain = 'up to what': spoken for sedang melakukan apa.

target: Ngapain beli yang mahal kalau yang murah juga bagus?
english: Why buy the expensive one when the cheap one is just as good?
grammar: Ngapain beli…? = 'why on earth buy…?' — casual why-bother question.

target: Anak-anak ngapain di halaman? Ramai sekali suaranya.
english: What are the kids doing in the yard? They're being so loud.
grammar: Anak-anak ngapain? = what are the kids doing? Spoken 'sedang apa'.

target: Ngapain menunggu lama-lama kalau bisa pesan lewat aplikasi?
english: Why wait around forever when you can order through the app?
grammar: Ngapain menunggu? = why bother waiting? Ngapain questions the point.

target: Bantu aku angkat kardus ini dong, berat sekali.
english: Come on, help me lift this box, it's really heavy.
grammar: Dong softens requests: bantu dong = 'come on, help me'. Spoken only.

target: Pelan-pelan dong, aku belum selesai mencatat alamatnya.
english: Slow down, will you — I haven't finished writing down the address.
grammar: Dong adds friendly pressure: pelan-pelan dong = 'slow down, will you'.

target: Cerita dong, liburanmu di Bali kemarin seru tidak?
english: Come on, tell me — was your Bali trip fun or not?
grammar: Dong invites: cerita dong = 'come on, tell me'.

target: Coba deh makan di warung sate dekat stasiun itu.
english: Go on, try eating at that satay stall near the station.
grammar: Deh nudges a suggestion: coba deh = 'go on, try it'.

target: Besok aku ganti uangmu, janji deh.
english: I'll pay you back tomorrow — I promise, really.
grammar: Sentence-final deh = 'really/I mean it': janji deh = I promise.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, aku berangkat sendiri deh.
english: If you're busy, fine, I'll just head out on my own then.
grammar: Deh marks giving in: aku sendiri deh = 'fine, I'll go alone then'.

target: Kok kamu belum siap? Kita harus berangkat sekarang.
english: How come you're not ready yet? We have to leave now.
grammar: Kok opens surprised questions: kok belum siap? = how come you're not ready?

target: Tenang, obatnya tidak pahit kok, anak kecil juga mau.
english: Don't worry, the medicine isn't bitter, really — even little kids take it.
grammar: Sentence-final kok reassures: tidak pahit kok = 'it's not bitter, really'.

target: Kok tiba-tiba listriknya mati, padahal tidak hujan?
english: How come the power suddenly went out when it isn't even raining?
grammar: Kok = puzzled 'how come': kok mati? = how come it went out?

target: Kamu ini kenapa sih, dari tadi diam terus?
english: What is it with you, you've been silent this whole time?
grammar: Sih sharpens a question: kenapa sih? = 'what IS it with you?'

target: Enak sih, tapi porsinya kecil untuk harga segitu.
english: It IS tasty, sure, but the portion is small for that price.
grammar: Sih concedes before a 'but': enak sih, tapi… = it IS tasty, but…

target: Siapa sih yang taruh sepatu basah di dalam rumah?
english: Who on earth put wet shoes inside the house?
grammar: Siapa sih…? = 'who on earth…?' — sih adds exasperation.

target: Entar sore aku mampir ke rumahmu bawa oleh-oleh.
english: Later this afternoon I'll drop by your place with some souvenirs.
grammar: Entar = nanti (later): entar sore = nanti sore.

target: Ntar dulu, aku masih cari kunci motor di tas.
english: Hold on a sec, I'm still looking for the motorbike key in my bag.
grammar: Ntar dulu = nanti dulu ('hold on a sec'). Ntar/entar = spoken nanti.

target: Jangan lupa entar malam kita telepon nenek bareng-bareng.
english: Don't forget, tonight we're calling Grandma together.

target: Kalau ntar hujan, acaranya pindah ke dalam aula.
english: If it rains later, the event moves inside the hall.

target: Dia emang jago masak, semua tamu minta tambah.
english: He really is a great cook — all the guests asked for seconds.
grammar: Emang = memang (really/indeed): emang jago = memang jago.

target: Emang kamu yakin tokonya buka hari libur begini?
english: Are you really sure the shop is open on a holiday like this?
grammar: Question-opening emang = memang: 'is it really true that…?'

target: Jalannya emang sempit, tapi pemandangannya luar biasa.
english: The road IS narrow, but the view is incredible.

target: Emang murah di pasar itu, tapi harus pintar menawar.
english: It really is cheap at that market, but you have to be good at bargaining.

target: Aku ke bioskop sama teman kantor habis pulang kerja.
english: I went to the movies with some coworkers after getting off work.
grammar: Spoken sama = dengan (with): sama teman = dengan teman.

target: Dia tinggal sama neneknya sejak kecil di Bogor.
english: She's lived with her grandmother in Bogor since she was little.

target: Jangan lupa foto sama keluarga sebelum pesawat berangkat.
english: Don't forget to take a photo with the family before the plane leaves.

target: Aku setuju sama pendapatmu soal jadwal baru itu.
english: I agree with your take on that new schedule.
grammar: After verbs, sama = dengan: setuju sama = setuju dengan (agree with).

target: Teman saya di Jakarta bilang, "Gue tunggu lo di depan halte."
english: My friend in Jakarta said, "I'll wait for you in front of the bus stop." (street-casual)
grammar: Jakarta slang pronouns: gue = saya, lo = kamu. Heard constantly; never use with elders.

target: Di film itu tokohnya berteriak, "Lo semua harus dengar gue!"
english: In that movie the character shouts, "All of you have to listen to me!" (street-casual)
grammar: Gue/lo (I/you) are Jakarta street pronouns — fine among close friends, rude to strangers.

target: Yuk berangkat sekarang, soalnya jalanan mulai ramai.
english: Come on, let's head out now, because the roads are getting busy.
grammar: Yuk invites: yuk berangkat = 'come on, let's go'. Softer cousin of ayo.

target: Kamu bawa payung kan? Langitnya mendung dari tadi.
english: You brought an umbrella, right? The sky's been overcast for a while.
grammar: Tag kan seeks agreement: bawa kan? = 'you brought it, right?'

target: Aku cuma mau tanya jadwal kereta terakhir ke Bogor.
english: I just want to ask about the last train to Bogor.

target: Nih, aku bawakan mangga dari kebun tetangga.
english: Here, I brought you some mangoes from the neighbor's garden.
grammar: Nih presents something at hand: nih = 'here (you go)'.

target: Tuh lihat, antreannya panjang sampai ke pintu depan.
english: Look at that — the line goes all the way to the front door.
grammar: Tuh points away from you: tuh lihat = 'look at that over there'.

target: Kita nonton film yang baru itu yuk, katanya seru.
english: Let's watch that new movie — people say it's great.
grammar: Nonton = spoken menonton (watch): nonton film = menonton film.

target: Aku ngobrol lama dengan sopir taksi soal harga bensin.
english: I chatted for a long time with the taxi driver about fuel prices.
grammar: Ngobrol = spoken 'to chat' (root obrol): ngobrol = mengobrol.

target: Habis makan siang, kita langsung rapat di lantai tiga ya.
english: After lunch we go straight into the meeting on the third floor, okay?

target: Duh, aku ketinggalan dompet di rumah lagi.
english: Ugh, I left my wallet at home again.

target: Motorku mogok di tengah jalan, aku dorong sampai bengkel.
english: My motorbike broke down mid-road; I pushed it all the way to the repair shop.

target: Telepon ibumu dulu, dia dari tadi cari kamu.
english: Call your mom first — she's been looking for you for a while.

target: Wah, rambutmu beda, potong di mana kemarin?
english: Whoa, your hair looks different — where did you get it cut?

target: Jangan buru-buru, keretanya baru datang setengah jam lagi.
english: No rush, the train doesn't arrive for another half hour.

target: Aku telat bangun, jadi lari ke halte tanpa sarapan.
english: I overslept, so I ran to the bus stop without breakfast.
grammar: Telat = spoken terlambat (late): telat bangun = overslept.

target: Titip beli air minum ya, aku tunggu di sini.
english: Grab me some drinking water, would you — I'll wait here.
grammar: Titip = 'get me…while you're at it': titip beli air = grab me some water.

target: Kabarnya kantor kita pindah gedung bulan depan, kamu tahu?
english: Word is our office is moving buildings next month — did you know?

target: Ayo cepat, filmnya mulai lima menit lagi.
english: Come on, hurry, the movie starts in five minutes.

target: Anakku susah makan sayur, maunya ayam goreng terus.
english: My kid won't eat vegetables — all he ever wants is fried chicken.

target: Tadi malam listrik mati dua jam, jadi kami mengobrol di teras.
english: Last night the power was out for two hours, so we chatted on the porch.

target: Besok libur, mendingan kita ke pantai pagi-pagi.
english: Tomorrow's a day off — better we hit the beach early.
grammar: Mendingan = spoken 'better (to)': mendingan pulang = better just go home.

target: Aku belum sempat cuci motor, kotornya minta ampun.
english: I haven't had a chance to wash the motorbike; it's unbelievably dirty.
grammar: Minta ampun after a quality = 'unbelievably': kotornya minta ampun.

target: Pelayan, tolong tambah sambal dan satu es teh manis.
english: Waiter, more sambal please, and one sweet iced tea.

target: Ternyata warung langgananku tutup, padahal aku sudah lapar sekali.
english: Turns out my usual food stall was closed, and I was already starving.

target: Kamu duluan ya, aku masih tunggu paket datang.
english: You go ahead — I'm still waiting for a package to arrive.
grammar: Duluan = spoken 'first/ahead': kamu duluan = you go first.

target: Hati-hati bawa motornya, rem belakangnya kurang pakem.
english: Careful riding the motorbike — the rear brake doesn't bite well.
grammar: Pakem = slangy 'grippy/sharp' for brakes: remnya pakem = the brakes bite well.

target: Seharian aku bolak-balik antara bank dan kantor pos.
english: I spent all day going back and forth between the bank and the post office.

target: Adikku baru lulus, sekarang sibuk cari kerja di Jakarta.
english: My little sister just graduated; now she's busy job-hunting in Jakarta.

target: Parkir di sini bayar berapa sejam, bang?
english: How much is parking here per hour, bro?
grammar: Bang (from abang) = 'bro/mister' for young men: bang, berapa? Casual address.

target: Bu, kembaliannya kurang dua ribu, tolong dihitung lagi.
english: Ma'am, the change is two thousand short — please count it again.

target: Malam ini aku menginap di rumah teman dekat kampus.
english: Tonight I'm staying over at a friend's place near campus.

target: Jangan main ponsel terus, matamu bisa sakit.
english: Stop playing on your phone all the time — your eyes will hurt.

target: Kapan-kapan kita coba kafe baru di ujung jalan itu.
english: Sometime we should try that new cafe at the end of the street.
grammar: Kapan-kapan = vague 'sometime': kapan-kapan kita ketemu = let's meet up sometime.

target: Tolong angkat jemuran, sepertinya sebentar lagi hujan.
english: Please bring in the laundry — looks like it's about to rain.

target: Aku baru sadar uang di dompetku tinggal dua puluh ribu.
english: I just realized I only have twenty thousand left in my wallet.

target: Katanya besok ada demo, jalan utama ditutup sampai sore.
english: They say there's a protest tomorrow — the main road is closed until evening.

target: Pak, lewat jalan belakang bisa tembus ke stasiun tidak?
english: Sir, does the back road cut through to the station?
grammar: Tembus = 'cuts through to': bisa tembus ke stasiun = comes out at the station.

target: Anak tetangga ribut terus dari pagi, aku jadi susah fokus.
english: The neighbor's kids have been rowdy since morning; now I can't focus.
grammar: Susah = spoken sulit: susah fokus = sulit fokus (hard to focus).

target: Santai, pesawat kita masih lama, ruang tunggunya juga nyaman.
english: Relax, our flight isn't for a while, and the waiting room is comfortable anyway.

target: Kamu dengar suara itu? Sepertinya ada kucing di atap.
english: Did you hear that sound? I think there's a cat on the roof.

target: Gara-gara hujan deras, sepatuku basah semua.
english: Thanks to the downpour, my shoes got completely soaked.
grammar: Gara-gara = 'because of' (with blame): gara-gara macet = all because of the jam.

target: Untung kamu ingatkan, aku hampir lupa bayar listrik bulan ini.
english: Good thing you reminded me — I almost forgot to pay the electric bill this month.

target: KTP saya hilang minggu lalu, sekarang saya harus mengurus kartu pengganti.
english: My ID card went missing last week; now I have to sort out a replacement card.
grammar: Mengurus = to take care of (paperwork): mengurus KTP baru = sort out a new ID card. THE bureaucracy verb.

target: Sebelum meminta KTP baru, saya harus melaporkan kehilangannya ke kantor polisi.
english: Before asking for a new ID card, I have to report the loss to the police station.

target: Petugas bilang blanko KTP sedang habis, jadi saya cuma dapat surat keterangan.
english: The clerk said the blank ID cards had run out, so I only got a certificate.
grammar: Surat keterangan = an official note standing in for a document: surat keterangan hilang = certificate of loss.

target: Foto di KTP saya sudah lama sekali, mukanya beda dengan sekarang.
english: The photo on my ID card is really old; the face looks different from now.

target: Alamat di KTP saya masih alamat rumah lama di Bandung.
english: The address on my ID card is still my old home address in Bandung.

target: Kalau pindah rumah, data di kartu keluarga juga harus diubah.
english: If you move house, the data on the family card has to be changed too.
grammar: Kartu keluarga (KK) lists every household member — data di KK harus diubah = the KK data must be changed.

target: Kartu keluarga kami belum diubah setelah adik saya lahir.
english: Our family card hasn't been changed yet since my younger sibling was born.

target: Nama anak baru bisa masuk kartu keluarga setelah akta kelahirannya jadi.
english: A child's name can only go on the family card after their birth certificate is ready.
grammar: Jadi also means 'ready, done' for documents: aktanya sudah jadi = the certificate is ready.

target: Saya mengantre dari jam tujuh pagi untuk mencetak ulang KTP yang rusak.
english: I've been queuing since seven in the morning to reprint my damaged ID card.

target: KTP saya patah jadi dua karena dompet sering diduduki.
english: My ID card snapped in two because my wallet often gets sat on.

target: Petugas memeriksa data saya, lalu bilang semuanya sudah cocok.
english: The clerk checked my data, then said everything already matched.

target: Data e-KTP saya harus direkam ulang karena fotonya buram.
english: My e-KTP data has to be recorded again because the photo is blurry.

target: Kata petugas, KTP elektronik sekarang berlaku seumur hidup.
english: According to the clerk, the electronic ID card is now valid for life.
grammar: Seumur hidup = for life: berlaku seumur hidup = valid for life. Umur = age, lifetime.

target: Sistemnya sedang ada gangguan, jadi saya disuruh balik lagi besok.
english: The system is having problems, so I was told to come back again tomorrow.
grammar: Balik lagi besok = come back again tomorrow — the classic counter phrase. Balik = go back.

target: Ada satu angka yang salah di nomor KTP baru saya.
english: There's one wrong digit in my new ID card number.

target: Untung fotokopi KTP lama saya masih tersimpan di rumah.
english: Luckily a photocopy of my old ID card is still kept at home.

target: Untuk urusan surat pindah, saya harus meminta surat pengantar dari RT dulu.
english: For the moving papers, I first have to ask the RT for a cover letter.
grammar: RT is the neighborhood unit; its head (Pak RT) signs your surat pengantar = cover letter for paperwork.

target: Pak RT baru pulang kerja malam, jadi saya ke rumahnya setelah makan malam.
english: The RT head only gets home from work at night, so I went to his house after dinner.

target: Surat pengantar dari RT harus dicap dulu oleh RW sebelum dibawa ke kelurahan.
english: The cover letter from the RT has to be stamped by the RW first before being taken to the ward office.
grammar: Cap = official stamp: dicap = to get stamped. No cap, no service.

target: Kantor kelurahan buka jam delapan, tapi loketnya sering baru jalan jam sembilan.
english: The ward office opens at eight, but the counter often only gets going at nine.

target: Saya salah datang ke kecamatan, padahal suratnya diurus di kelurahan.
english: I went to the district office by mistake, even though the letter is handled at the ward office.

target: Ibu itu bingung karena disuruh bolak-balik antara kelurahan dan kecamatan.
english: That lady is confused because she was told to go back and forth between the ward and district offices.
grammar: Bolak-balik = back and forth: disuruh bolak-balik = told to go back and forth. Doubling adds repetition.

target: Petugas kelurahan meminta fotokopi kartu keluarga dua lembar.
english: The ward office clerk asked for two photocopies of the family card.

target: Berkas saya kurang satu, jadi harus balik lagi besok pagi.
english: My paperwork is one document short, so I have to come back again tomorrow morning.

target: Sebelum jam istirahat, ambil dulu nomor antrean di depan loket.
english: Before the break hour, first take a queue number in front of the counter.

target: Loket pelayanan tutup jam dua belas untuk istirahat siang.
english: The service counter closes at twelve for the midday break.

target: Surat keterangan domisili saya akhirnya jadi setelah tiga hari kerja.
english: My certificate of residence was finally ready after three working days.
grammar: Hari kerja = working day: tiga hari kerja = three working days — weekends don't count.

target: Tanda tangan lurah baru bisa didapat hari Senin karena beliau sedang dinas luar.
english: The ward head's signature can only be gotten on Monday because he is away on official duty.
grammar: Beliau = respectful he/she for elders and officials: beliau sedang rapat = he/she is in a meeting.

target: Semua berkas sudah lengkap, tinggal menunggu dipanggil petugas.
english: All the papers are complete; all that's left is waiting to be called by the clerk.
grammar: Tinggal + verb = all that's left is: tinggal menunggu = just have to wait.

target: Warga desa bisa meminta surat keterangan tidak mampu untuk biaya sekolah anak.
english: Villagers can request a low-income certificate for their children's school costs.

target: Paspor saya habis masa berlakunya bulan depan, harus segera diperpanjang.
english: My passport expires next month; it has to be renewed right away.
grammar: Masa berlaku = validity period: masa berlakunya habis = it has expired (lit. its validity is used up).

target: Sekarang antrean paspor diambil lewat aplikasi, bukan datang langsung ke kantor.
english: These days the passport queue slot is taken via an app, not by coming straight to the office.

target: Saya pilih jadwal wawancara paspor hari Kamis jam sepuluh pagi.
english: I picked a passport interview slot on Thursday at ten in the morning.

target: Jangan lupa bawa KTP asli dan kartu keluarga waktu mengurus paspor.
english: Don't forget to bring your original ID card and family card when sorting out your passport.

target: Petugas imigrasi menanyakan rencana perjalanan saya ke Jepang.
english: The immigration officer asked about my travel plans to Japan.

target: Setelah difoto dan diambil sidik jarinya, saya tinggal menunggu kabar dari kantor imigrasi.
english: After being photographed and fingerprinted, I just have to wait for word from the immigration office.
grammar: Sidik jari = fingerprint (lit. finger trace): diambil sidik jarinya = had their fingerprints taken.

target: Paspor baru bisa diambil empat hari kerja setelah pembayaran.
english: The new passport can be picked up four working days after payment.

target: Biaya paspor biasa lebih murah daripada paspor elektronik.
english: The fee for a regular passport is cheaper than an electronic passport.

target: Nama di paspor harus sama persis dengan nama di akta kelahiran.
english: The name in the passport has to be exactly the same as the name on the birth certificate.
grammar: Persis = exactly: sama persis = exactly the same. Stronger than plain sama.

target: Halaman paspor saya hampir penuh dengan cap dari berbagai negara.
english: My passport pages are almost full of stamps from various countries.

target: Anak di bawah umur perlu surat izin orang tua untuk membuat paspor.
english: A minor needs a parental permission letter to make a passport.

target: Kantor imigrasi penuh sekali menjelang musim haji dan liburan sekolah.
english: The immigration office is really packed ahead of the hajj season and school holidays.

target: Paspor lama tetap dikembalikan, tapi ujungnya sudah digunting.
english: The old passport is still returned, but its corner has been cut off.

target: Umur tujuh belas tahun sudah boleh bikin SIM di Indonesia.
english: At seventeen you're already allowed to get a driver's license in Indonesia.
grammar: Bikin = everyday 'make, get made': bikin SIM = get a license made. Casual but heard everywhere.

target: Sebelum tes, mata saya diperiksa dulu di klinik dekat kantor polisi.
english: Before the test, my eyes were checked first at a clinic near the police station.

target: Saya lulus ujian teori, tapi gagal di ujian praktik motor.
english: I passed the theory exam but failed the motorbike practical exam.

target: Jalur ujian praktiknya sempit sekali, banyak orang jatuh di belokan.
english: The practical test track is really narrow; lots of people fall at the curve.

target: Dia baru lulus ujian praktik setelah mencoba tiga kali.
english: He only passed the practical exam after trying three times.

target: SIM saya mati dua bulan lalu, jadi harus bikin baru dari awal.
english: My license expired two months ago, so I have to get a new one from scratch.
grammar: Documents 'die' in Indonesian: SIM saya mati = my license has expired. Habis works too.

target: Sekarang SIM bisa diperpanjang lewat mobil layanan SIM keliling dekat pasar.
english: Nowadays a license can be renewed through the mobile SIM service van near the market.
grammar: SIM keliling = mobile license-renewal van (keliling = go around). Renew without the police station.

target: Bawa SIM lama, KTP, dan hasil tes kesehatan waktu memperpanjang SIM.
english: Bring your old license, ID card, and health test results when renewing your license.

target: Foto dan sidik jari diambil lagi setiap kali memperpanjang SIM.
english: Your photo and fingerprints are taken again every time you renew your license.

target: Kalau menyetir mobil tanpa SIM, kamu bisa kena denda besar.
english: If you drive a car without a license, you can get a big fine.

target: SIM A untuk mobil, SIM C untuk sepeda motor.
english: A class-A license is for cars, a class-C license is for motorbikes.
grammar: SIM A = car license, SIM C = motorbike. Letters, not numbers, mark the classes.

target: Dompet saya ketinggalan di rumah, untung tidak ada razia hari ini.
english: My wallet got left at home; luckily there's no traffic check today.

target: Warung fotokopi di depan kantor kelurahan selalu ramai pagi hari.
english: The photocopy shop in front of the ward office is always busy in the morning.

target: Tolong fotokopi KTP ini tiga lembar, ya.
english: Please make three copies of this ID card, okay?

target: Semua berkas difotokopi dua kali, satu untuk arsip, satu untuk saya.
english: All the papers get photocopied twice: one set for the archive, one for me.

target: Surat pernyataan ini harus ditempel materai sepuluh ribu.
english: This statement letter has to have a ten-thousand duty stamp stuck on it.
grammar: Materai = duty stamp stuck on official statements to make them binding. Sold at post offices.

target: Materai bisa dibeli di kantor pos atau warung fotokopi.
english: Duty stamps can be bought at the post office or the photocopy shop.

target: Sebagian tanda tangan harus kena di atas materai.
english: Part of the signature has to land on the duty stamp.

target: Ijazah saya perlu dilegalisir di kampus sebelum dipakai melamar kerja.
english: My diploma needs to be certified at the campus before being used to apply for jobs.
grammar: Dilegalisir = certified as a true copy: ijazah dilegalisir kampus = diploma certified by the campus.

target: Mesin fotokopinya rusak, jadi saya jalan ke toko alat tulis di seberang.
english: The photocopier is broken, so I walked to the stationery shop across the street.

target: Simpan salinan semua dokumen penting di rumah dan di email.
english: Keep copies of all important documents at home and in your email.

target: Harga fotokopi di sini masih lima ratus rupiah per lembar.
english: The price of photocopies here is still five hundred rupiah per sheet.

target: Saya baru mendaftar BPJS Kesehatan lewat aplikasi di ponsel.
english: I just registered for BPJS health insurance through the app on my phone.
grammar: BPJS Kesehatan is the national health insurance; nearly every resident is a member.

target: Iuran BPJS dibayar sebelum tanggal sepuluh setiap bulan.
english: The BPJS premium is paid before the tenth of every month.

target: Kalau iuran telat, kartunya tidak bisa dipakai di rumah sakit.
english: If the premium is late, the card can't be used at the hospital.

target: Semua anggota keluarga harus didaftarkan BPJS, tidak bisa satu orang saja.
english: All family members have to be registered for BPJS; it can't be just one person.

target: Pilih dulu klinik terdekat sebagai tempat berobat pertama kamu.
english: First choose the nearest clinic as your primary place for treatment.
grammar: Berobat = to seek treatment: berobat ke klinik = go to the clinic for treatment. Obat = medicine.

target: Sebelum ke rumah sakit besar, pasien BPJS harus meminta rujukan dari klinik.
english: Before going to a big hospital, BPJS patients have to ask the clinic for a referral.
grammar: Rujukan = referral: meminta rujukan = ask for a referral. Clinic first, hospital second.

target: Kartu BPJS sekarang bisa ditunjukkan lewat aplikasi, tidak perlu kartu fisik.
english: The BPJS card can now be shown via the app; no physical card needed.

target: Kelas rawat BPJS menentukan kamar yang kamu dapat di rumah sakit.
english: Your BPJS care class determines the room you get at the hospital.

target: Bayi harus didaftarkan BPJS paling lambat dua puluh delapan hari setelah lahir.
english: Babies have to be registered for BPJS at the latest twenty-eight days after birth.

target: Nomor BPJS saya tertulis di belakang kartu lama.
english: My BPJS number is written on the back of the old card.

target: Kantor BPJS penuh di awal bulan, lebih baik datang siang.
english: The BPJS office is packed at the start of the month; better to come at midday.

target: Saya mau membuka rekening baru, syaratnya apa saja, ya?
english: I'd like to open a new account; what are the requirements?
grammar: Syarat = requirement: syaratnya apa saja? = what are the requirements? Ask this before any queue.

target: Cukup bawa KTP dan uang setoran awal seratus ribu rupiah.
english: Just bring your ID card and an initial deposit of one hundred thousand rupiah.

target: Petugas bank membantu saya mengisi formulir pembukaan rekening.
english: The bank clerk helped me fill in the account-opening form.

target: Pilih rekening tanpa biaya bulanan kalau tabungan kamu masih kecil.
english: Choose an account without monthly fees if your savings are still small.

target: Kartu ATM dan buku tabungan diberikan langsung hari itu juga.
english: The ATM card and savings book are handed over that very same day.
grammar: Hari itu juga = that very same day. Juga after a time phrase adds 'right then'.

target: Jangan kasih tahu nomor PIN kamu ke siapa pun, termasuk petugas bank.
english: Don't tell your PIN number to anyone at all, including bank staff.
grammar: Siapa pun = anyone at all: jangan kasih tahu siapa pun = don't tell anyone. Pun strengthens.

target: Saldo minimal rekening ini lima puluh ribu rupiah.
english: The minimum balance for this account is fifty thousand rupiah.

target: Kartu ATM saya tertelan mesin, jadi harus melapor ke kantor cabang.
english: My ATM card got swallowed by the machine, so I have to report it to the branch office.
grammar: Ter- marks accidents: tertelan = accidentally swallowed (by the machine), ketinggalan = left behind.

target: Rekening bisa diblokir sementara kalau kartunya hilang.
english: The account can be temporarily blocked if the card goes missing.

target: Sekarang membuka rekening juga bisa dari rumah lewat aplikasi bank.
english: These days opening an account can also be done from home through the bank's app.

target: Bunga tabungan biasa kecil sekali, hampir tidak terasa.
english: The interest on a regular savings account is tiny; you hardly notice it.

target: Transfer antar bank kena biaya dua ribu lima ratus rupiah.
english: Transfers between banks incur a fee of two thousand five hundred rupiah.

target: Mesin ATM di dekat kampus sering kehabisan uang di akhir pekan.
english: The ATM near campus often runs out of cash on weekends.

target: Simpan bukti transfer sampai uangnya benar-benar masuk.
english: Keep the transfer receipt until the money has really arrived.
grammar: Benar-benar = really, truly: benar-benar masuk = has really arrived. Doubling intensifies.

target: Visa turis saya cuma berlaku tiga puluh hari.
english: My tourist visa is only valid for thirty days.

target: Visa saya bisa diperpanjang satu kali di kantor imigrasi terdekat.
english: My visa can be extended once at the nearest immigration office.

target: Teman saya kena denda karena tinggal lewat dari batas visanya.
english: My friend got fined for staying past his visa limit.
grammar: Kena = to get hit with (bad things): kena denda = get fined, kena flu = catch the flu.

target: Untuk kerja di Indonesia, kamu perlu KITAS, bukan visa turis.
english: To work in Indonesia, you need a KITAS, not a tourist visa.
grammar: KITAS = temporary stay permit card for foreigners who work or live in Indonesia. Visa turis won't do.

target: KITAS karyawan asing biasanya diurus oleh perusahaan sponsor.
english: A foreign employee's KITAS is usually handled by the sponsoring company.

target: Proses perpanjangan visa makan waktu sekitar lima hari kerja.
english: The visa extension process takes about five working days.
grammar: Makan waktu = to take time (lit. eat time): prosesnya makan waktu lima hari = it takes five days.

target: Saya harus datang sendiri ke imigrasi untuk foto dan sidik jari.
english: I have to come to immigration in person for the photo and fingerprints.

target: Periksa dulu halaman kosong di paspor sebelum mengurus perpanjangan visa.
english: First check the blank pages in your passport before sorting out a visa extension.

target: Waktu visanya habis, dia keluar ke Singapura lalu masuk lagi.
english: When his visa ran out, he exited to Singapore and then came back in.

target: Petugas imigrasi meminta bukti tiket pulang dan alamat penginapan.
english: The immigration officer asked for proof of a return ticket and the address of my accommodation.

target: Biaya perpanjangan visa dibayar lewat kode pembayaran di bank.
english: The visa extension fee is paid via a payment code at the bank.

target: Pemegang KITAS bisa membuka rekening bank dan membuat SIM lokal.
english: KITAS holders can open a bank account and get a local driver's license.

target: Pendaftaran sekolah negeri dibuka bulan Juni setiap tahun.
english: Registration for public schools opens in June every year.

target: Kami mendaftarkan anak ke sekolah dekat rumah lewat jalur zonasi.
english: We registered our child at a school near home through the zoning track.
grammar: Jalur zonasi = school placement by home distance: lewat jalur zonasi = via the zoning track.

target: Syarat daftar SD antara lain akta kelahiran dan kartu keluarga.
english: The requirements for elementary school registration include a birth certificate and the family card.
grammar: Antara lain = among others: syaratnya antara lain KTP = the requirements include an ID card.

target: Umur anak minimal enam tahun untuk masuk kelas satu SD.
english: A child has to be at least six years old to enter first grade of elementary school.

target: Ibu itu menyiapkan rapor dan fotokopi ijazah untuk pendaftaran SMP anaknya.
english: That mother is preparing the report card and diploma photocopies for her child's junior high registration.

target: Pengumuman hasil seleksi bisa dilihat di papan sekolah atau situs resmi.
english: The selection results announcement can be seen on the school board or the official website.

target: Anak yang diterima harus mendaftar ulang paling lambat hari Jumat.
english: Children who are accepted have to re-register by Friday at the latest.
grammar: Daftar ulang = re-register to claim your seat (ulang = again). Miss it and the spot is gone.

target: Waktu daftar ulang, anak saya diukur untuk seragam sekolah baru.
english: At re-registration, my child was measured for the new school uniform.

target: Sekolah meminta pas foto anak ukuran tiga kali empat, dua lembar.
english: The school asked for two of the child's ID photos, size three by four.
grammar: Pas foto = ID photo; sizes are in cm: tiga kali empat = 3x4. Standard for every form.

target: Tahun ajaran baru dimulai pertengahan Juli setelah libur panjang.
english: The new school year starts in mid-July after the long holiday.

target: Kalau berkasnya kurang, panitia pendaftaran akan menghubungi lewat telepon.
english: If the papers are incomplete, the registration committee will get in touch by phone.

target: Orang tua murid baru diundang ke pertemuan perkenalan minggu depan.
english: Parents of new students are invited to an introduction meeting next week.

target: Ambil nomor antrean dari mesin, lalu duduk menunggu dipanggil.
english: Take a queue number from the machine, then sit and wait to be called.

target: Nomor antrean saya masih jauh, jadi saya sempat keluar mencari sarapan.
english: My queue number was still far off, so I had time to go out and find breakfast.

target: Loket empat memanggil nomor seratus dua, tapi orangnya sudah pergi.
english: Counter four called number one hundred two, but the person had already left.

target: Kalau nomormu terlewat, kamu harus mengambil nomor baru lagi.
english: If your number gets skipped, you have to take a new number again.
grammar: Terlewat = accidentally passed, missed: nomormu terlewat = your number got skipped.

target: Datang setengah jam sebelum kantor buka supaya dapat antrean awal.
english: Come half an hour before the office opens so you get an early queue spot.

target: Bapak di sebelah saya sudah tiga kali ke sini untuk berkas yang sama.
english: The man next to me has already been here three times for the same paperwork.

target: Petugasnya ramah, tapi aturannya memang tidak bisa ditawar.
english: The clerk is friendly, but the rules really can't be bargained with.

target: Jangan pakai jasa calo, biayanya jadi dua kali lipat.
english: Don't use a fixer's services; the cost becomes double.
grammar: Calo = tout who 'helps' with tickets or paperwork for a fee: pakai jasa calo = use a fixer.

target: Semua pengurusan dokumen di kantor ini sebenarnya gratis.
english: All document processing at this office is actually free.

target: Pelayanan hari ini sampai jam tiga saja karena ada rapat kantor.
english: Service today is only until three o'clock because there's an office meeting.

target: Akhirnya semua dokumen saya selesai, rasanya lega sekali.
english: Finally all my documents are done; it feels like such a relief.

target: Setiap tujuh belas Agustus, kampung kami mengadakan berbagai lomba untuk anak-anak dan orang dewasa.
english: Every seventeenth of August, our neighborhood holds various competitions for children and adults.
grammar: Independence Day is 17 Agustus; the whole festive season is called tujuh belasan.

target: Adik saya menang lomba makan kerupuk di lapangan dekat rumah kemarin sore.
english: My younger sibling won the cracker-eating contest at the field near the house yesterday afternoon.
grammar: Lomba makan kerupuk: eat a cracker hung on a string, hands behind your back — the classic race.

target: Bapak-bapak berusaha memanjat pohon pinang yang licin untuk mengambil hadiah di puncaknya.
english: The men try to climb the slippery areca-palm trunk to grab the prizes at its top.
grammar: Panjat pinang: teams climb a greased palm trunk for prizes tied at the top.

target: Anak-anak melompat dalam karung sampai garis akhir, dan penonton tertawa keras.
english: The children jump along in sacks to the finish line, and the spectators laugh loudly.

target: Sebelum lomba dimulai, kami mengikuti upacara bendera di lapangan kecamatan.
english: Before the races begin, we take part in the flag ceremony at the district field.

target: Warga kompleks bekerja sama memasang bendera merah putih di depan setiap rumah.
english: The residents of the complex work together putting up red-and-white flags in front of every house.

target: Ibu-ibu menghias gapura kampung dengan cat merah dan putih minggu lalu.
english: The neighborhood women decorated the kampung gateway with red and white paint last week.

target: Ayah dan paman ikut lomba tarik tambang melawan tim kampung sebelah.
english: Dad and my uncle join the tug-of-war against the team from the next kampung.

target: Tim ibu-ibu kalah tipis dalam lomba bakiak tahun ini.
english: The mothers' team lost narrowly in the wooden-clog race this year.
