target: Hadiah utama lomba tahun ini sepeda baru dari pak lurah.
english: This year's main competition prize is a new bicycle from the village head.

target: Setelah upacara, ayah mengajak kami menonton pawai budaya di alun-alun.
english: After the ceremony, Dad takes us to watch the cultural parade on the town square.

target: Anak saya membawa bendera kecil dan mengikuti karnaval sekolah dengan bangga.
english: My child carries a small flag and joins the school carnival proudly.

target: Malam sebelum tujuh belas Agustus, warga berkumpul untuk malam tirakatan di balai kampung.
english: The night before August seventeenth, residents gather for the tirakatan evening at the kampung hall.
grammar: Malam tirakatan: neighbors gather on the eve of the 17th for prayers, speeches, and snacks.

target: Kakek bercerita tentang masa perjuangan setiap kali melihat upacara di televisi.
english: Grandpa tells stories about the independence struggle every time he sees the ceremony on television.

target: Panitia lomba membagikan hadiah kepada para pemenang sore harinya.
english: The competition committee hands out prizes to the winners that afternoon.

target: Suasana kampung meriah sekali dengan umbul-umbul warna-warni di sepanjang jalan.
english: The kampung atmosphere is very festive with colorful banners all along the road.

target: Kami sekeluarga memakai baju merah putih saat acara tujuh belasan di kompleks.
english: Our whole family wears red-and-white clothes during the Independence Day event at the complex.

target: Ibu tertawa melihat adik gagal memasukkan pensil ke dalam botol.
english: Mom laughs watching my little sibling fail to get the pencil into the bottle.

target: Ayah menjadi juri lomba paduan suara antarwarga tahun ini.
english: Dad is a judge for the inter-neighborhood choir competition this year.

target: Setelah semua lomba selesai, warga makan bersama di halaman masjid.
english: After all the competitions are over, residents eat together in the mosque courtyard.

target: Spanduk bertuliskan Dirgahayu Republik Indonesia digantung di depan kantor kelurahan.
english: A banner reading 'Long Live the Republic of Indonesia' is hung in front of the ward office.
grammar: Dirgahayu = 'long live', banner language: Dirgahayu Republik Indonesia.

target: Nenek paling suka menonton lomba balap karung dari teras rumahnya.
english: Grandma likes watching the sack race most, from the terrace of her house.

target: Tahun depan giliran kampung kami mengatur seluruh acara tujuh belasan.
english: Next year it is our kampung's turn to organize the whole Independence Day program.

target: Selama bulan Ramadan, banyak warung tutup pada siang hari.
english: During the month of Ramadan, many food stalls are closed in the daytime.

target: Teman kantor saya bangun jam tiga pagi untuk makan sahur.
english: My office friend gets up at three in the morning to eat the pre-dawn meal.
grammar: Sahur = the pre-dawn meal before a fasting day; the set phrase is makan sahur.

target: Ibu membangunkan seluruh keluarga untuk sahur sebelum imsak.
english: Mom wakes the whole family for the pre-dawn meal before the imsak cut-off.
grammar: Imsak = the cut-off a few minutes before dawn prayer — stop eating then.

target: Banyak orang menunggu waktu buka puasa sambil jalan-jalan sore, namanya ngabuburit.
english: Many people wait for the fast-breaking time while strolling in the afternoon; it's called ngabuburit.
grammar: Ngabuburit (Sundanese) = pleasantly killing time before buka puasa: strolling, hunting snacks.

target: Kami berbuka puasa dengan kurma dan es buah di rumah nenek.
english: We break the fast with dates and iced fruit at Grandma's house.
grammar: Buka puasa = breaking the fast at sunset; berbuka is the everyday verb.

target: Menjelang sore, pedagang takjil memenuhi trotoar di depan sekolah.
english: Toward late afternoon, takjil vendors fill the sidewalk in front of the school.
grammar: Takjil = small sweets and snacks for breaking the fast, sold roadside every afternoon.

target: Adik saya baru belajar puasa setengah hari tahun ini.
english: My little sibling is just learning to fast half a day this year.

target: Setelah buka puasa, ayah dan kakak pergi tarawih di masjid dekat rumah.
english: After breaking the fast, Dad and my older sibling go to tarawih prayers at the mosque near home.
grammar: Tarawih = the extra evening prayers at the mosque on Ramadan nights.

target: Ibu memasak kolak pisang untuk menu buka puasa hari pertama.
english: Mom cooks banana kolak for the first day's fast-breaking menu.

target: Jalan raya sangat sepi saat orang-orang sedang berbuka di rumah masing-masing.
english: The main road is very quiet while people are breaking the fast in their own homes.

target: Selama puasa, rapat kantor biasanya digeser ke pagi hari.
english: During the fasting month, office meetings are usually shifted to the morning.

target: Dia tetap kuat bekerja seharian meskipun sedang berpuasa.
english: He still has the strength to work all day even though he is fasting.

target: Suara bedug dari masjid menandakan waktu berbuka sudah tiba.
english: The sound of the mosque drum signals that the time to break the fast has arrived.

target: Kami sering diundang buka puasa bersama di rumah teman ayah.
english: We are often invited to a group iftar at the house of Dad's friend.

target: Anak-anak berlatih menahan lapar dan haus sampai sore hari.
english: The children practice holding back hunger and thirst until late afternoon.

target: Pasar sore dadakan muncul di dekat stasiun selama bulan puasa.
english: An impromptu afternoon market pops up near the station during the fasting month.

target: Minggu terakhir Ramadan, ibu mengajak kami mencari baju baru di pusat perbelanjaan.
english: In the last week of Ramadan, Mom takes us to look for new clothes at the mall.

target: Malam takbiran, suara takbir terdengar dari masjid sampai pagi.
english: On takbiran night, the sound of the takbir can be heard from the mosques until morning.
grammar: Malam takbiran = the eve of Lebaran; takbir chants echo from mosques all night.

target: Kantor kami mengadakan buka puasa bersama di restoran Padang.
english: Our office holds a group iftar at a Padang restaurant.

target: Banyak orang membayar zakat di masjid pada akhir Ramadan.
english: Many people pay their alms at the mosque at the end of Ramadan.

target: Dua hari sebelum Lebaran, kami mudik ke kampung halaman ayah di Jawa Tengah.
english: Two days before Lebaran, we travel home to Dad's hometown in Central Java.

target: Karyawan biasanya menerima THR paling lambat seminggu sebelum hari raya.
english: Employees usually receive their holiday bonus at the latest a week before the holiday.
grammar: THR = Tunjangan Hari Raya, the holiday bonus: one month's salary, required by law.

target: Adik langsung membeli sepatu baru begitu THR ayah cair.
english: My little sibling buys new shoes right away as soon as Dad's holiday bonus comes through.
grammar: Cair (lit. 'liquid') = paid out: THR cair — the money has landed.

target: Pagi hari raya, kami ikut salat Idulfitri di lapangan dekat rumah.
english: On the holiday morning, we join the Eid prayer at the field near the house.

target: Setelah salat, kami sungkeman kepada kakek dan nenek di ruang tamu.
english: After the prayer, we do the sungkeman to Grandpa and Grandma in the living room.
grammar: Sungkeman: kneeling before elders to ask forgiveness — the tearjerker of Lebaran morning.

target: Ibu menyiapkan ketupat, opor ayam, dan sambal goreng ati sejak subuh.
english: Mom prepares ketupat, chicken opor, and spicy fried liver from before dawn.

target: Ketupat buatan nenek selalu lebih padat daripada buatan kami.
english: Grandma's ketupat is always denser than the ones we make.
grammar: Ketupat: rice cakes boiled in woven palm-leaf pouches — Lebaran's signature food.

target: Kami berkeliling kompleks untuk bersilaturahmi dengan para tetangga.
english: We go around the complex to pay friendly visits to the neighbors.
grammar: Silaturahmi = keeping ties warm; bersilaturahmi is what all the visiting is called.

target: Anak-anak antre salaman sambil menerima amplop kecil dari om dan tante.
english: The kids line up to shake hands while receiving small envelopes from their uncles and aunts.

target: Toples nastar di meja tamu sudah setengah kosong sebelum siang.
english: The jar of nastar cookies on the guest table is already half empty before noon.

target: Kue kering buatan ibu selalu habis lebih dulu daripada yang dibeli di toko.
english: Mom's homemade cookies always run out sooner than the store-bought ones.

target: Kami mengucapkan mohon maaf lahir dan batin kepada semua saudara.
english: We say 'forgive me, outwardly and inwardly' to all our relatives.
grammar: Mohon maaf lahir dan batin ≈ 'forgive my wrongs, outward and inner' — the Lebaran formula.

target: Kantor kami mengadakan halal bihalal seminggu setelah libur Lebaran.
english: Our office holds a halal bihalal gathering a week after the Lebaran break.
grammar: Halal bihalal: a post-Lebaran gathering for mutual forgiveness, beloved by offices.

target: Acara halal bihalal keluarga besar tahun ini diadakan di rumah paman tertua.
english: This year's extended-family halal bihalal is held at the eldest uncle's house.

target: Menurut berita, arus balik tahun ini lebih padat daripada arus mudik.
english: According to the news, this year's return traffic is heavier than the outbound exodus.
grammar: Arus mudik = the outbound exodus; arus balik = the return wave. News-speak you'll hear daily.

target: Tiket kereta untuk mudik habis terjual dalam beberapa jam saja.
english: Train tickets for the homecoming sold out in just a few hours.

target: Nenek membagikan uang baru kepada semua cucunya setiap pagi Lebaran.
english: Grandma hands out crisp new banknotes to all her grandchildren every Lebaran morning.

target: Kami menukar uang lama dengan uang baru di bank sebelum mudik.
english: We exchange old bills for new ones at the bank before going home for the holiday.

target: Rumah kakek penuh dengan mobil saudara dari berbagai kota selama Lebaran.
english: Grandpa's house is full of relatives' cars from various cities during Lebaran.

target: Hari kedua Lebaran, keluarga besar berziarah ke makam kakek buyut.
english: On the second day of Lebaran, the extended family visits great-grandfather's grave.

target: Ibu memesan parsel berisi sirup dan kue untuk dikirim kepada tetangga lama.
english: Mom orders a hamper of syrup and cookies to be sent to an old neighbor.

target: Baju koko ayah masih bagus, tetapi dia tetap membeli satu lagi.
english: Dad's koko shirt is still in good shape, but he buys another one anyway.

target: Setiap Lebaran, berat badan saya naik karena opor dan rendang.
english: Every Lebaran my weight goes up because of the opor and rendang.

target: Grup keluarga penuh dengan kartu ucapan hari raya digital sejak subuh.
english: The family group chat has been full of digital holiday greeting cards since dawn.

target: Asisten rumah tangga kami pulang kampung, jadi rumah agak berantakan.
english: Our household helper has gone back to her village, so the house is a bit of a mess.

target: Jakarta terasa kosong saat semua orang merayakan Lebaran di kampung masing-masing.
english: Jakarta feels empty when everyone is celebrating Lebaran back in their own hometowns.

target: Saat Imlek, keluarga besar teman saya berkumpul untuk makan malam bersama.
english: At Chinese New Year, my friend's extended family gathers for dinner together.
grammar: Imlek = Chinese New Year — a public holiday in Indonesia since 2003.

target: Anak-anak yang belum menikah menerima angpao dari om dan tante mereka.
english: Children who are not yet married receive red envelopes from their uncles and aunts.
grammar: Angpao: red envelopes of cash at Imlek — married adults give, unmarried receive.

target: Kami mengajak anak-anak menonton pertunjukan barongsai di pusat perbelanjaan.
english: We take the kids to watch a lion dance performance at the shopping center.
grammar: Barongsai = the Chinese lion dance; malls book troupes all through Imlek.

target: Lampion merah digantung di sepanjang jalan menuju kelenteng tua itu.
english: Red lanterns are hung all along the road leading to the old Chinese temple.

target: Ibu teman saya membuat kue keranjang untuk dibagikan kepada para tetangga.
english: My friend's mother makes sticky rice cakes to hand out to the neighbors.
grammar: Kue keranjang: sticky sweet rice cake — Imlek's must-have, like ketupat at Lebaran.

target: Menurut teman saya, hujan saat Imlek dianggap membawa rezeki.
english: According to my friend, rain at Chinese New Year is considered to bring good fortune.

target: Toko kue itu menerima pesanan kue keranjang sejak sebulan sebelumnya.
english: That bakery takes orders for sticky rice cakes from a month beforehand.

target: Seluruh keluarga memakai baju berwarna merah saat makan malam Imlek.
english: The whole family wears red clothes at the Chinese New Year dinner.

target: Kantor teman saya tutup dua hari karena perayaan Imlek jatuh pada hari Senin.
english: My friend's office is closed for two days because Imlek falls on a Monday.

target: Dia mengucapkan selamat tahun baru Imlek kepada tetangganya sambil tersenyum.
english: She wishes her neighbor a happy Chinese New Year with a smile.

target: Keluarga tante saya menghias pohon Natal besar di ruang tamu mereka.
english: My aunt's family decorates a big Christmas tree in their living room.

target: Kami menghadiri ibadah malam Natal di gereja dekat rumah nenek.
english: We attend the Christmas Eve service at the church near Grandma's house.

target: Anak-anak membuka kado Natal mereka pagi-pagi sekali tanggal dua puluh lima.
english: The children open their Christmas presents very early on the twenty-fifth.

target: Ibu memasak ayam panggang khusus untuk makan malam Natal.
english: Mom cooks roast chicken specially for Christmas dinner.

target: Toko-toko memutar lagu Natal sejak awal bulan Desember.
english: The shops have been playing Christmas songs since the beginning of December.

target: Malam tahun baru, kami membakar jagung dan sate di halaman belakang.
english: On New Year's Eve, we grill corn and satay in the backyard.
grammar: Bakar jagung — grilling corn with the neighbors — is the default New Year's Eve plan.

target: Suara terompet kertas anak-anak ramai sekali menjelang tengah malam.
english: The sound of the children's paper horns gets really noisy toward midnight.

target: Kembang api menyala di langit kota tepat jam dua belas malam.
english: Fireworks light up the city sky exactly at twelve o'clock at night.
grammar: Spoken time uses jam: jam dua belas malam = 12 at night. Pukul is for announcements.

target: Kami menonton pesta kembang api dari atap gedung apartemen teman.
english: We watch the fireworks show from the roof of a friend's apartment building.

target: Jalan menuju Puncak macet total setiap malam tahun baru.
english: The road to Puncak is completely jammed every New Year's Eve.
grammar: Puncak = the mountain resort area south of Jakarta; macet total every long weekend.

target: Tahun ini resolusi saya lebih sederhana: tidur cukup dan olahraga teratur.
english: This year my resolution is simpler: enough sleep and regular exercise.

target: Kami begadang sampai pagi sambil main kartu dan makan jagung bakar.
english: We stay up till morning playing cards and eating grilled corn.

target: Beberapa keluarga memilih menginap di vila untuk menyambut tahun baru.
english: Some families choose to stay at a villa to welcome the new year.

target: Petasan berbunyi di mana-mana sampai bayi tetangga terbangun dan menangis.
english: Firecrackers go off everywhere until the neighbor's baby wakes up and cries.

target: Pagi tahun baru, jalanan penuh sampah sisa perayaan semalam.
english: On New Year's morning, the streets are full of trash left from last night's celebration.

target: Saat Nyepi, seluruh pulau Bali benar-benar sunyi selama satu hari penuh.
english: During Nyepi, the whole island of Bali goes completely silent for a full day.
grammar: Nyepi = Bali's Day of Silence: no lights, no travel, no work, for a full day.

target: Bandara di Bali tutup total selama Nyepi, jadi periksa jadwal penerbanganmu.
english: The airport in Bali closes completely during Nyepi, so check your flight schedule.
grammar: For Nyepi even the airport shuts — Bali's is the only one in the world that does.

target: Turis harus tetap berada di dalam hotel selama hari raya Nyepi.
english: Tourists must stay inside their hotels throughout the Nyepi holiday.

target: Malam sebelum Nyepi, pawai ogoh-ogoh memenuhi jalan-jalan di Denpasar.
english: The night before Nyepi, ogoh-ogoh parades fill the streets of Denpasar.
grammar: Ogoh-ogoh: giant demon figures paraded on Nyepi eve, then usually burned.

target: Anak-anak muda mengarak ogoh-ogoh raksasa buatan banjar mereka.
english: The young people parade the giant ogoh-ogoh built by their neighborhood association.

target: Kami memesan kamar hotel dengan makanan lengkap karena semua restoran tutup.
english: We book a hotel room with full meals because all the restaurants are closed.

target: Lampu-lampu di seluruh desa dimatikan, dan langit malam penuh bintang.
english: The lights across the whole village are turned off, and the night sky is full of stars.

target: Layanan internet di ponsel juga dimatikan selama hari Nyepi.
english: Mobile internet service is switched off as well during Nyepi day.
grammar: Since 2018 even mobile internet is off during Nyepi — download your maps early.

target: Sehari setelah Nyepi, warga saling berkunjung untuk bermaaf-maafan.
english: The day after Nyepi, residents visit one another to exchange apologies.

target: Sebelum Nyepi, umat Hindu melakukan upacara Melasti di pantai.
english: Before Nyepi, Hindu worshippers perform the Melasti ceremony on the beach.

target: Teman saya sengaja datang ke Bali untuk merasakan suasana Nyepi.
english: My friend comes to Bali on purpose to experience the atmosphere of Nyepi.

target: Hotel kami menyiapkan kegiatan meditasi dan yoga selama hari sunyi itu.
english: Our hotel prepares meditation and yoga activities during the day of silence.

target: Kami merencanakan pesta kejutan untuk ulang tahun ibu bulan depan.
english: We are planning a surprise party for Mom's birthday next month.

target: Semua tamu bersembunyi di ruang tamu sebelum ibu pulang kerja.
english: All the guests hide in the living room before Mom comes home from work.

target: Waktu lampu menyala, kami semua berteriak, dan ibu menangis terharu.
english: When the lights come on, we all shout, and Mom cries with emotion.

target: Sebelum meniup lilin, adik memejamkan mata dan mengucapkan harapan dalam hati.
english: Before blowing out the candles, my little sibling closes her eyes and makes a wish silently.
grammar: The tiup lilin ritual: close your eyes, make a wish, blow — and never tell the wish.

target: Tahun ini kakek meniup lilin angka delapan puluh dengan bantuan cucu-cucunya.
english: This year Grandpa blows out the number-eighty candle with his grandchildren's help.

target: Menurut kebiasaan kantor, yang berulang tahun wajib mentraktir teman-temannya.
english: By office custom, whoever has a birthday must treat their friends.
grammar: Birthday rule reversed: the birthday person treats everyone — dia yang mentraktir!

target: Teman-teman menaburkan tepung ke rambutnya setelah acara tiup lilin.
english: His friends sprinkle flour onto his hair after the candle-blowing.
grammar: Getting doused with flour (and eggs) on your birthday is an affectionate prank.

target: Sekretaris kantor memesan nasi tumpeng kuning untuk syukuran ulang tahun perusahaan.
english: The office secretary orders a yellow rice cone for the company's anniversary thanksgiving.
grammar: Tumpeng: a yellow rice cone for milestones; the first slice goes to the most honored guest.

target: Potongan tumpeng pertama diberikan kepada kakek sebagai tanda hormat.
english: The first slice of the tumpeng is given to Grandpa as a sign of respect.

target: Kami hanya merayakan ulang tahun anak dengan doa dan makan bersama.
english: We celebrate our child's birthday simply with a prayer and a meal together.

target: Kakak mengunggah foto masa kecil saya dengan ucapan panjang di media sosial.
english: My older sibling uploads my childhood photo with a long birthday message on social media.

target: Kado ulang tahun kakak dari ayah tahun ini tiket konser band favoritnya.
english: My older sibling's birthday present from Dad this year is a ticket to her favorite band's concert.

target: Keluarga kami mengadakan syukuran kecil setelah adik lulus kuliah.
english: Our family holds a small thanksgiving gathering after my younger sibling graduates from college.
grammar: Syukuran: a small thanksgiving meal for any good news — a degree, a house, a baby.

target: Tetangga mengundang kami ke syukuran rumah baru mereka besok malam.
english: The neighbors invite us to the housewarming blessing for their new house tomorrow night.

target: Sebelum pindah rumah, keluarga kami membagikan nasi kotak kepada para tetangga.
english: Before moving house, our family hands out boxed rice meals to the neighbors.

target: Acara tujuh bulanan kakak ipar dihadiri seluruh keluarga besar.
english: My sister-in-law's seventh-month pregnancy ceremony is attended by the whole extended family.
grammar: Tujuh bulanan: the blessing ceremony held in the seventh month of a pregnancy.

target: Di kampung ayah, panen besar juga dirayakan dengan makan bersama di sawah.
english: In Dad's village, a big harvest is also celebrated with a shared meal in the rice fields.

target: Kalender Indonesia penuh hari libur karena semua agama besar dirayakan.
english: The Indonesian calendar is full of holidays because all the major religions are celebrated.
grammar: Indonesia's calendar marks the holidays of six religions — everyone shares the days off.

target: Setiap perayaan di Indonesia hampir selalu berakhir dengan makan bersama keluarga.
english: Almost every celebration in Indonesia ends with a meal together with family.

target: Obat ini harus ditebus dengan resep dokter di apotek.
english: This medicine has to be filled with a doctor's prescription at the pharmacy.
grammar: Obat resep = prescription medicine: harus ditebus dengan resep = must be filled with a prescription.

target: Obat warung biasanya cukup untuk sakit kepala ringan seperti ini.
english: Corner-stall medicine is usually enough for a mild headache like this.
grammar: Obat warung = cheap over-the-counter meds from corner stalls, sold per strip — no resep needed.

target: Apoteker menjelaskan aturan pakai obat ini dengan sangat sabar.
english: The pharmacist explains this medicine's directions for use very patiently.

target: Sirup obat batuk ini harus dikocok dulu sebelum diminum.
english: This cough syrup has to be shaken first before being drunk.
grammar: Dulu after a verb = 'first': dikocok dulu sebelum diminum = shaken first before drinking.

target: Anak saya lebih suka obat sirup daripada tablet karena rasanya manis.
english: My child prefers syrup medicine to tablets because it tastes sweet.

target: Salep ini dioleskan tipis-tipis pada kulit yang gatal dua kali sehari.
english: This ointment is applied thinly on the itchy skin twice a day.
grammar: Doubling an adjective = 'in that manner': dioleskan tipis-tipis = spread on thinly.

target: Minum tablet ini sesudah makan supaya lambung kamu tidak perih.
english: Take this tablet after eating so your stomach doesn't sting.

target: Jangan melebihi dosis yang tertulis di kemasan obat itu.
english: Don't exceed the dose written on that medicine's packaging.

target: Apotek dekat rumah kami buka dua puluh empat jam setiap hari.
english: The pharmacy near our house is open twenty-four hours every day.

target: Saya perlu membeli vitamin dan obat tetes mata di apotek.
english: I need to buy vitamins and eye drops at the pharmacy.

target: Obat ini bisa membuat kamu mengantuk, jadi jangan menyetir setelah meminumnya.
english: This medicine can make you drowsy, so don't drive after taking it.

target: Kalau demamnya tidak turun dalam tiga hari, segera periksakan ke dokter.
english: If the fever doesn't go down in three days, have it checked by a doctor right away.
grammar: Periksakan = have it checked: periksakan ke dokter = take it to the doctor. The -kan asks it done.

target: Apoteker menyarankan obat generik karena harganya jauh lebih murah.
english: The pharmacist recommends the generic medicine because its price is much cheaper.
grammar: Obat generik = generic medicine, same content but cheaper: minta obat generik = ask for the generic.

target: Simpan sirup ini di kulkas setelah botolnya dibuka pertama kali.
english: Store this syrup in the fridge after the bottle is opened for the first time.

target: Ibu selalu menyimpan kotak obat kecil di lemari dapur untuk keadaan darurat.
english: Mom always keeps a small medicine box in the kitchen cupboard for emergencies.

target: Obat alergi ini hanya boleh diminum satu tablet per hari.
english: This allergy medicine may only be taken one tablet per day.

target: Saya lupa membawa resep, jadi apoteker tidak bisa memberikan obatnya.
english: I forgot to bring the prescription, so the pharmacist can't hand over the medicine.

target: Tolong tuliskan aturan pakai di label supaya nenek tidak bingung.
english: Please write the directions for use on the label so Grandma doesn't get confused.

target: Tolong panggil ambulans, ayah saya tiba-tiba jatuh pingsan di kamar mandi!
english: Please call an ambulance, my father suddenly fainted in the bathroom!
grammar: Tolong + verb = please (asking for help): tolong panggil ambulans = please call an ambulance.

target: Pasien kecelakaan itu langsung dibawa ke UGD rumah sakit terdekat.
english: That accident patient was taken straight to the ER of the nearest hospital.
grammar: UGD (Unit Gawat Darurat) = the ER; many hospitals label it IGD instead. Ke UGD = to the ER.

target: Perawat di IGD memeriksa tekanan darah dan denyut nadi saya.
english: The nurse in the ER checks my blood pressure and pulse.

target: Nomor darurat di Indonesia adalah seratus dua belas, mudah diingat.
english: The emergency number in Indonesia is one hundred twelve, easy to remember.
grammar: 112 is Indonesia's general emergency number: nomor darurat = emergency number.

target: Luka di dahinya cukup dalam sehingga harus dijahit lima jahitan.
english: The wound on his forehead is quite deep, so it has to be closed with five stitches.

target: Adik saya keracunan makanan laut dan muntah-muntah sepanjang malam.
english: My younger sibling got food poisoning from seafood and kept vomiting all night.

target: Dokter jaga memasang infus karena pasien itu kekurangan cairan.
english: The doctor on duty puts in an IV drip because that patient lacks fluids.

target: Jangan panik, tekan lukanya dengan kain bersih sampai pendarahan berhenti.
english: Don't panic, press the wound with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops.

target: Golongan darah saya O, jadi saya sering diminta mendonorkan darah.
english: My blood type is O, so I'm often asked to donate blood.

target: Kalau ada kebakaran, jangan memakai lift, turunlah lewat tangga darurat.
english: If there's a fire, don't use the elevator; go down via the emergency stairs.
grammar: -lah softens a command: turunlah lewat tangga = do go down the stairs.

target: Suami saya menelepon ambulans sambil menenangkan anak-anak yang ketakutan.
english: My husband calls the ambulance while calming the frightened children.

target: Petugas UGD bertanya obat apa saja yang sedang diminum pasien.
english: The ER staff asks what medicines the patient is currently taking.

target: Untung ada tetangga yang mengantar kami ke rumah sakit tengah malam.
english: Luckily there was a neighbor who drove us to the hospital in the middle of the night.
grammar: Untung at the start of a sentence = luckily: untung ada tetangga = luckily there was a neighbor.

target: Dia tersedak bakso, untung temannya tahu cara menolongnya.
english: He choked on a meatball; luckily his friend knew how to help him.

target: Sebelum ambulans datang, baringkan pasien dan longgarkan kerah bajunya.
english: Before the ambulance arrives, lay the patient down and loosen his shirt collar.

target: Kepalanya terbentur pintu mobil, sekarang dia merasa mual dan pusing.
english: His head hit the car door; now he feels nauseous and dizzy.

target: Adik menangis keras waktu disuntik di lengan kirinya.
english: My little sibling cries loudly when injected in his left arm.

target: Keluarga pasien menunggu dengan cemas di depan ruang operasi.
english: The patient's family waits anxiously in front of the operating room.

target: Sejak pagi saya merasa mual dan tidak nafsu makan sama sekali.
english: Since morning I have felt nauseous and have no appetite at all.

target: Nenek mengeluh sesak napas setiap kali naik tangga ke lantai dua.
english: Grandma complains of shortness of breath every time she climbs the stairs to the second floor.
grammar: Mengeluh = to complain (of): mengeluh sesak napas = complains of shortness of breath.

target: Saya alergi udang, wajah saya langsung bengkak sesudah memakannya.
english: I am allergic to shrimp; my face swells up right after eating it.

target: Kulit saya gatal dan muncul bintik merah setelah meminum obat baru itu.
english: My skin is itchy and red spots appeared after I took that new medicine.

target: Tenggorokan saya kering dan suara saya hampir hilang sejak kemarin.
english: My throat is dry and my voice has almost disappeared since yesterday.

target: Badan saya lemas dan kepala saya pusing seperti berputar.
english: My body is weak and my head is dizzy, like it's spinning.
grammar: Pusing covers both dizzy and stressed-out: kepala saya pusing = my head is spinning.

target: Anak itu demam tinggi dan menggigil meskipun sudah memakai selimut tebal.
english: That child has a high fever and is shivering even though he's already using a thick blanket.

target: Dokter bertanya sudah berapa lama saya merasakan nyeri di dada.
english: The doctor asks how long I have been feeling pain in my chest.

target: Perut saya kembung dan mulas setelah makan pedas semalam.
english: My stomach is bloated and crampy after eating spicy food last night.
grammar: Kembung = bloated, full of gas: perut kembung = a bloated belly.

target: Mata saya merah dan berair, mungkin karena debu di jalan.
english: My eyes are red and watery, maybe because of the dust on the road.

target: Dia batuk berdahak sudah seminggu, sebaiknya dia segera ke dokter.
english: He has had a phlegmy cough for a week already; he had better go to the doctor soon.

target: Telinga kanan saya berdenging sejak turun dari pesawat tadi malam.
english: My right ear has been ringing since I got off the plane last night.

target: Tekanan darah ayah naik lagi karena dia lupa meminum obatnya.
english: Dad's blood pressure went up again because he forgot to take his medicine.

target: Saya sulit tidur karena hidung tersumbat dan kepala terasa berat.
english: I have trouble sleeping because my nose is blocked and my head feels heavy.

target: Lutut saya bengkak setelah jatuh dari sepeda kemarin sore.
english: My knee is swollen after I fell off my bicycle yesterday afternoon.

target: Napasnya berbunyi seperti siulan, mungkin asmanya kambuh lagi.
english: His breathing sounds like whistling; maybe his asthma is flaring up again.
grammar: Kambuh = (an illness) flares up again: asmanya kambuh = his asthma is back.

target: Setiap musim hujan, alergi dingin saya kambuh dan kulit jadi gatal.
english: Every rainy season my cold allergy flares up and my skin gets itchy.

target: Dia mengalami mimisan tiba-tiba, mungkin karena cuaca terlalu panas.
english: He suddenly got a nosebleed, maybe because the weather is too hot.

target: Kartu BPJS saya tertinggal di rumah, untung ada versi digitalnya.
english: My BPJS card was left at home; luckily there is a digital version of it.
grammar: BPJS = Indonesia's national health insurance; nearly everyone carries the kartu BPJS = BPJS card.

target: Untuk berobat murah, warga biasanya datang dulu ke puskesmas dekat rumah.
english: For cheap medical treatment, residents usually go first to the puskesmas near their homes.
grammar: Puskesmas (pusat kesehatan masyarakat) = community health center, the cheap first stop for care.

target: Petugas puskesmas meminta saya mengambil nomor antrean di mesin.
english: The puskesmas staff asks me to take a queue number at the machine.

target: Tanpa surat rujukan dari puskesmas, BPJS tidak menanggung biaya rumah sakit.
english: Without a referral letter from the puskesmas, BPJS doesn't cover the hospital costs.
grammar: BPJS is tiered: you need a surat rujukan (referral letter) from the puskesmas before the hospital.

target: Ibu rutin memeriksakan gula darahnya di puskesmas setiap awal bulan.
english: Mom routinely has her blood sugar checked at the puskesmas at the start of every month.

target: Iuran BPJS keluarga kami dibayar otomatis lewat aplikasi bank.
english: Our family's BPJS premiums are paid automatically through the bank app.
grammar: Iuran = a regular membership fee: iuran BPJS = the monthly BPJS premium.

target: Antrean di puskesmas pagi ini panjang sekali sampai ke halaman.
english: The queue at the puskesmas this morning is really long, all the way to the yard.

target: Dokter puskesmas merujuk saya ke dokter spesialis kulit di rumah sakit.
english: The puskesmas doctor refers me to a skin specialist at the hospital.

target: Bidan di puskesmas memeriksa kandungan kakak saya setiap bulan.
english: The midwife at the puskesmas examines my older sister's pregnancy every month.

target: Anak-anak mendapat imunisasi gratis di posyandu dekat balai desa.
english: The children get free immunizations at the posyandu near the village hall.
grammar: Posyandu = neighborhood health post: monthly weigh-ins and shots for kids. Di posyandu = at the post.

target: Kelas BPJS menentukan jenis kamar rawat inap yang kamu dapat.
english: Your BPJS tier determines the type of inpatient room you get.

target: Saya harus memperbarui data alamat supaya kartu BPJS tetap aktif.
english: I have to update my address data so my BPJS card stays active.

target: Obat dari puskesmas gratis, kita hanya perlu menunjukkan kartu berobat.
english: Medicine from the puskesmas is free; we only need to show our patient card.

target: Puskesmas keliling datang ke kampung kami setiap hari Rabu pagi.
english: The mobile puskesmas comes to our neighborhood every Wednesday morning.

target: Pak RT membantu mengurus kartu BPJS untuk warga yang belum punya.
english: The neighborhood chief helps arrange BPJS cards for residents who don't have one yet.

target: Gigi geraham saya berlubang dan sakitnya menjalar sampai ke telinga.
english: My molar has a cavity and the pain spreads all the way to my ear.
grammar: Menjalar = (pain) spreads, creeps: sakitnya menjalar ke telinga = the pain spreads to the ear.

target: Dokter gigi menyarankan gigi itu ditambal sebelum lubangnya makin besar.
english: The dentist suggests that tooth be filled before the cavity gets bigger.

target: Anak saya takut sekali setiap kali diajak ke dokter gigi.
english: My child is really scared every time he is taken to the dentist.

target: Gigi bungsunya harus dicabut karena tumbuh miring dan menekan gigi lain.
english: His wisdom tooth has to be pulled because it grows crooked and presses on the other teeth.
grammar: Gigi bungsu = wisdom tooth, literally 'youngest-child tooth': dicabut = gets pulled.

target: Setelah gigi dicabut, jangan berkumur terlalu keras selama satu hari.
english: After the tooth is pulled, don't rinse your mouth too hard for one day.

target: Saya membersihkan karang gigi di klinik setiap enam bulan sekali.
english: I get my tartar cleaned at the clinic once every six months.

target: Adik memakai behel, jadi setiap bulan dia ke dokter gigi untuk kontrol.
english: My younger sibling wears braces, so every month she goes to the dentist for a checkup.

target: Gusi saya berdarah setiap kali menyikat gigi terlalu kencang.
english: My gums bleed every time I brush my teeth too hard.

target: Dokter gigi memuji anak saya karena rajin menggosok gigi sebelum tidur.
english: The dentist praises my child for diligently brushing his teeth before bed.

target: Biaya menambal satu gigi di klinik swasta lumayan mahal.
english: The cost of filling one tooth at a private clinic is pretty expensive.

target: Mata minus saya bertambah karena terlalu sering menatap layar ponsel.
english: My nearsightedness has gotten worse because I stare at my phone screen too often.
grammar: Mata minus = nearsighted, said with the number: minus saya bertambah = my prescription got worse.

target: Petugas optik memeriksa mata saya dengan mesin sebelum membuat kacamata.
english: The optician checks my eyes with a machine before making the glasses.

target: Kacamata baru ini membuat tulisan di papan terlihat jelas lagi.
english: These new glasses make the writing on the board look clear again.

target: Bingkai kacamata itu cocok dengan bentuk wajah kamu.
english: That glasses frame suits the shape of your face.

target: Ayah memakai kacamata baca setiap kali membuka koran pagi.
english: Dad puts on his reading glasses every time he opens the morning paper.
grammar: Kacamata = glasses, literally kaca (glass) + mata (eye): kacamata baca = reading glasses.

target: Lensa kontak lebih praktis untuk olahraga, tapi mata saya cepat kering.
english: Contact lenses are more practical for sports, but my eyes dry out quickly.

target: Kacamata saya patah karena diduduki adik kecil saya kemarin.
english: My glasses broke because my little sibling sat on them yesterday.

target: Di optik itu, kacamata bisa selesai dalam waktu satu jam saja.
english: At that optical shop, glasses can be finished in just one hour.

target: Ukuran minus mata kiri dan kanan saya ternyata berbeda jauh.
english: It turns out the prescriptions of my left and right eyes differ a lot.

target: Dokter mata menyarankan saya mengistirahatkan mata setiap dua puluh menit.
english: The eye doctor advises me to rest my eyes every twenty minutes.

target: Kalau badan pegal dan meriang, orang Indonesia bilang sedang masuk angin.
english: When the body is achy and feverish, Indonesians say you have 'masuk angin'.
grammar: Masuk angin ('wind got in') = the classic catch-all unwellness: chills, bloating, fatigue. Untranslatable.

target: Nenek minta dikerok punggungnya setiap kali merasa masuk angin.
english: Grandma asks to have her back coin-rubbed every time she feels she has masuk angin.
grammar: Kerokan: rubbing a coin down the back until it stripes red — the beloved home cure for masuk angin.

target: Bekas kerokan di punggung ayah merah semua, katanya makin merah makin manjur.
english: The kerokan marks on Dad's back are all red; he says the redder, the more effective.

target: Setiap pagi ibu minum jamu kunyit asam buatan tetangga.
english: Every morning Mom drinks turmeric-tamarind jamu made by the neighbor.
grammar: Jamu = traditional herbal tonic (turmeric, ginger...): minum jamu = drink jamu, for health not taste.

target: Penjual jamu gendong masih lewat depan rumah kami setiap pagi.
english: The traveling jamu seller still passes in front of our house every morning.
grammar: Jamu gendong = jamu sold by a walking vendor carrying bottles in a back sling (gendong = carry on the back).

target: Kata nenek, wedang jahe hangat ampuh untuk menghangatkan badan saat hujan.
english: According to Grandma, warm ginger drink works wonders for warming the body when it rains.

target: Ibu mengoleskan minyak kayu putih di perut adik yang kembung.
english: Mom rubs cajuput oil on my little sibling's bloated tummy.
grammar: Minyak kayu putih = cajuput oil, the warm-smelling cure-all rubbed on every Indonesian child's belly.

target: Tukang urut langganan keluarga kami datang ke rumah setiap bulan.
english: Our family's regular massage man comes to the house every month.

target: Setelah diurut, kaki saya yang keseleo terasa jauh lebih enak.
english: After being massaged, my sprained foot feels much better.

target: Banyak orang percaya bawang merah bisa menurunkan demam anak kecil.
english: Many people believe shallots can bring down a small child's fever.

target: Minum air kelapa muda katanya bagus untuk meredakan panas dalam.
english: Drinking young coconut water is said to be good for soothing 'panas dalam'.
grammar: Panas dalam ('inner heat') = folk ailment behind sore throats and canker sores; cooled with kelapa muda.

target: Sehabis melahirkan, kakak saya minum jamu supaya badannya cepat pulih.
english: After giving birth, my older sister drinks jamu so her body recovers quickly.

target: Campuran madu dan jeruk nipis jadi andalan ibu untuk meredakan batuk.
english: A mix of honey and lime is Mom's go-to for easing a cough.

target: Meskipun modern, dokter kami tidak melarang kerokan asal kulit tidak terluka.
english: Even though he is modern, our doctor doesn't forbid kerokan as long as the skin isn't injured.
grammar: Asal = as long as (condition): asal kulit tidak terluka = as long as the skin isn't hurt.

target: Balsam hangat ini selalu ada di dalam tas nenek ke mana-mana.
english: This warming balm is always in Grandma's bag wherever she goes.

target: Kantor saya menanggung asuransi kesehatan untuk karyawan dan keluarganya.
english: My office covers health insurance for the employees and their families.

target: Sebelum pulang, saya harus menyelesaikan tagihan rumah sakit di kasir.
english: Before going home, I have to settle the hospital bill at the cashier.

target: Jangan membuang kuitansi obat karena kita memerlukannya untuk klaim asuransi.
english: Don't throw away the medicine receipts because we need them for the insurance claim.
grammar: Kuitansi = official receipt (from Dutch 'kwitantie'): minta kuitansi = ask for a receipt.

target: Pihak asuransi menolak klaim kami karena satu dokumen kurang lengkap.
english: The insurance company rejected our claim because one document was incomplete.

target: Biaya rawat inap tiga hari itu hampir sepuluh juta rupiah.
english: The cost of that three-day hospital stay is almost ten million rupiah.

target: Untung asuransi kantor menanggung sebagian besar biaya operasi suami saya.
english: Luckily the office insurance covers most of the cost of my husband's operation.

target: Petugas administrasi menjelaskan rincian tagihan sebelum kami membayar.
english: The administration officer explains the breakdown of the bill before we pay.

target: Saya mencicil sisa tagihan rumah sakit selama enam bulan.
english: I am paying off the rest of the hospital bill in installments over six months.
grammar: Mencicil = pay in installments: mencicil tagihan = pay the bill bit by bit.

target: Simpan semua hasil laboratorium dan surat dokter untuk berkas klaim.
english: Keep all the lab results and doctor's letters for the claim file.

target: Asuransi perjalanan menanggung biaya berobat saya waktu sakit di Bali.
english: The travel insurance covered my treatment costs when I was sick in Bali.

target: Sore ini kami akan menjenguk paman yang dirawat di rumah sakit.
english: This afternoon we are going to visit our uncle who is hospitalized.
grammar: Menjenguk = visit someone sick or a new baby — a real social duty: menjenguk paman = visit uncle.

target: Teman-teman kantor patungan membeli parsel buah untuk menjenguk Bu Sari.
english: The office friends chip in to buy a fruit basket for visiting Mrs. Sari.
grammar: Patungan = chip in together: patungan membeli parsel = pool money to buy a gift basket.

target: Jangan lupa membawakan bubur ayam kesukaannya waktu menjenguk kakek nanti.
english: Don't forget to bring his favorite chicken porridge when visiting Grandpa later.

target: Semoga cepat sembuh, ya, kabari kami kalau perlu bantuan apa pun.
english: Get well soon, okay? Let us know if you need any help at all.
grammar: Semoga cepat sembuh = get well soon, literally 'hopefully quickly recover' — the standard sick wish.

target: Ibu menitip salam dan doa untuk tantemu yang sedang sakit.
english: Mom sends her greetings and prayers for your aunt who is sick.

target: Kami bergantian menjaga nenek di rumah sakit selama seminggu penuh.
english: We take turns watching over Grandma at the hospital for a full week.

target: Setelah operasi, pasien hanya boleh dijenguk oleh dua orang saja.
english: After the operation, the patient may only be visited by just two people.

target: Grup keluarga langsung ramai begitu kabar opname kakek tersebar.
english: The family group chat got lively as soon as news of Grandpa's hospitalization spread.
grammar: Opname (from Dutch) = being admitted to hospital: kabar opname kakek = news of Grandpa's hospital stay.

target: Tetangga datang membawa sup hangat waktu anak saya sakit demam berdarah.
english: The neighbors came bringing warm soup when my child was sick with dengue fever.
grammar: Demam berdarah (DBD) = dengue fever, literally 'bleeding fever' — the rainy-season worry.

target: Jenguklah dia selagi masih dirawat, dia pasti senang melihat kalian.
english: Do visit him while he is still hospitalized; he will surely be happy to see you all.

target: Sepulang dari rumah sakit, ayah dilarang bekerja berat selama sebulan.
english: After coming home from the hospital, Dad is forbidden from doing heavy work for a month.

target: Sejak kuliah di Bandung, adik saya tinggal di kamar kos dekat kampus.
english: Since studying in Bandung, my younger sibling has lived in a boarding room near campus.
grammar: Kos = a rented room in a shared house, classic student housing: kamar kos = boarding room.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka pindah dari kamar kos ke rumah kontrakan dua kamar.
english: After getting married, they moved from a boarding room to a two-bedroom rented house.
grammar: Kontrakan = a whole house you rent, usually yearly; kos = just a room: rumah kontrakan = rented house.

target: Harga kos di dekat kantor baru saya ternyata mahal sekali.
english: The price of a room near my new office turns out to be really expensive.

target: Ibu kos saya baik; kalau saya telat membayar beberapa hari, dia tidak marah.
english: My landlady is kind; if I am a few days late paying, she does not get angry.
grammar: Ibu kos = the landlady who runs a boarding house: bayar ke ibu kos = pay the landlady.

target: Biaya kos saya sudah termasuk listrik dan air, jadi pengeluaran gampang dihitung.
english: My room fee already includes electricity and water, so expenses are easy to calculate.

target: Kontrakan kami dibayar per tahun, jadi kami harus menyiapkan uang besar sekaligus.
english: Our rented house is paid for per year, so we have to prepare a large sum at once.

target: Sebelum menandatangani kontrak, cek dulu apakah harganya termasuk air dan listrik.
english: Before signing the contract, first check whether the price includes water and electricity.

target: Teman sekamar saya di kos sering lupa membayar iuran kebersihan.
english: My roommate at the boarding house often forgets to pay the cleaning dues.
grammar: Iuran = a regular fee everyone pays into: iuran kebersihan = the cleaning dues.

target: Anak kos biasanya memasak sendiri di akhir bulan supaya lebih hemat.
english: Boarding-house kids usually cook for themselves at the end of the month to be more thrifty.
grammar: Anak kos = someone living in a kos — shorthand for a tight budget: masakan anak kos = cheap cooking.

target: Pemilik kontrakan menaikkan harga sewa lima persen mulai tahun depan.
english: The owner of the rented house is raising the rent five percent starting next year.

target: Kami masih mencari kontrakan yang dekat sekolah anak-anak dan pasar.
english: We are still looking for a rental house near the children's school and the market.

target: Daripada mengontrak terus, lebih baik uangnya dipakai untuk mencicil rumah kecil.
english: Rather than renting forever, it is better to use the money to pay for a small house in installments.

target: Bulan depan kontrak kos saya habis, dan saya belum tahu mau memperpanjang atau pindah.
english: Next month my room lease runs out, and I do not know yet whether I want to extend or move.

target: Listrik di rumah kami pakai token, jadi harus diisi sebelum habis.
english: The electricity at our house uses tokens, so it has to be topped up before it runs out.
grammar: Token = prepaid electricity credit: beli token listrik = buy a code and punch it into the meter.

target: Tengah malam meteran berbunyi, ternyata token listriknya hampir habis.
english: In the middle of the night the meter beeped; it turned out the electricity credit was almost gone.

target: Saya selalu membeli token listrik seratus ribu setiap awal bulan.
english: I always buy a hundred thousand worth of electricity credit at the start of each month.

target: Kalau mati lampu, kami menyalakan lilin dan mengobrol di teras.
english: When the power goes out, we light candles and chat on the porch.
grammar: Mati lampu = a power cut of any kind, not just the lamps: sedang mati lampu = the power is out.

target: Angka di meteran listrik dicatat petugas setiap tanggal dua puluh.
english: The reading on the electricity meter is recorded by an officer on the twentieth of every month.

target: Mati lampu di daerah kami biasanya sebentar saja, paling lama satu jam.
english: Power cuts in our area are usually only brief, one hour at most.

target: Tagihan listrik kantor naik terus karena AC menyala sampai malam.
english: The office electricity bill keeps going up because the AC stays on until night.

target: Nomor meteran harus dimasukkan waktu membeli token lewat aplikasi.
english: The meter number has to be entered when buying electricity credit through the app.

target: Rumah kontrakan kami yang lama masih memakai meteran bulanan, bukan token.
english: Our old rented house still uses a monthly meter, not tokens.

target: Kulkas sempat mati waktu mati lampu kemarin, untung makanannya belum rusak.
english: The fridge went off for a while during yesterday's power cut; luckily the food had not spoiled.

target: Kata ayah, setrika dan pemanas air paling banyak memakan token listrik.
english: According to dad, the iron and the water heater eat up the most electricity credit.

target: Kami sengaja memilih AC baru yang katanya lebih irit listrik.
english: We deliberately chose a new AC that is said to use less electricity.

target: Waktu token habis tengah malam, minimarket dekat rumah jadi penyelamat.
english: When the electricity credit ran out in the middle of the night, the minimart near the house became the savior.

target: Air PAM di kompleks kami sering mati siang hari, jadi kami menampung air di ember.
english: The city water in our housing complex often goes off during the day, so we store water in buckets.
grammar: PAM = the city water utility: air PAM = tap water, used for washing rather than drinking.

target: Tagihan air PAM bulan ini lebih besar karena ada pipa bocor.
english: This month's city water bill is bigger because there was a leaking pipe.

target: Untuk minum kami pakai air galon; air PAM hanya untuk mandi dan mencuci.
english: For drinking we use gallon water; the tap water is only for bathing and washing.
grammar: Galon = the big 19-liter water bottle at home: air galon = drinking water from the dispenser.

target: Kalau air galon habis, tinggal telepon warung, nanti diantar sampai dapur.
english: When the gallon water runs out, just phone the corner shop, and it gets delivered right to the kitchen.

target: Satu galon isi ulang di depot dekat rumah harganya enam ribu.
english: One refill gallon at the depot near the house costs six thousand.
grammar: Isi ulang = refill: galon isi ulang = a refilled gallon from the water depot, cheaper than branded.

target: Abang galon langsung mengangkat galon kosong dan memasang yang baru.
english: The water delivery guy immediately lifted the empty gallon and installed the new one.

target: Pemakaian air kami bulan kemarin tinggi, mungkin karena banyak tamu menginap.
english: Our water usage last month was high, maybe because many guests stayed over.

target: Di kompleks kami, air PAM mengalir kencang hanya pagi dan malam hari.
english: In our complex, the city water flows strongly only in the morning and at night.

target: Ibu menyuruh kami menghemat air karena musim kemarau masih panjang.
english: Mom told us to save water because the dry season is still long.

target: Mereka membeli motor baru dengan DP tiga juta dan cicilan dua tahun.
english: They bought a new motorbike with a three-million down payment and two years of installments.
grammar: DP (say de-pe) = down payment: DP tiga juta = a three-million down payment. Also called uang muka.

target: Cicilan motor itu delapan ratus ribu per bulan, belum termasuk asuransi.
english: The installments for that motorbike are eight hundred thousand a month, not yet including insurance.
grammar: Cicilan = an installment; mencicil = pay bit by bit: cicilan dua tahun = two years of installments.

target: Kami menunda membeli kulkas baru karena masih ada dua cicilan berjalan.
english: We are putting off buying a new fridge because there are still two installment plans running.

target: Kalau uang mukanya lebih besar, cicilan bulanannya jadi lebih ringan.
english: If the down payment is bigger, the monthly installments become lighter.

target: Sisa cicilan rumah kami masih delapan tahun, pelan-pelan pasti lunas.
english: The remainder of our house installments is still eight years; slowly but surely it will be paid off.
grammar: Lunas = fully paid off: cicilannya sudah lunas = the installments are all paid.

target: Uang bonus akhir tahun langsung dia pakai untuk melunasi cicilan HP.
english: He immediately used his year-end bonus money to pay off his phone installments.

target: Jangan sampai menunggak cicilan, karena dendanya lumayan besar.
english: Do not let yourself fall behind on the installments, because the fine is quite big.
grammar: Menunggak = to fall behind on payments: menunggak cicilan = to miss installments.

target: Sebelum mengambil cicilan baru, hitung dulu semua pengeluaran bulananmu.
english: Before taking on a new installment plan, first count up all your monthly expenses.

target: Teman kantor saya menyesal mengambil cicilan mobil sebelum gajinya naik.
english: My office friend regrets taking on car installments before his salary went up.

target: Toko itu menawarkan cicilan tanpa bunga untuk pembelian di atas satu juta.
english: That store offers installments without interest for purchases above one million.
grammar: Bunga = flower AND interest: cicilan tanpa bunga = zero-interest installments.

target: DP rumah biasanya paling sedikit sepuluh persen dari harga rumahnya.
english: The down payment on a house is usually at least ten percent of the house price.

target: Arisan ibu-ibu di kompleks kami berkumpul setiap tanggal lima belas.
english: The neighborhood mothers' arisan in our complex gathers on the fifteenth of every month.
grammar: Arisan = a rotating savings club — all pay in, one takes the pot: ikut arisan = join one.

target: Nama ibu keluar waktu arisan dikocok, lumayan untuk membayar uang sekolah adik.
english: Mom's name came out when the arisan was drawn — helpful for paying my younger sibling's school fees.
grammar: Dikocok = shaken up and drawn by lot: nama ibu keluar = mom's name came out, she wins this round.

target: Banyak orang ikut arisan supaya bisa menabung sambil tetap bertemu teman-teman.
english: Many people join an arisan so they can save money while still meeting their friends.

target: Iuran arisan kantor kami dua ratus ribu, ditarik setiap tanggal gajian.
english: Our office arisan dues are two hundred thousand, collected every payday.

target: Ibu memakai uang arisan untuk membayar DP kulkas baru di toko elektronik.
english: Mom used her arisan money to pay the down payment on a new fridge at the electronics store.

target: Kalau dapat giliran pertama, uang arisan terasa seperti pinjaman tanpa bunga.
english: If you get the first turn, the arisan money feels like an interest-free loan.
grammar: Giliran = your turn in a rotation: dapat giliran pertama = get the first turn.

target: Setiap arisan selesai, ibu-ibu masih duduk lama membahas harga sembako.
english: Every time the arisan is over, the mothers still sit around a long time discussing staple food prices.
grammar: Sembako = the nine basic goods (rice, oil, sugar, and so on): harga sembako = staple prices.

target: Gaji pertama saya dulu di bawah UMR, tapi pengalamannya sangat berharga.
english: My first salary back then was below the regional minimum wage, but the experience was very valuable.
grammar: UMR = the regional minimum wage: di bawah UMR = below minimum wage.

target: UMR di Jakarta lebih tinggi daripada di kota kecil, tapi biaya hidupnya juga tinggi.
english: The minimum wage in Jakarta is higher than in small towns, but the cost of living is also high.

target: Setiap akhir tahun, pemerintah daerah mengumumkan UMR baru untuk tahun berikutnya.
english: Every end of year, the regional government announces the new minimum wage for the following year.

target: Gaji saya cukup untuk kebutuhan bulanan, sisanya saya tabung sedikit-sedikit.
english: My salary is enough for monthly needs; the rest I save bit by bit.

target: Gaji di kantor kami cair setiap tanggal dua puluh lima, langsung dipotong iuran.
english: The salary at our office comes through on the twenty-fifth, with dues deducted right away.
grammar: Cair, literally liquid = money comes through: gajinya sudah cair = the salary has landed.

target: Perusahaan kami menaikkan gaji sekali setahun, biasanya sesudah penilaian kerja.
english: Our company raises salaries once a year, usually after the performance review.

target: Selain gaji pokok, dia menerima uang makan dan uang transportasi.
english: Besides his base salary, he receives meal money and transport money.
grammar: Gaji pokok = base salary, before the extras: selain gaji pokok = on top of base salary.

target: Kata teman saya, gaji di pabrik baru itu sedikit di atas UMR.
english: According to my friend, the pay at that new factory is slightly above minimum wage.

target: Setelah tiga tahun bekerja di sana, akhirnya gajinya naik cukup besar.
english: After working there for three years, his salary finally went up quite a lot.

target: Gaji suaminya masuk ke rekening bersama untuk kebutuhan rumah tangga.
english: Her husband's salary goes into a joint account for household needs.

target: Kami membagi gaji ke tiga pos: kebutuhan, tabungan, dan hiburan.
english: We divide the salary into three categories: needs, savings, and fun.
grammar: Pos = a budget category: pos tabungan = the savings slot in the family budget.

target: Kakak saya hemat sekali; sepatu kerjanya dipakai sampai lima tahun.
english: My older sibling is really frugal; their work shoes get worn for up to five years.
grammar: Hemat = careful with money, boros = wasteful — everyday opposites: dia hemat sekali = very frugal.

target: Saya gampang boros kalau lapar; semua jajanan di pasar ingin saya beli.
english: I easily overspend when I am hungry; I want to buy every snack in the market.

target: Bulan ini kami harus lebih hemat karena ada biaya sekolah anak.
english: This month we have to be more frugal because there are the children's school costs.

target: Membawa bekal dari rumah jauh lebih hemat daripada membeli makan siang setiap hari.
english: Bringing a packed lunch from home is far more economical than buying lunch every day.

target: Dia kelihatan boros, padahal barang-barang mahalnya dibeli waktu diskon besar.
english: He looks like a big spender, even though his expensive things were bought during big sales.

target: Kata ibu, hemat itu bukan pelit, tapi tahu mana yang penting.
english: According to mom, being frugal is not being stingy, it is knowing what matters.
grammar: Pelit = stingy; hemat = sensibly careful: hemat itu bukan pelit = frugal is not stingy.

target: Langganan aplikasi yang jarang dipakai pelan-pelan membuat kita boros.
english: App subscriptions that are rarely used slowly make us wasteful.

target: Supaya hemat bensin, dia berangkat lebih pagi dan menghindari jam macet.
english: To save on fuel, he leaves earlier and avoids rush hour.

target: Kebiasaan kecil seperti mematikan lampu siang hari lama-lama terasa di tagihan.
english: Small habits like turning off the lights during the day eventually show in the bill.

target: Belanja bulanan kami biasanya di pasar dan supermarket dekat rumah.
english: Our monthly shopping is usually at the market and the supermarket near the house.
grammar: Belanja bulanan = the big monthly shop: uang belanja = the household shopping money.

target: Ibu selalu menulis daftar dulu supaya belanja bulanan tidak ada yang terlewat.
english: Mom always writes a list first so nothing in the monthly shop gets missed.

target: Beras, minyak goreng, dan sabun selalu ada di daftar belanja bulanan kami.
english: Rice, cooking oil, and soap are always on our monthly shopping list.

target: Belanja bulanan tanpa daftar ujung-ujungnya penuh barang yang tidak penting.
english: A monthly shop without a list ends up full of unimportant stuff.
grammar: Ujung-ujungnya = it always ends up: ujung-ujungnya boros = in the end you overspend.

target: Kami membandingkan harga di dua supermarket sebelum belanja bulanan yang besar.
english: We compare prices at two supermarkets before the big monthly shop.

target: Belanja sembako di pasar pagi lebih murah, tapi harus pintar menawar.
english: Shopping for staples at the morning market is cheaper, but you have to be good at bargaining.

target: Anak-anak senang ikut belanja bulanan karena boleh memilih satu camilan.
english: The kids love coming along on the monthly shop because they may pick one snack.

target: Sejak harga-harga naik, uang belanja bulanan kami sering kurang di minggu terakhir.
english: Since prices went up, our monthly shopping money often falls short in the last week.

target: Ayah kebagian tugas mengangkat semua kantong belanja dari mobil ke dapur.
english: Dad gets the job of carrying all the shopping bags from the car to the kitchen.

target: Harga cabai naik lagi, Bu? Rasanya kemarin masih setengah dari ini.
english: Chili prices are up again, ma'am? I feel like yesterday it was still half this much.
grammar: Chili prices are national small talk — they jump constantly: harga cabai naik lagi = up again.

target: Dulu lima puluh ribu cukup untuk seminggu, sekarang dua hari saja sudah habis.
english: Fifty thousand used to be enough for a week; now it is gone in just two days.

target: Menjelang hari raya, harga daging dan telur biasanya naik lebih dulu.
english: In the run-up to the big holiday, meat and egg prices usually go up first.

target: Ibu-ibu di warung sayur setiap pagi membahas harga minyak goreng.
english: The women at the vegetable stall discuss cooking-oil prices every morning.

target: Katanya harga gas tiga kilo mau naik lagi bulan depan.
english: They say the price of the three-kilo gas canister is going to go up again next month.

target: Harga kopi di kafe dekat kantor naik, jadi kami kembali ke kopi saset.
english: The coffee price at the cafe near the office went up, so we went back to sachet coffee.

target: Waktu semua harga naik begini, warung kecil bingung mau menaikkan harga atau tidak.
english: When all prices rise like this, small food stalls are not sure whether to raise prices or not.

target: Setiap harga BBM naik, ongkos angkot ikut naik pelan-pelan.
english: Every time fuel prices rise, minibus fares slowly rise along with them.
grammar: BBM = bahan bakar minyak, fuel: harga BBM naik = fuel prices went up — everything follows.

target: Untung gaji naik sedikit tahun ini, jadi kenaikan harga tidak terlalu terasa.
english: Luckily salaries went up a little this year, so the price increases are not felt too much.

target: Berapa ongkos angkot dari sini sampai terminal, Bang?
english: How much is the minibus fare from here to the terminal, sir?
grammar: Ongkos = fare, the cost of getting somewhere: ongkos angkot = the minibus fare.

target: Saya memilih toko yang lebih jauh karena ongkirnya gratis.
english: I chose the store that is farther away because its shipping is free.
grammar: Ongkir = ongkos kirim, the delivery fee; plain ongkos is a transport fare: gratis ongkir = free shipping.

target: Ongkir ke luar pulau bisa lebih mahal daripada harga barangnya sendiri.
english: Shipping to another island can be more expensive than the price of the item itself.

target: Kalau belanja di atas seratus ribu, aplikasi itu memberi gratis ongkir.
english: If you shop above one hundred thousand, that app gives free shipping.

target: Dulu ongkos bus ke kampung dua puluh ribu, sekarang hampir dua kali lipat.
english: The bus fare to the village used to be twenty thousand; now it is almost double.
grammar: Dua kali lipat = double: hampir dua kali lipat = almost twice as much.

target: Sopir travel menaikkan ongkos waktu musim liburan, katanya harga bensin juga naik.
english: The shuttle drivers raise fares during holiday season; they say fuel prices have gone up too.

target: Penjual online biasanya menulis bahwa harga belum termasuk ongkir.
english: Online sellers usually write that the price does not yet include shipping.

target: Saya menggabungkan dua pesanan dalam satu keranjang supaya ongkirnya lebih murah.
english: I combined two orders into one cart so the shipping would be cheaper.

target: Ongkos parkir langganan di gedung kantor dipotong langsung dari gaji bulanan.
english: The monthly parking fee at the office building is deducted straight from the monthly salary.

target: Kami patungan membeli kado pernikahan untuk teman satu tim di kantor.
english: We chipped in together to buy a wedding gift for a teammate at the office.
grammar: Patungan = to chip in together: kami patungan = we split the cost.

target: Untuk acara makan-makan akhir bulan, setiap orang patungan lima puluh ribu.
english: For the end-of-month get-together meal, each person chips in fifty thousand.

target: Anak-anak kompleks patungan membeli jaring baru untuk lapangan voli.
english: The kids in the complex chipped in to buy a new net for the volleyball court.

target: Daripada sewa mobil sendiri-sendiri, lebih murah kalau kita patungan satu mobil besar.
english: Rather than renting cars separately, it is cheaper if we all chip in for one big car.

target: Keluarga besar kami patungan membayar biaya rumah sakit kakek bulan lalu.
english: Our extended family chipped in to pay grandpa's hospital costs last month.

target: Kalau bensinnya patungan, perjalanan mudik naik mobil terasa lebih ringan.
english: If the fuel is split between everyone, the drive home for the holidays feels much lighter.

target: Uang patungan kemarin masih sisa tiga puluh ribu, mau dipakai untuk apa?
english: There is still thirty thousand left from yesterday's pooled money — what shall we use it for?

target: Target kami tahun ini menabung sepuluh juta untuk DP rumah kecil.
english: Our target this year is to save ten million for the down payment on a small house.

target: Sejak kecil, ayah mengajari saya menyisihkan uang jajan ke celengan.
english: Since I was little, dad taught me to set aside pocket money into a piggy bank.
grammar: Celengan = a piggy bank: menyisihkan uang ke celengan = set money aside in the piggy bank.

target: Dia menabung di rekening terpisah supaya uangnya tidak gampang terpakai.
english: She saves in a separate account so the money does not get spent by accident.

target: Kami menabung sedikit demi sedikit untuk biaya kuliah anak nanti.
english: We are saving little by little for the children's future college costs.
grammar: Sedikit demi sedikit = little by little: menabung sedikit demi sedikit = save bit by bit.

target: Uang receh di toples itu ternyata cukup untuk membeli kipas angin.
english: The loose change in that jar turned out to be enough to buy a fan.

target: Setiap gajian, dia langsung memindahkan uang tabungan ke rekening lain.
english: Every payday, he immediately moves his savings money to another account.

target: Tabungan liburan kami sempat terpakai waktu motor tiba-tiba masuk bengkel.
english: Our holiday savings did get used at one point when the motorbike suddenly went into the repair shop.

target: Menabung di awal bulan lebih mudah daripada menunggu sisa uang di akhir bulan.
english: Saving at the start of the month is easier than waiting for leftover money at the end of the month.

target: Nenek lebih percaya menyimpan uangnya di lemari daripada di bank.
english: Grandma trusts keeping her money in the wardrobe more than in the bank.

target: Saldo dompet digital saya tinggal lima ribu, nanti saya isi di minimarket.
english: My digital wallet balance is down to five thousand; I will top it up later at the minimart.
grammar: Isi saldo = top up a balance: saya isi di minimarket = I will top it up at the minimart.

target: Sekarang mengisi saldo bisa lewat aplikasi bank, tidak perlu antre di konter.
english: Nowadays topping up the balance can be done through the bank app; no need to queue at a counter.

target: Tukang parkir di pasar sekarang juga menerima pembayaran lewat dompet digital.
english: The parking attendants at the market now also accept payment through digital wallets.
grammar: Tukang = the ... guy, by trade: tukang parkir = parking attendant, tukang galon = the water guy.

target: Saya mengisi saldo dua ratus ribu setiap minggu khusus untuk ongkos ojek online.
english: I top up two hundred thousand every week just for online motorbike-taxi fares.

target: Membayar pakai dompet digital sering dapat potongan, tapi hati-hati jadi boros.
english: Paying with a digital wallet often gets you a discount, but be careful you do not turn wasteful.

target: Ibu akhirnya mau belajar memakai dompet digital supaya gampang membayar uang sekolah adik.
english: Mom is finally willing to learn to use a digital wallet so paying my younger sibling's school fees is easy.

target: Waktu sinyal hilang, dompet digital tidak bisa dibuka; untung masih ada uang tunai.
english: When the signal disappeared, the digital wallet could not be opened; luckily there was still cash.

target: Anak muda sekarang jarang membawa dompet karena semua pembayaran lewat HP.
english: Young people these days rarely carry a wallet because all payments go through their phones.

target: Mengisi saldo di minimarket biasanya kena biaya tambahan seribu rupiah.
english: Topping up a balance at the minimart usually incurs an extra fee of one thousand rupiah.
grammar: Kena biaya = get charged a fee: kena biaya seribu = charged one thousand.

target: Tukang itu membawa palu, obeng, dan gergaji di dalam kotak peralatannya.
english: That handyman carries a hammer, a screwdriver, and a saw in his toolbox.
grammar: Tukang + a trade names the worker: tukang kayu = carpenter, tukang ledeng = plumber.

target: Pinjam obeng kecil itu sebentar, saya mau mengencangkan sekrup di pintu lemari.
english: Lend me that small screwdriver for a moment; I want to tighten a screw on the cupboard door.

target: Paku di dinding ini sudah berkarat, jadi harus diganti dengan yang baru.
english: The nail in this wall has rusted, so it has to be replaced with a new one.
grammar: ber- + noun = 'to have/produce it': karat rust, berkarat rusty; debu dust, berdebu dusty.

target: Kalau bornya rusak, kita tidak bisa memasang rak kayu ini hari ini.
english: If the drill is broken, we can't put up this wooden shelf today.

target: Dia menaiki tangga untuk memperbaiki atap yang bocor sejak minggu lalu.
english: He climbs the ladder to fix the roof that has been leaking since last week.

target: Tolong ambilkan ember dan selang, saya mau mencuci mobil di halaman.
english: Please fetch the bucket and the hose; I want to wash the car in the yard.

target: Gergaji ini terlalu tumpul untuk memotong papan yang tebal itu.
english: This saw is too dull to cut that thick plank.

target: Sebelum mengecat tembok, tutup lantai dengan plastik supaya tidak kotor.
english: Before painting the wall, cover the floor with plastic so it doesn't get dirty.
grammar: One-syllable roots take menge-: cat, mengecat = to paint; cas, mengecas = to charge.

target: Kunci inggris ada di laci paling bawah, di sebelah kotak paku.
english: The wrench is in the bottom drawer, next to the box of nails.
grammar: Kunci inggris — literally 'English key' — is the everyday Indonesian word for a wrench.

target: Mesin jahit nenek masih berfungsi walaupun umurnya lebih dari empat puluh tahun.
english: Grandma's sewing machine still works even though it is more than forty years old.

target: Meja ini terbuat dari kayu jati, makanya berat sekali.
english: This table is made of teak wood; that's why it is so heavy.
grammar: terbuat dari + material = 'made of': terbuat dari kayu jati = made of teak wood.

target: Botol kaca lebih ramah lingkungan daripada botol plastik sekali pakai.
english: Glass bottles are more environmentally friendly than single-use plastic bottles.
grammar: sekali pakai = single-use, literally 'once use': botol plastik sekali pakai.

target: Pagar besi itu dicat ulang setiap dua tahun supaya tidak berkarat.
english: That iron fence is repainted every two years so it doesn't rust.

target: Kain dari pulau itu ditenun dengan tangan selama berminggu-minggu.
english: The cloth from that island is woven by hand over many weeks.

target: Sepatu kulit cepat rusak kalau sering kena hujan dan tidak pernah dirawat.
english: Leather shoes get ruined quickly if they often get rained on and are never cared for.

target: Rumah tradisional di desa itu dibangun dari bambu dan batu kali.
english: The traditional houses in that village are built from bamboo and river stone.

target: Sandal karet ini murah, ringan, dan cocok untuk musim hujan.
english: These rubber sandals are cheap, light, and right for the rainy season.

target: Tukang bangunan sedang mencampur semen dengan pasir di depan rumah kosong itu.
english: The construction workers are mixing cement with sand in front of that empty house.

target: Banjir tahun lalu lebih parah karena sungai penuh sampah plastik.
english: Last year's flood was worse because the river was full of plastic trash.

target: Jalan menuju bandara ditutup karena tergenang air setinggi lutut.
english: The road to the airport is closed because it is flooded with knee-deep water.
grammar: se- + adjective = 'as X as': setinggi lutut = knee-high, sebesar rumah = as big as a house.

target: Semakin lama musim kemarau, semakin sulit petani mendapatkan air untuk sawahnya.
english: The longer the dry season, the harder it is for farmers to get water for their rice fields.
grammar: semakin X, semakin Y = 'the more X, the more Y': semakin lama, semakin sulit.

target: Badai semalam menumbangkan pohon besar di depan kantor kami.
english: Last night's storm toppled the big tree in front of our office.

target: Kalau ada petir, jangan berteduh di bawah pohon yang tinggi.
english: If there's lightning, don't take shelter under a tall tree.
grammar: berteduh = to take shelter, from teduh (shade): berteduh di warung = shelter at a stall.

target: Angin kencang membuat penerbangan ke Lombok ditunda sampai besok pagi.
english: Strong winds made the flight to Lombok get postponed until tomorrow morning.

target: Kabut tebal turun setiap pagi di daerah pegunungan ini, jadi nyalakan lampu mobil.
english: Thick fog comes down every morning in this mountain area, so turn on the car's lights.

target: Gempa kecil sering terjadi di sini, jadi warga sudah terbiasa.
english: Small earthquakes often happen here, so the residents are already used to them.

target: Setelah hujan deras tiga hari, tanah di bukit itu longsor dan menutup jalan.
english: After three days of heavy rain, the ground on that hill slid and blocked the road.

target: Gelombang panas seperti ini berbahaya untuk orang tua dan anak kecil.
english: A heat wave like this is dangerous for the elderly and small children.

target: Atap rumah tetangga terbang ketika angin puting beliung lewat kemarin sore.
english: The neighbor's roof flew off when a whirlwind passed through yesterday afternoon.

target: Karena kekeringan, pemerintah mengirim truk air bersih ke desa-desa yang jauh.
english: Because of the drought, the government is sending clean-water trucks to the distant villages.
grammar: ke-...-an on adjectives names the state: kering dry, kekeringan drought; aman safe, keamanan safety.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini datang lebih awal daripada perkiraan.
english: This year's rainy season arrived earlier than predicted.

target: Nelayan tidak berani melaut karena ombak sangat tinggi minggu ini.
english: The fishermen don't dare go to sea because the waves are very high this week.

target: Kalau langit tiba-tiba gelap dan angin berhenti, biasanya hujan besar akan segera turun.
english: If the sky suddenly darkens and the wind stops, usually heavy rain will soon fall.

target: Keputusan sebesar ini tidak boleh diambil ketika kamu sedang marah.
english: A decision this big must not be made while you are angry.
grammar: ke-...-an also makes nouns from verbs: putus decide, keputusan decision; sempat, kesempatan chance.

target: Kesempatan seperti ini jarang datang dua kali, jadi pikirkan baik-baik.
english: An opportunity like this rarely comes twice, so think it over carefully.

target: Pengalaman bekerja di luar negeri mengubah cara saya melihat dunia.
english: The experience of working abroad changed the way I see the world.

target: Kepercayaan pelanggan lebih sulit dibangun daripada gedung bertingkat.
english: Customer trust is harder to build than a high-rise building.

target: Tanggung jawab terbesar seorang pemimpin adalah mendengarkan orang yang dipimpinnya.
english: A leader's biggest responsibility is listening to the people they lead.

target: Kegagalan pertama justru memberi saya keberanian untuk mencoba lagi.
english: The first failure actually gave me the courage to try again.
grammar: justru flips an expectation: 'actually, on the contrary'. Gagal justru membuat saya berani.

target: Kesabaran ibu saya hampir tidak ada batasnya kalau soal anak-anaknya.
english: My mother's patience has almost no limit when it comes to her children.

target: Perbedaan pendapat itu biasa; yang penting kita saling menghormati.
english: Differences of opinion are normal; what matters is that we respect each other.
grammar: saling + verb = 'each other': saling menghormati = respect each other. No object needed.

target: Persahabatan kami mulai dari kos yang sama lima belas tahun lalu.
english: Our friendship started from the same boarding house fifteen years ago.

target: Kebiasaan kecil seperti menabung sepuluh ribu sehari lama-lama terasa hasilnya.
english: A small habit like saving ten thousand a day — over time you feel the results.
grammar: lama-lama = 'eventually, over time': lama-lama terasa hasilnya = in time you feel the results.

target: Harapan orang tuanya sederhana: anak-anaknya hidup sehat dan jujur.
english: His parents' hope is simple: that their children live healthy and honest lives.

target: Kenyataan di lapangan sering berbeda dengan rencana yang dibuat di kantor.
english: The reality on the ground often differs from the plans made at the office.
